The results of this paper can be read as a minimal calculus for building hierarchical structure while keeping directionality honest.
The core observation is that three notions often conflated in informal discussions are logically distinct and have distinct mathematical \emph{certificates}:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Stability / objects (completion).} A theory level is specified by an idempotent endomap (exact or approximate); its fixed points are the “objects” at that theory level.
  In order theory this is a closure operator; in dynamics it is the induced endomap $E_{\tau,f}$.
  The certificate is (approximate) idempotence, quantified by the TV defect $\delta_{\tau,f}$.
  \item \textbf{Novelty / open-endedness (theory extension).} Iterating a fixed completion rule saturates by idempotence.
  Strict ladder climbing therefore requires changing the theory/completion rule.
  The certificate is \emph{non-definability}: a new predicate is not measurable with respect to the old partition-based theory.
  Our finite forcing lemma makes this generic: when there is hidden volume ($N-K>0$), uniformly random predicate extensions are overwhelmingly non-definable.
  \item \textbf{Directionality / irreversibility (audit).} Arrow-of-time is defined on path space as $\Sigma_T(\rho)=D_{\mathrm{KL}}(\mathbb P_{\rho,T}\|\mathcal{R}_{*}\mathbb P_{\rho,T})$.
  The certificate is either positive path-space KL or, under the accounted regime, a non-exact log-ratio 1-form (nonzero cycle affinities).
  Data processing ensures coarse-graining cannot create this certificate, and the protocol-trap theorem ensures it is not an artifact of hiding an internal clock.
\end{itemize}

\label{thm:T-IC-01}
\textbf{T-IC-01.}\par
Assume \textbf{A\_FIN}+\textbf{A\_LENS}.
There exist finite Markov kernels $P$ and times $\tau$ together with two lenses
\[
f_{\mathrm{fine}}:Z\to X_{\mathrm{fine}},\qquad f_{\mathrm{coarse}}:Z\to X_{\mathrm{coarse}},
\]
such that $f_{\mathrm{coarse}}$ is a coarsening of $f_{\mathrm{fine}}$ (the fine partition refines the coarse),
and for the canonical lift $U_f$ defining $E_{\tau,f}$ (Definition~\ref{def:D-IC-01}),
the number of $\varepsilon$-stable prototypes can either increase or decrease under refinement
for a fixed stability threshold $\varepsilon>0$.

More precisely, both behaviors occur:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{Refinement reveals objects}) in one example, refinement increases the number of
$\varepsilon$-stable prototypes.
\item (\emph{Refinement destroys objects}) in another example, the stable count decreases.
\end{enumerate}

\label{thm:protocol_trap}
Assume \textbf{A\_FIN}+\textbf{A\_AUT}.
Suppose:
(i) the phase chain $\mathsf S$ is reversible with stationary distribution $s$;
(ii) each $K_\phi$ is reversible with respect to a \emph{common} stationary distribution $\pi$ on $X$.
Then the product measure $\mu:=\pi\times s$ is stationary for the lifted chain on $Z=X\times\Phi$ and the lifted chain is reversible (hence $\Sigma_T(\mu)=0$ for all $T$).
Consequently, by Theorem~\ref{thm:dpi_path} applied to the projection $X\times\Phi\to X$, the observed process on $X$ has zero path reversal asymmetry at every finite horizon.

In particular, any \emph{apparent} arrow-of-time obtained by analysing a stroboscopic composition of kernels on $X$ must be traced to either:
(a) an external schedule (violating \textbf{A\_AUT}), or
(b) a driven/bias phase dynamics (nonzero affinity, cf.\ Section~\ref{sec:acc}).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\begin{lemma}
Assume \textbf{A\_FIN}+\textbf{A\_LENS} and let $f:Z\to X$ have blocks $\Pi_f=\{B_x\}_{x\in X}$.
For each block $B_x$,
\[
\mathbb P(h \text{ is constant on } B_x)=2^{1-|B_x|},
\]
and by a union bound,
\[
\mathbb P(\exists x\in X\text{ such that }h\text{ is constant on }B_x)\ \le\ \sum_{x\in X} 2^{1-|B_x|}.
\]
In particular, if every block has size at least $m\ge 2$, then
\[
\mathbb P(h \text{ splits every block}) \ \ge\ 1 - K\,2^{1-m}.
\]
\end{lemma}

\begin{proof}
On a block of size $|B_x|$, the only constant labelings are ``all zeros'' and ``all ones'', each with probability $2^{-|B_x|}$, hence $2^{1-|B_x|}$ total.
The union bound gives the stated inequality, and the final display uses $|B_x|\ge m$ for all $x$.
\end{proof}

Here P5, P6, P4, and P2 are by construction from the lens/refinement data, while P1 and P3 isolate the only nontrivial compatibility requirements as named hypothesis slots (HL-META-1/2/3). P5 (Packaging). Each equivalence _j yields a quotient/packaging map Pi_j: P→ P/ _j and induces an idempotent saturation on predicates/events via cl_j(A):=Pi_j^ -1 (Pi_j(A)) (cf.\ Sections and ). P6 (Accounting). The refinement order on quotients induces a preorder and monotone ``audit'' quantities (e.g.\ j↦ |X_j| ); this is an information/feasibility order only (not, by itself, a thermodynamic arrow-of-time). P4 (Staging). The refinement chain generates a depth index j , and bounded interfaces ensure |X_j| (j+1) . Nontrivial staging corresponds to strict refinement at some scale (HL-META-2: _ j+1 _j for some j ). P2 (Constraints). Assume D-META-PROC-01, D-META-LENS-01, D-META-REF-01, and D-META-BND-01.
Then the six primitives P1--P6 appear canonically as closure mechanics.
Here \textbf{P5}, \textbf{P6}, \textbf{P4}, and \textbf{P2} are by construction from the lens/refinement data, while \textbf{P1} and \textbf{P3} isolate the only nontrivial compatibility requirements as named hypothesis slots (HL-META-1/2/3).
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{P5 (Packaging).} Each equivalence $\sim_j$ yields a quotient/packaging map
  $\Pi_j:\mathcal P\to \mathcal P/\!\sim_j$ and induces an idempotent saturation on predicates/events via
  $\mathrm{cl}_j(A):=\Pi_j^{-1}(\Pi_j(A))$ (cf.\ Sections~\ref{sec:closure} and \ref{sec:idempotent-endo}).
  \item \textbf{P6 (Accounting).} The refinement order on quotients induces a preorder and monotone ``audit'' quantities (e.g.\ $j\mapsto |X_j|$); this is an information/feasibility order only (not, by itself, a thermodynamic arrow-of-time).
  \item \textbf{P4 (Staging).} The refinement chain generates a depth index $j$, and bounded interfaces ensure $|X_j|\lesssim (j+1)$. Nontrivial staging corresponds to strict refinement at some scale (HL-META-2: $\sim_{j+1}\subsetneq \sim_j$ for some $j$).
  \item \textbf{P2 (Constraints).} Feasible macrostates are those representable as images under $\Pi_j$,
  yielding a constraint set carved by interface compatibility.
  \item \textbf{P1 (Operator rewrite).} Fix a micro-update $F:\mathcal P\to\mathcal P$. The induced macro-update
  $F^\sharp([p]) := [F(p)]$ on $\mathcal P/\!\sim_j$ is well-defined iff $p\sim_j q \Rightarrow F(p)\sim_j F(q)$ (HL-META-1).
  When (HL-META-1) fails, one must either (i) refine the lens so stability holds, (ii) modify/extend $F$ to respect $\sim_j$, or (iii) accept that no closed macro dynamics exists at depth $j$.
  \item \textbf{P3 (Holonomy).} Assuming there exist two admissible closure/evolution routes with the same input/output type (HL-META-3)
  (e.g.\ $\Pi_j\circ F$ versus $F^\sharp\circ \Pi_j$ when $F^\sharp$ is well-defined), their discrepancy defines a holonomy-like diagnostic.
  In normed operator instantiations we measure this by $\mathrm{RM}(j)$ (Appendix~\ref{app:tk-defects}, Eq.~\eqref{eq:tk-rm}); this is a discrepancy diagnostic, not itself a directionality certificate (see Section~\ref{sec:aot}).
 \end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Fix a threshold $\theta>0$ and a scale index $j\in\mathbb N$.
Let $E_j:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ be an activity observable at level $j$, and define the frontier
\[
j_*(t):=\max\{j:\ E_j(t)\ge \theta\}.
\]
Define crossing times and step durations by
\[
t_j := \inf\{t:\ j_*(t)\ge j\},\qquad \Delta t_j := t_{j+1}-t_j.
\]
A \emph{Zeno cascade} is the event that $(t_j)$ remains bounded as $j\to\infty$, equivalently
$\sum_{j\ge j_0}\Delta t_j<\infty$.

\label{thm:ect-summary}
Fix a depth-indexed family of packaged bridges $(\mathsf Z_j)_j$ with port spaces $U_j$ and a horizon $T>0$.
Assume the following slot conditions hold for all sufficiently large $j$:

\begin{enumerate}
  \item[\textbf{HL-ECT-1}] (\emph{Mode compression}) $\mathsf Z_j$ admits an atomic/sector decomposition with mode count
  $m_j \le C_0 (j+1)$.
  A sufficient route in this appendix is: sectorization + P5-min + quantized index, which yields $m_j \lesssim (j+1)$
  (see Corollary~\ref{cor:ect-hl1}).
  \item[\textbf{HL-ECT-3}] (\emph{Uniform per-atom ICAP}) each atom $\mathsf Z_{j,r}$ in the decomposition satisfies ICAP with a
  uniform constant $\Lambda_0$ (independent of $j,r$). A sufficient condition is bounded kernel mass
  (Lemma~\ref{lem:ect-fmem}). In particular, dissipative atoms with semigroup decay (Definition~\ref{def:ect-atom-ss})
  and balanced coupling (Definition~\ref{def:ect-bal}) satisfy uniform ICAP via Lemma~\ref{lem:ect-bal-kmass}
  and Corollary~\ref{cor:ect-bal-icap}.
  \item[\textbf{HL-ECT-2}] (\emph{Feasibility removes lossless directions, if strictness is needed}) feasibility gating excludes
  lossless directions so that a coercive norm is induced on feasible inputs (see Remark~\ref{rem:hl-p2-core},
  Lemma~\ref{lem:ect-coer-feas}, and the depth-scaling lemma Lemma~\ref{lem:ect-shrink}).
\end{enumerate}

Then the ICAP capacity constant obeys a linear bound
\[
\mathrm{Cap}(\mathsf Z_j)\ \le\ \Lambda_0\,C_0\,(j+1),
\]
and consequently
\[
\sum_{j\ge 0}\frac{1}{\mathrm{Cap}(\mathsf Z_j)}=\infty.
\]
In particular, this verifies the \emph{DIV} ingredient used in the No-Zeno criterion (Theorem~\ref{thm:no-zeno} in Appendix~D).
WORK quantization and a feasibility/energy-density cap are supplied there.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:ect-fmem}
Let $U$ be a finite-dimensional port space and $\mathcal U:=L^2([0,T];U)$.
Consider a causal convolution bridge $\mathsf Z:\mathcal U\to\mathcal U$ of the form
\[
(\mathsf Zu)(t)\ :=\ \int_0^t K(t-\tau)\,u(\tau)\,d\tau,
\]
where $K:[0,\infty)\to \mathrm{End}(U)$ is measurable and $k(\tau):=\|K(\tau)\|_{\mathrm{op}}$ satisfies
$M:=\int_0^\infty k(\tau)\,d\tau<\infty$.
For $0\le s\le t\le T$ define the truncated input $u^{[s,t]}:=u\,\mathbf 1_{[s,t]}$ and output $y^{[s,t]}:=\mathsf Z(u^{[s,t]})$.
Then the positive supplied work computed from $y^{[s,t]}$ satisfies
\[
W^+[s,t]\ \le\ M\int_s^t \|u(\tau)\|_U^2\,d\tau.
\]

\label{lem:ect-mech}
Let $\mathsf Z=\sum_{r=1}^m \mathsf Z_r$ be an atomic decomposition in the sense of Definition~\ref{def:ect-atom}.
Assume each atom satisfies ICAP with a uniform constant $\Lambda_0$, i.e.\ for all $r$ and all $0\le s\le t\le T$,
\[
W_r^+[s,t]\le \Lambda_0\int_s^t\|u(\tau)\|_U^2\,d\tau,
\]
where $u^{[s,t]}:=u\,\mathbf 1_{[s,t]}$ and $W_r^+[s,t]$ is computed from $y_r=\mathsf Z_r u^{[s,t]}$.
Then $\mathsf Z$ satisfies ICAP with constant $m\Lambda_0$, hence
\[
\mathrm{Cap}(\mathsf Z)\ \le\ m\Lambda_0.
\]
In particular, in a depth-indexed family $(\mathsf Z_j)_j$ with mode counts $m_j\le C_0(j+1)$ we obtain
\[
\mathrm{Cap}(\mathsf Z_j)\ \le\ \Lambda_0\,C_0\,(j+1),
\qquad\text{and consequently}\qquad
\sum_{j\ge 0}\frac{1}{\mathrm{Cap}(\mathsf Z_j)}=\infty.
\]

source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:ect-coer-feas}
Let $\mathsf Z_j:\mathcal U_j\to\mathcal U_j$ be a causal bridge.
Assume that for every feasible input $u\in\mathcal U_j^{\mathrm{feas}}$ and every $0\le s\le t\le T$, with output $y=\mathsf Z_j u$,
\[
\int_s^t \langle u(\tau),y(\tau)\rangle\,d\tau\ \ge\ \int_s^t \langle u(\tau),G_j u(\tau)\rangle\,d\tau.
\]
Then, on $\mathcal U_j^{\mathrm{feas}}$,
\[
\int_s^t \langle u(\tau),(\mathsf Z_j u)(\tau)\rangle\,d\tau\ \ge\ |u|_{L^2_X(s,t)}^2.
\]

\label{lem:ect-shrink}
Assume the setup of Definition~\ref{def:ect-gate} and Lemma~\ref{lem:ect-coer-feas}.
Suppose there exists a constant $a_j>0$ such that for every feasible input $u\in\mathcal U_j^{\mathrm{feas}}$ and every interval $0\le s\le t\le T$,
\[
|u|_{L^2_X(s,t)}^2 \;\ge\; a_j^2\int_s^t \|u(\tau)\|_{U_j}^2\,d\tau.
\]
Then for every feasible $u$ and every $0\le s\le t\le T$ we have the depth-scaled coercive lower bound
\[
\int_s^t \langle u(\tau),(\mathsf Z_j u)(\tau)\rangle\,d\tau
\;\ge\;
a_j^2\int_s^t \|u(\tau)\|_{U_j}^2\,d\tau.
\]
Equivalently, relative to the baseline $L^2([0,T];U_j)$ norm the effective coercivity coefficient is $c_j=a_j^2$.

conclusion: A finite audited typed closure description D is a finitely presented collection of typed raw records and annotations subject to finiteness, closure, and honest-bookkeeping conditions. The role vocabulary P1–P6 enters D not as a constraint on admissibility but as a family of derived projections pi_i(D) , each available when threshold, witness, level, and audit data are attached to raw features. The terminal theorem (Theorem ) states that for every D ∈ FATCD there exists a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion record Dec D carrying exactly the six typed closure-role channels P1, , P6, each in exactly one of five statuses, with all residual features covered by an explicit classification and, under an explicit recognition hypothesis, no seventh irreducible role required in the covered scope. The claim is about role channels, not active projections, and the decomposition is existential, not unique.

\begin{theorem}[Six-role lower bounds]\label{thm:six-role-lower-bounds}
For each role index \(i \in \{1,\ldots,6\}\), there exists a description
\(D_i \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) and a derived active projection
\(\pi_i(D_i)\) witnessing the role channel \(P_i\) in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:role-projection}. In particular, each of
\ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P2}}, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P3}}, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P4}}, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P5}}, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}} is instantiated
by at least one admissible description in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}. This is an occurrence
theorem, not an exhaustion theorem.\footnote{Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (\texttt{SixBirds.six\_role\_lower\_bounds}); see Appendix~\ref{app:mechanization}.}
\end{theorem}

A witness for role \(P_i\) consists of the data specified below,
following the role-projection discipline of
\S\ref{subsec:derived-role-projections} and the threshold-attachment
discipline of \S\ref{subsec:threshold-attachment}.

\(D_i \in \FATCD{}\) and a derived active projection
\(\pi_i(D_i)\) witnessing the role channel \(P_i\) in the sense of
Definition~\ref{def:role-projection}. In particular, each of
\Pone{}, \Ptwo{}, \Pthree{}, \Pfour{}, \Pfive{}, \Psix{} is instantiated
by at least one admissible description in \FATCD{}. This is an occurrence
theorem, not an exhaustion theorem.\footnote{Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (\texttt{SixBirds.six\_role\_lower\_bounds}); see Appendix~\ref{app:mechanization}.}
\end{theorem}

A witness for role \(P_i\) consists of the data specified below,
following the role-projection discipline of
\S\ref{subsec:derived-role-projections} and the threshold-attachment
discipline of \S\ref{subsec:threshold-attachment}.

conclusion: [topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt] P1: admissible only when the candidate cluster carries a selected update, a quotient or relation record, and a witness of descent compatibility, descent obstruction, or update-vs-quotient mismatch. Generic semantics, generic predicate meaning, generic selection criteria, and generic agency are not admissible as P1 projections in the absence of such a witness. P2: admissible only when the candidate carries a macro specification, a realization relation, specification-satisfaction data, and evidence of representability or non-representability. Macro-level predicates or objectives count only insofar as they are treated as content to be represented. Mere quotient equality, arbitrary relations without representability structure, and empirical observations without level and threshold data are not admissible as P2 projections. P3: admissible only when the candidate carries enriched route grammar, generated same-source, same-target route terms, and route-comparison data with a non-reducibility or coherence-mismatch certificate. Generic transitions, generic causal arrows, generic path records, and route undefinedness arising from P1 obstruction are not admissible as P3 projections unless the route/coherence threshold is explicitly present and the route comparison is specifically of the P3 type. P4: admissible only when the candidate carries a stage, order, transition, refinement, staged-dynamics, or regime-ordering record with laws beyond bare labels. Bare labels, arbitrary relations without order, transition, or refinement law, quotient packaging, and audit bookkeeping are not admissible as P4 projections. P5: admissible only when the candidate carries a quotient relation, a packaging map, the identification of distinct micro-elements, a same-package or quotient-object record, and quotient-validity evidence. Generic structural paths, derivations, topologies or geometries merely because they have paths, and causal chains are not admissible as P5 projections unless quotient or packaging data is present. P6: admissible only when the candidate carries an audit record with event reference, provenance or dependency trace, replay or check structure, and bookkeeping or checkability structure. Passive logs alone, arbitrary metadata, and certificate-only content without audit/provenance/replay/check structure are not admissible as P6 projections. Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (SixBirds.alignment_rules); see Appendix .

\label{prop:alignment-rules}
Under honest bookkeeping and the witness discipline of
Definition~\ref{def:common-witness-data}, each role projection is
constrained as follows.
\begin{itemize}[topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}: admissible only when the candidate cluster carries a
    selected update, a quotient or relation record, and a witness of
    descent compatibility, descent obstruction, or update-vs-quotient
    mismatch. Generic semantics, generic predicate meaning, generic
    selection criteria, and generic agency are not admissible as
    \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}} projections in the absence of such a witness.
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P2}}: admissible only when the candidate carries a macro
    specification, a realization relation, specification-satisfaction
    data, and evidence of representability or non-representability.
    Macro-level predicates or objectives count only insofar as they are
    treated as content to be represented. Mere quotient equality,
    arbitrary relations without representability structure, and
    empirical observations without level and threshold data are not
    admissible as \ensuremath{\mathrm{P2}} projections.
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P3}}: admissible only when the candidate carries enriched
    route grammar, generated same-source, same-target route terms, and
    route-comparison data with a non-reducibility or coherence-mismatch
    certificate. Generic transitions, generic causal arrows, generic
    path records, and route undefinedness arising from \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}
    obstruction are not admissible as \ensuremath{\mathrm{P3}} projections unless the
    route/coherence threshold is explicitly present and the route
    comparison is specifically of the \ensuremath{\mathrm{P3}} type.
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P4}}: admissible only when the candidate carries a stage,
    order, transition, refinement, staged-dynamics, or regime-ordering
    record with laws beyond bare labels. Bare labels, arbitrary
    relations without order, transition, or refinement law, quotient
    packaging, and audit bookkeeping are not admissible as \ensuremath{\mathrm{P4}}
    projections.
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P5}}: admissible only when the candidate carries a quotient
    relation, a packaging map, the identification of distinct
    micro-elements, a same-package or quotient-object record, and
    quotient-validity evidence. Generic structural paths, derivations,
    topologies or geometries merely because they have paths, and causal
    chains are not admissible as \ensuremath{\mathrm{P5}} projections unless quotient
    or packaging data is present.
  \item \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}: admissible only when the candidate carries an audit
    record with event reference, provenance or dependency trace, replay
    or check structure, and bookkeeping or checkability structure.
    Passive logs alone, arbitrary metadata, and certificate-only
    content without audit/provenance/replay/check structure are not
    admissible as \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}} projections.
\end{itemize}\footnote{Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (\texttt{SixBirds.alignment\_rules}); see Appendix~\ref{app:mechanization}.}

\(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) whose content takes one of the recognized forms below

\begin{definition}[Recognition hypothesis]\label{def:recognition-hypothesis}
A description \(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) satisfies the \emph{recognition hypothesis}
when every residual feature \(r \in \Residual{D}\) is \emph{recognized}: the
closure content of \(r\) either supplies the witness type of one of the six
role meanings of Definition~\ref{def:primitive-roles} --- so that \(r\), or a
finite composite of its constituents, projects to \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}
under Proposition~\ref{prop:alignment-rules} --- or instantiates one of the six
annotation kinds of Definition~\ref{def:annotations}, or is substrate already
accounted for by the audit discipline of \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}. Equivalently, \(D\) carries
no finite audited residual feature whose closure content is irreducible to the
six role meanings, and in particular none whose role-theoretic content emerges
only in an assembled cluster and is not the join of its constituents' role
labels.
\end{definition}

\begin{remark}[The recognition hypothesis is assumed, not derived]\label{rem:recognition-open}
The recognition hypothesis is an explicit assumption on \(D\), not a consequence
of the \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}} definitions. Two kinds of finite, audited, in-domain feature are
not known to be recognized: a feature carrying a conservation or balance law over
declared records --- a finite resource invariant of the kind admitted by
Definition~\ref{def:finite} --- whose content supplies none of the six witness
types, and a feature whose closure content is an emergent obstruction or holonomy
of an assembled cluster, not reducible to the role labels of its constituents.
Whether every finite audited feature is recognized --- equivalently, whether the
six roles are \emph{recognition-complete} for \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}} --- is left open and is
recorded with the endogenous-instrument meta-limit of
Sections~\ref{subsec:meta-limit} and~\ref{subsec:future-meta-limit}. The three
threat closures of
Propositions~\ref{prop:probability-closure}--\ref{prop:agency-closure} establish
the recognition hypothesis unconditionally for the three highest-priority threat
classes; the classification theorem below assumes it in general.
\end{remark}

\label{prop:channel-vs-activation}
Let \(D \in \ensuremath{\mathsf{FATCD}}\) and let \(\Dec{D}\) be a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion
record. The following are distinct statements:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \emph{Six channels}: the channel sequence
    \((\Chan{i}{D})_{i=1}^{6}\) has length six with the fixed role names
    \ensuremath{\mathrm{P1}}, \ldots, \ensuremath{\mathrm{P6}}.
  \item \emph{Six active projections}: for each \(i\),
    \(\Status{i}{D} = \texttt{active\_projection}\) and the channel carries an active
    \(\pi_i(D)\).
\end{enumerate}

\label{prop:channel-vs-activation}
Let \(D \in \FATCD{}\) and let \(\Dec{D}\) be a well-formed decomposition/exhaustion
record. The following are distinct statements:
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*),topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
  \item \emph{Six channels}: the channel sequence
    \((\Chan{i}{D})_{i=1}^{6}\) has length six with the fixed role names
    \Pone{}, \ldots, \Psix{}.
  \item \emph{Six active projections}: for each \(i\),
    \(\Status{i}{D} = \activeproj\) and the channel carries an active
    \(\pi_i(D)\).
\end{enumerate}
Theorem~\ref{thm:six-channel-exactness} establishes (i) for every
\(D \in \FATCD{}\). It does not establish (ii). In particular, an
admissible \(D \in \FATCD{}\) may carry any number of active projections
between zero and six; inactive channels are recorded with status
\(\belowthr\), \(\collapsedbc\), \(\absentrec\), or \(\outsidescope\)
and are not active witnesses for the corresponding roles.\footnote{Tracked in the formalization harness as a conditional schema (\texttt{SixBirds.channel\_vs\_activation}); see Appendix~\ref{app:mechanization}.}

conclusion: The three parts introduced in Section play complementary roles. The primitive role architecture (Section ) fixes the vocabulary: six role meanings, the behavioral, verification, and structural-categorical level pattern, and the local boundary distinctions. This vocabulary alone does not certify any claim, since it does not specify which role talk is admissible. The admissibility and meta-theory regime (Section ) supplies that certification through honest bookkeeping, typed non-collapse, the forgetting and selected-lift architecture, activation thresholds, instrument-relative visibility, and empirical-bridge admissibility. Admissibility alone, however, yields no terminal claim; it only regulates what may be asserted. The exact-six theorem chain (Sections – ) supplies the quantification: the FATCD domain, the six lower-bound witnesses, the upper-bound classification, the decomposition/exhaustion theorem, and the integrated stress certification together deliver Theorem . Vocabulary without admissibility would be undisciplined; admissibility without a theorem chain would be inconclusive; a theorem chain without the first two would lack a subject.

conclusion: Six Birds Foundations I introduced the theory-package formalism T = (Z, f, Sigma_f, E, A) and derived the P1–P6 vocabulary under minimal hypotheses of composability with limited interface access. The present paper does not re-derive that vocabulary; it takes the six roles as given and asks a different question: whether, within a specific admissibility regime and over a specific class of admissible descriptions, the six roles are exactly enough. The Foundations theorem gives the canonical unavoidability side of the picture; the terminal theorem here gives the scoped exhaustion side. The two statements address different questions and address them at different levels; combining them does not yield a stronger claim, and neither theorem follows from the other. The theorem chain also draws on a nearby result. , complementing the no-go analysis of , established that protocol holonomy is not a directionality certificate: noncommutativity of update sequences can be nonzero while path-reversal asymmetry remains zero, so route mismatch is a diagnostic, not an arrow of time. conclusion: The paper records five core finite-calculus theorems in Section 6: No total six-symbol algebra (Theorem 1, Section 6): cell status does not factor through the primitive pair (P_ i ,P_ j ) alone, blocking any total binary algebra on P as a status-decoding map. Typed non-collapse (Theorem 2, Section 6): an admissible directed-cell judgment P_i P_j , even with status action , does not identify the actor and informant primitives. Cell well-formedness decidability (Theorem 3, Section 6): the well-formedness predicate on a finite typed cell record is decidable on finite records. Covered-cell status uniqueness (Theorem 4, Section 6): on a covered finite cell, the classifier of Subsection 5.6 returns a unique cell status. Status-family separation (Theorem 5, Section 6): the five judgment-attached status families remain typed-separately judgment-indexed, with gate and square status families likewise kept separate by their own inputs.

The paper records five core finite-calculus theorems in Section 6:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{No total six-symbol algebra} (Theorem 1, Section 6): cell status does not factor through the primitive pair \((P_{i},P_{j})\) alone, blocking any total binary algebra on \(\mathbb P\) as a status-decoding map.
\item
  \emph{Typed non-collapse} (Theorem 2, Section 6): an admissible directed-cell judgment \(P_i\leftarrow P_j\), even with status \(\texttt{action}\), does not identify the actor and informant primitives.
\item
  \emph{Cell well-formedness decidability} (Theorem 3, Section 6): the well-formedness predicate on a finite typed cell record is decidable on finite records.
\item
  \emph{Covered-cell status uniqueness} (Theorem 4, Section 6): on a covered finite cell, the classifier of Subsection 5.6 returns a unique cell status.
\item
  \emph{Status-family separation} (Theorem 5, Section 6): the five judgment-attached status families remain typed-separately judgment-indexed, with gate and square status families likewise kept separate by their own inputs.
\end{itemize}

The paper records the promotion-and-stacking theorems of Section 10 and the self-reference theorems of Section 11:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Promotion gate soundness} (Theorem 19) and \emph{strict promotion implies nonfactorization} (Theorem 20): any accepted-family promotion verdict requires every required core gate to exist and pass, and a strict promotion verdict implies a nonfactorization witness on the carrier.
\item
  \emph{Non-strict promotion implies factorization} (Theorem 21): a non-strict promotion verdict on an admissible bridge implies a factorization filler.
\item
  \emph{Toy strict bridge} (Example Theorem 22): a finite two-layer bridge witnesses the strict-promotion pattern without proving any general stacking-composition theorem.
\item
  \emph{No-overreading suppression} (Theorem 23, Section 11): no \(I\)-accepted claim depends on unbridged suppressed content.
\item
  \emph{Same-level self-audit failure} (Theorem 24, Section 11): an instrument \(I_{0}\) does not certify its own complete soundness; the verdict is \(\texttt{outside\_scope}\) or \(\texttt{undefined\_circular}\).
\item
  \emph{Finite rotating-audit theorem} (Theorem 25, Section 11): a finite stack \(\mathbb I_{\le N}\) admits a level-\(N+1\) extension instrument that audits the lower stack and accepts compliance iff the stack-audit defect is empty, while remaining non-final on its own soundness.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: This subsection records the finite rotating-audit theorem of Foundations III. The theorem is theorem-grade: it states that, given any finite stack of admissible instruments, there is a one-level extension instrument and an audit bridge that can finitely audit the lower stack and accept its compliance iff the stack-audit defect is empty, while the higher instrument does not thereby certify itself. The statement, proof, and non-finality are recorded in Subsubsections 11.8.1–11.8.3. The theorem supports NC-17 of Subsection 2.4.3.

The paper records its earned content as a layered theorem stack:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Finite typed calculus and core theorems.} Sections 6 and 7 record the no-total-algebra theorem (Theorem 1), the four core finite-interaction theorems (Theorems 2--5), and the nine descent/packaging/completion/strictness theorems (Theorems 6--14), all theorem-grade with verdict \(\texttt{accepted}\).
\item
  \emph{No-go and cohomological theorems.} Section 8 records the four cohomological no-drive theorems (Theorems 15--18) on graph-supported drive.
\item
  \emph{Countermodel/no-go atlas.} Section 9 and Appendix C record twelve countermodels (CM\_1--CM\_12), each blocking a specific overclaim about the calculus under a finite typed structure.
\item
  \emph{Promotion and instrument-indexed semantics.} Section 10 records the promotion gate and strictness theorems (Theorems 19--21) together with the Toy22 strict-bridge example (Theorem 22), and Section 11 records the no-overreading suppression theorem (Theorem 23), the same-level self-audit failure theorem (Theorem 24), and the finite rotating-audit theorem (Theorem 25), each accompanied by the finite typed instrument-indexed claim form.
\item
  \emph{Scoped model realizations.} Section 12 records theorem-grade abstract-interpretation host results (Theorems 26--28) and the model-grade abstract-interpretation family result (Model Theorem 29). Section 13 records the PICA realization (Model Theorem 33), the Cantor strict-bridge realization (Model Theorem 34), and the graph/cohomology realization, all model-grade with verdict \(\texttt{model\_realization}\) on declared fragments.
\item
  \emph{High-structure semantics as secondary organization.} Section 14 records three decorated-square recovery theorems (Theorems 30--32) over a finite double-category fragment, presented as secondary organization rather than as a replacement for the core calculus.
\item
  \emph{Lean validation audit.} Section 15 records the manifest-scoped Lean 4 validation artifact and Proposition 35, with the audit-grade verdict \(\texttt{audit\_report}\).
\end{itemize}

The paper records its earned content as a layered theorem stack:

\begin{itemize}
\tightlist
\item
  \emph{Finite typed calculus and core theorems.} Sections 6 and 7 record the no-total-algebra theorem (Theorem 1), the four core finite-interaction theorems (Theorems 2--5), and the nine descent/packaging/completion/strictness theorems (Theorems 6--14), all theorem-grade with verdict \(\texttt{accepted}\).
\item
  \emph{No-go and cohomological theorems.} Section 8 records the four cohomological no-drive theorems (Theorems 15--18) on graph-supported drive.
\item
  \emph{Countermodel/no-go atlas.} Section 9 and Appendix C record twelve countermodels (CM\_1--CM\_12), each blocking a specific overclaim about the calculus under a finite typed structure.
\item
  \emph{Promotion and instrument-indexed semantics.} Section 10 records the promotion gate and strictness theorems (Theorems 19--21) together with the Toy22 strict-bridge example (Theorem 22), and Section 11 records the no-overreading suppression theorem (Theorem 23), the same-level self-audit failure theorem (Theorem 24), and the finite rotating-audit theorem (Theorem 25), each accompanied by the finite typed instrument-indexed claim form.
\item
  \emph{Scoped model realizations.} Section 12 records theorem-grade abstract-interpretation host results (Theorems 26--28) and the model-grade abstract-interpretation family result (Model Theorem 29). Section 13 records the PICA realization (Model Theorem 33), the Cantor strict-bridge realization (Model Theorem 34), and the graph/cohomology realization, all model-grade with verdict \(\texttt{model\_realization}\) on declared fragments.
\item
  \emph{High-structure semantics as secondary organization.} Section 14 records three decorated-square recovery theorems (Theorems 30--32) over a finite double-category fragment, presented as secondary organization rather than as a replacement for the core calculus.
\item
  \emph{Lean validation audit.} Section 15 records the manifest-scoped Lean 4 validation artifact and Proposition 35, with the audit-grade verdict \(\texttt{audit\_report}\).
\end{itemize}

In the finite decorated double-category fragment of Subsection 14.1, the decorated square Xi_ comp for a pair of finite completions E_ 1 ,E_ 2 :C→ C is exact iff E_ 1 E_ 2 =E_ 2 E_ 1 on C . The square is obstructed iff there exists c∈ C with E_ 1 E_ 2 (c)≠ E_ 2 E_ 1 (c) , and the noncommutation E_ 1 E_ 2 ≠ E_ 2 E_ 1 is recovered as a P_ 3 -pasting defect of the calculus. Proof. The decorated square Xi_ comp has both horizontal edges equal to E_ 2 and both vertical edges equal to E_ 1 . Exactness in the sense of Subsubsection 14.1.2 is the commutation equality of the boundary composition: the upper-right path E_ 1 E_ 2 :C→ C equals the lower-left path E_ 2 E_ 1 :C→ C . By definition of composition on the finite poset C , this is the equation E_ 1 E_ 2 =E_ 2 E_ 1 on C .

The square is obstructed iff there exists \(c\in C\) with \(E_{1}E_{2}(c)\neq E_{2}E_{1}(c)\), and the noncommutation \(E_{1}E_{2}\neq E_{2}E_{1}\) is recovered as a \(P_{3}\)-pasting defect of the calculus.

By definition of composition on the finite poset \(C\), this is the equation \(E_{1}E_{2}=E_{2}E_{1}\) on \(C\).

conclusion: q_I factors through pi
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:F10}
Let \(\sigma_I:H\to\Sigma\) be an observation signature with access
quotient \(q_I:H\to Q_I\).  Every observable \(o:H\to R\) that
is constant on access classes factors uniquely through
\(q_I\):
\[
  o=\overline o\circ q_I
\]
for a unique \(\overline o:Q_I\to R\).  Moreover, \(Q_I\) is the
coarsest quotient carrying the declared observations: if
\(\pi:H\to Q'\) is any quotient whose fibers are observation-invisible,
then \(q_I\) factors through \(\pi\).

A functorial gate using only the existing access quotient cannot
produce a strict new current distinction.  If a readout
\(d:H\to D\) is current-visible without additional apparatus data,

\[
  \splitObs_{\mathrm{dist}}(q_I,d)=\varnothing,
  \qquad\text{equivalently}\qquad
  d=\overline d\circq_I
\]
for some \(\overline d:Q_I\to D\).  If the obstruction is nonempty,
the distinction requires declared memory data, bridge data, residual
budget, scope change, or an enlarged calibration family.

\begin{definition}[Hiddenness interface]\label{def:hiddenness-exposure}
A \emph{hiddenness interface} \(I\) consists of a closure carrier
\(\mathcal H_I\), a current quotient
\(\currQ_I:\mathcal H_I\to Q_I\), a predictive quotient
\(\predM_I:\mathcal H_I\to M_I\) refining \(\currQ_I\), and the
following predicates:
\[
  \operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I),
\]
together with
\[
  \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I),\quad
  \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I).
\]
The hidden-from-current predicate records that one current fiber
contains at least two predictive classes.  The quotient-exposed
predicate records that the lawful exposure quotient removes exactly
those predictive splits.  The hiddenness normal form is the
five-conjunct property
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{HiddennessNormalForm}(I)
  :={}&
  \operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I)\bigr)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)\bigr)\\
  &{}\wedge
  \bigl(\operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I)
    \leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I)\bigr).
\end{align*}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Hiddenness Normal Form]\label{thm:F13a}
Let \(I\) be a hiddenness interface and let
\[
  \mathsf{src}:
  \operatorname{Paper7SaturatedSATInstance}(I)
\]
be the opaque saturated-SAT source certificate.  Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I).
\end{align*}
That is, \(I\) satisfies
\(\operatorname{HiddennessNormalForm}(I)\).
\end{theorem}
\footnote{The Lean theorem at
\texttt{Access.HiddennessNormalForm.hiddenness\_normal\_form}
proves the layer-agnostic statement under a substrate-pending axiom
\texttt{hiddenness\_pending} guarded by an opaque source predicate;
the substrate proof appears in \citep{Tsiokos2026PvNP} and will
discharge the axiom when its Lean ships.  See
\Cref{app:formalization} for the narrowing disclosure.}
\begin{proof}
Apply the same-paper substrate-pending axiom
\(\mathrm{hiddenness\_pending}\), specialized to the hiddenness
interface \(I\) under the saturated-SAT source certificate \(\mathsf{src}\).
The axiom delivers the conjunction
\[
  \operatorname{HiddennessNormalForm}(I),
\]
that is, the five displayed conjuncts in the statement:
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{determiningStateTyped}(I),\qquad
  \operatorname{minimalRelevantUpstream}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{QuotientExposed}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{PredictiveCollapse}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{lawfulCurrentExposure}(I),\\
  &\operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(I)
    \iff \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(I).
\end{align*}
The substrate-side proof of the axiom lives in the saturated-SAT
analysis of \citet{Tsiokos2026PvNP}; within this paper the
wrapper records the layer-agnostic conjunction as the hiddenness
normal form.  The opacity-guard pattern of \Cref{sec:apparatus}
ensures that no instantiation of \(\mathrm{hiddenness\_pending}\) can
derive \(\mathrm{False}\) from the axiom alone: the guard
\(\operatorname{Paper7SaturatedSATInstance}\) has no public
constructor, so an actual instance must come from the saturated-SAT
substrate Lean.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:F13b}
Let \(\mathsf{FPC}\) be the class of formed predictive closures
\(\mathcal C\), each carrying a hiddenness interface with current
quotient \(Q\) and predictive quotient \(M\), together with
four declared side-condition predicates
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{genuinelyFormed}(\mathcal C),\qquad
  \operatorname{saturatedCurrentizers}(\mathcal C),\\
  &\operatorname{determiningStateDeclared}(\mathcal C),\qquad
  \operatorname{sourceReadoutSeparated}(\mathcal C).
\end{align*}
Write
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{FormedClosureReady}(\mathcal C)
  :={}&
  \operatorname{genuinelyFormed}(\mathcal C)
  \wedge\operatorname{saturatedCurrentizers}(\mathcal C)\\
  &{}\wedge\operatorname{determiningStateDeclared}(\mathcal C)
  \wedge\operatorname{sourceReadoutSeparated}(\mathcal C).
\end{align*}
Let \(\operatorname{CSLSrc}:\mathsf{FPC}\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be the
opaque CSL diagnosis-source predicate.
Then for every \(\mathcal C\in\mathsf{FPC}\),
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{CSLSrc}(\mathcal C)
  \Longrightarrow{}&
    \operatorname{FormedClosureReady}(\mathcal C)\\
  \Longrightarrow{}&
    \bigl(
      \operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}(\mathcal C)
      \iff
      \operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}(\mathcal C)
    \bigr).
\end{align*}
Here \(\operatorname{PredictiveSurplus}\) and
\(\operatorname{HiddenFromCurrent}\) are the predictive-surplus and
hidden-from-current predicates of \Cref{def:hiddenness-exposure}.  In
a formed predictive closure with the CSL diagnosis source and the
four declared side conditions, predictive surplus across the
\(M/Q\) gap survives exactly when the determining state is
hidden from current observation.

\label{thm:F6}
Let \(\mathcal P\) be a formed stability package with a
layer-dissolving membrane.  Suppose \(\mathcal P\) declares:
\begin{itemize}
  \item a currency block \(C\) on its exterior carrier of size \(e\);
  \item a layer-bridge block \(L\) of size \(y\times e\) and a
  dissolving-direction block \(D\) of size \(z\times e\), with block
  currency pieces \(K_{LL}\), \(K_{LD}\), \(K_{DL}\), and \(K_{DD}\);
  \item the symmetry conditions \(K_{DL}=K_{LD}^{\!\top}\) and
  \(K_{LL}^{\dagger}=(K_{LL}^{\dagger})^{\!\top}\), together with the
  Moore--Penrose projection identity
  \[
    K_{LL}\,K_{LL}^{\dagger}\,K_{LD}=K_{LD};
  \]
  \item currency and residual budgets
  \[
    K_{LL}\preceq \Theta_Y,
    \qquad
    \Xi(C,L,D,K_{LL}^{\dagger})\preceq \Omega_Z,
  \]
  where \(\Xi\) is the adequacy residual;
  \item a transport selector \(S\) of size \(d\times z\) satisfying
  the endpoint budget
  \[
    S\bigl(\widehat E\,\Theta_Y\,\widehat E^{\!\top}
      +\Omega_Z\bigr)S^{\!\top}\preceq\Theta_D,
  \]
  where \(\widehat E\) is the optimal native explanation determined
  by \((C,L,D,K_{LL}^{\dagger})\).
\end{itemize}
Then the transported dissolving block satisfies the Loewner endpoint
\[
  S\,K_{DD}\,S^{\!\top}\preceq\Theta_D .
\]
Equivalently, every layer-dissolving move accepted by \(\mathcal P\)
is bounded by its declared transport budget; no unpriced
layer-dissolving needle survives the formed package.

The first transport law is the quotient descent criterion already
introduced in \Cref{sec:intro}.  We use the split-pair obstruction of

\begin{definition}[Canonical target-repair quotient]\label{def:target-repair}
Let \(q:X\to Q\), \(F:X\to Y\), and \(r:Y\to R\).  The canonical
target-repair relation \(\equiv_F\) on \(R\) is the smallest
equivalence relation generated by the identifications
\[
  r(Fx)\equiv_F r(Fx')
  \qquad\text{whenever}\qquad
  q(x)=q(x').
\]
The \emph{canonical target-repair quotient} is
\[
  R_F:=R/{\equiv_F},
\]
with quotient map \(c_F:R\to R_F\).
\end{definition}

\label{thm:F4}
Let \(\mathcal G\) be a set of global states, let \(\mathcal F\) be a
set of local-family data, let
\(\operatorname{Comp}:\mathcal F\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be the
overlap-compatibility predicate, and let
\[
  R:\mathcal G\longrightarrow\mathcal F
\]
be a declared restriction map such that
\(\operatorname{Comp}(R(g))\) for every \(g\in\mathcal G\).  For
\(a\in\mathcal F\), write
\[
  \operatorname{Globalizes}_R(a)
  \quad:\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \exists g\in\mathcal G,\ R(g)=a.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Comp}(a)
  &\Longrightarrow
  \bigl(\operatorname{Globalizes}_R(a)
  \iff a\in R(\mathcal G)\bigr),\\
  \operatorname{ExactlyOneStatus}(a)
  &\iff
  \operatorname{OverlapInconsistent}(a)
  \mathbin{\dot\vee}
  \operatorname{CompatibleNonGlobal}(a)\\
  &\hspace{3.5em}\mathbin{\dot\vee}
  \operatorname{GloballyAmbiguous}(a)
  \mathbin{\dot\vee}
  \operatorname{GloballyExact}(a),
\end{align*}
where the four status predicates are determined by
\(\operatorname{Comp}(a)\), membership in \(R(\mathcal G)\), and the
cardinality of the fiber \(R^{-1}(a)\).

\label{thm:F5}
Let \(K:B\to Q_K\) be a branchwise quotient and
\(R:B\to Q_R\) a recombination quotient on the same branch carrier.
Then branchwise equality determines recombination equality if and only
if \(R\) factors through \(K\), that is, if and only if there exists
\(\rho:Q_K\to Q_R\) such that
\[
  R=\rho\circ K .
\]
Equivalently, the branch-merge split-pair obstruction of
\Cref{def:bridge-composition} is empty.

\begin{definition}[Selection obstruction]\label{def:selection-obstruction}
Let a declared symmetry group \(G\) act on a carrier \(X\), and let
\[
  p:X\to X/G
\]
be the orbit quotient.  For a selectedness predicate
\(\chi:X\to\{0,1\}\), the selection obstruction is the split-pair set
\[
  \Delta(p,\chi)
  =
  \{(x,x')\in X\times X:
      p(x)=p(x')\ \text{and}\ \chi(x)\ne\chi(x')\}.
\]
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Selection Obstruction / Repair Normal Form]\label{thm:F15a}
Let \(G\) act on a set \(X\) and on an orbit set \(O\) by
\(\rho_X:G\times X\to X\) and \(\rho_O:G\times O\to O\).  Let
\(\pi:X\to O\) be a surjective orbit map, let
\(s:X\to\{0,1\}\) be a selectedness predicate, let
\(\sigma:O\to X\) be a section, and let \(b:X\to B\) be a breaker
readout.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_s
  :=
  \{(x,x')\in X^2:\pi(x)=\pi(x')\ \text{and}\ s(x)\ne s(x')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{EquivariantSelector}(\rho_O,\rho_X,\sigma)
    \wedge \operatorname{TrivialOrbitAction}(\rho_O)\\
  &\hspace{4em}\Longrightarrow
    \forall o\in O,\ \forall g\in G,\
      \rho_X(g,\sigma(o))=\sigma(o),\\
  s\ \text{descends through}\ \pi
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_s=\emptyset
  \iff
  \exists\,\bar s:O\to\{0,1\}\ \text{with}\ \bar s\circ\pi=s,\\
  \operatorname{HasSelectionSplit}(\pi,s)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_s\ne\emptyset.
\end{align*}
Thus an equivariant selector can select only common fixed points
unless a declared breaker \(b\), memory, condition, or quotient
refinement supplies additional data.
\end{theorem}
\footnote{Verified in Lean as
\texttt{Symmetry.SelectionObstruction.selection\_obstruction}; see
\Cref{app:formalization}.}
\begin{proof}
Assume the actions \(\rho_X,\rho_O\), the surjective orbit map
\(\pi\), the selectedness predicate \(s\), and the section
\(\sigma\).  If \(\sigma\) is equivariant and the \(G\)-action on
\(O\) is trivial, then for every \(g\in G\) and \(o\in O\),
\[
  \pi(\rho_X(g,\sigma(o)))
  =
  \rho_O(g,\pi(\sigma(o)))
  =
  \rho_O(g,o)
  =
  o.
\]
Equivariance of the selector gives
\(\rho_X(g,\sigma(o))=\sigma(\rho_O(g,o))=\sigma(o)\), so
\(\sigma(o)\) lies in the common fixed locus of the \(G\)-action on
\(X\).

\label{thm:F15a}
Let \(G\) act on a set \(X\) and on an orbit set \(O\) by
\(\rho_X:G\times X\to X\) and \(\rho_O:G\times O\to O\).  Let
\(\pi:X\to O\) be a surjective orbit map, let
\(s:X\to\{0,1\}\) be a selectedness predicate, let
\(\sigma:O\to X\) be a section, and let \(b:X\to B\) be a breaker
readout.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_s
  :=
  \{(x,x')\in X^2:\pi(x)=\pi(x')\ \text{and}\ s(x)\ne s(x')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{EquivariantSelector}(\rho_O,\rho_X,\sigma)
    \wedge \operatorname{TrivialOrbitAction}(\rho_O)\\
  &\hspace{4em}\Longrightarrow
    \forall o\in O,\ \forall g\in G,\
      \rho_X(g,\sigma(o))=\sigma(o),\\
  s\ \text{descends through}\ \pi
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_s=\emptyset
  \iff
  \exists\,\bar s:O\to\{0,1\}\ \text{with}\ \bar s\circ\pi=s,\\
  \operatorname{HasSelectionSplit}(\pi,s)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_s\ne\emptyset.
\end{align*}
Thus an equivariant selector can select only common fixed points
unless a declared breaker \(b\), memory, condition, or quotient
refinement supplies additional data.

\label{thm:F15b}
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a closure space with a \(G\)-action, let
\(\Omega:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be the ground-state predicate,
and let \(\mathcal B=\mathcal C/G\) be the branch quotient.  Suppose
a future branch-selection formation source is given for
\((\mathcal C,G,\Omega)\).  Then there is a formation operator
\[
  F:\mathcal C\longrightarrow\mathcal B
\]
and data \(c\in\mathcal C\), \(g\in G\) such that
\[
  \Omega(c)
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  g\cdot F(c)\ne F(c).
\]
Equivalently,
\[
  \exists F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal B,\,
  \exists c\in\mathcal C,\,
  \exists g\in G,\,
  \Omega(c)\wedge g\cdot F(c)\ne F(c).
\]

\label{thm:F40}
Let \(G\) act on a history space \(H\) by
\(\alpha:G\times H\to H\), let \(q:H\to Q\) be a surjective quotient,
let \(\bar\alpha:G\times Q\to Q\) be a candidate descended action,
let \(D:G\times H\to\{0,1\}\) be a domain predicate, and let
\(r:H\to V\) be a readout with value action
\(\rho:G\times V\to V\).  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_{\alpha}
  :=
  \{(g,h,h'):\ q(h)=q(h')\ \text{and}\
    q(\alpha(g,h))\ne q(\alpha(g,h'))\},
\]
and define \(\mathcal O_D\) analogously by replacing
\(q(\alpha(g,h))\) with \(D(g,h)\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{SymmetryDescends}(q,\alpha)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\alpha}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{DomainDescends}(q,D)
  &\iff \mathcal O_D=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{GroupLawPreserved}(\bar\alpha)
  &\iff
  \forall g,g'\in G,\forall \bar h\in Q,\,
    \bar\alpha(gg',\bar h)=
    \bar\alpha(g,\bar\alpha(g',\bar h)),\\
  \operatorname{ReadoutPreserved}(r,\alpha,\rho)
  &\iff
  \forall g\in G,\forall h\in H,\,
    r(\alpha(g,h))=\rho(g,r(h)).
\end{align*}
An anomaly is precisely the failure of at least one of these four
conditions.

\label{thm:F41}
Let \(\mathcal C_A,\mathcal C_B\) be formed closures with quotients
\(q_A:\mathcal C_A\to Q_A\) and \(q_B:\mathcal C_B\to Q_B\).  Let
\(F:\mathcal C_A\to\mathcal C_B\) and
\(G:\mathcal C_B\to\mathcal C_A\) descend to
\(\bar F:Q_A\to Q_B\) and \(\bar G:Q_B\to Q_A\).  Let
\(r_A:R_A\to S_A\), \(r_B:R_B\to S_B\) be role readouts, let
\(\tau:R_A\to R_B\) be role translation, let
\(\rho:S_A\to S_B\) be the role-value map, and let
\(\phi:\mathcal R_A\to\mathcal R_B\) and
\(\kappa:\mathcal K_A\to\mathcal K_B\) translate routes and claims.
Then a role-preserving duality equivalence holds if and only if
\begin{align*}
  \bar G\circ\bar F&=\mathrm{id}_{Q_A}
  \quad\text{and}\quad
  \bar F\circ\bar G=\mathrm{id}_{Q_B},\\
  r_B\circ\tau&=\rho\circ r_A,\\
  \bar F\circ R_A(\gamma)
  &=R_B(\phi(\gamma))\circ\bar F
  \quad\forall \gamma\in\mathcal R_A,\\
  \operatorname{status}_B(\kappa(k))
  &=\operatorname{status}_A(k)
  \quad\forall k\in\mathcal K_A.
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F17}
Let \(H\) be a carrier with a family of access quotients
\(q_i:H\to Q_i\) indexed by \(i\in I\), a public quotient
\(p:H\to P\), and a target readout \(r:H\to R\).  Assume each
\(q_i\) is surjective, \(p\) is surjective, and the family satisfies
the common-quotient universal property
\(\operatorname{CommonQuotientUniversal}(q,p)\): \(p\) factors
through every \(q_i\), and any quotient through which all \(q_i\)
factor also factors through \(p\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{CommonAcrossAccesses}(q,r)
    \iff \operatorname{PublicDeterminesObject}(p,r),\\
  &\operatorname{CommonAcrossAccesses}(q,r)\\
  &\qquad{}\iff
    \forall i\in I,\,
      \operatorname{AccessObjectivityDefectEmpty}(q_i,r),\\
  &\operatorname{PublicDeterminesObject}(p,r)\\
  &\qquad{}\iff
    \operatorname{ObstructionEmpty}
      \bigl(\operatorname{PublicToObjectDefect}(p,r)\bigr),
\end{align*}
together with
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{CommonQuotientVisible}(q,p),\\
  &\operatorname{RetainsPublicQuotient}
      \bigl(p,\operatorname{objectiveExtension}(p,r)\bigr),\\
  &\operatorname{CarriesObject}
      \bigl(\operatorname{objectiveExtension}(p,r),r\bigr),
\end{align*}
and the status partition
\[
  \operatorname{ExactlyOneObjectivityStatus}(p,r).
\]

\label{thm:F17}
Let \(H\) be a carrier with a family of access quotients
\(q_i:H\to Q_i\) indexed by \(i\in I\), a public quotient
\(p:H\to P\), and a target readout \(r:H\to R\).  Assume each
\(q_i\) is surjective, \(p\) is surjective, and the family satisfies
the common-quotient universal property
\(\operatorname{CommonQuotientUniversal}(q,p)\): \(p\) factors
through every \(q_i\), and any quotient through which all \(q_i\)
factor also factors through \(p\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{CommonAcrossAccesses}(q,r)
    \iff \operatorname{PublicDeterminesObject}(p,r),\\
  &\operatorname{CommonAcrossAccesses}(q,r)\\
  &\qquad{}\iff
    \forall i\in I,\,
      \operatorname{AccessObjectivityDefectEmpty}(q_i,r),\\
  &\operatorname{PublicDeterminesObject}(p,r)\\
  &\qquad{}\iff
    \operatorname{ObstructionEmpty}
      \bigl(\operatorname{PublicToObjectDefect}(p,r)\bigr),
\end{align*}
together with
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{CommonQuotientVisible}(q,p),\\
  &\operatorname{RetainsPublicQuotient}
      \bigl(p,\operatorname{objectiveExtension}(p,r)\bigr),\\
  &\operatorname{CarriesObject}
      \bigl(\operatorname{objectiveExtension}(p,r),r\bigr),
\end{align*}
and the status partition
\[
  \operatorname{ExactlyOneObjectivityStatus}(p,r).
\]

\label{thm:F19}
Let \(H_i,H_j\) be carriers with access quotients
\(q_i:H_i\to Q_i\) and \(q_j:H_j\to Q_j\), and let
\(\gamma:H_i\to H_j\) be a declared transport.  Assume \(q_i\) and
\(q_j\) are surjective.  Let
\(\operatorname{viable}:Q_j\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be a viability
predicate, \(C:H_i\times H_j\to\mathrm{Prop}\) a relation predicate,
and let
\[
  \bar\gamma:Q_i\to Q_j,\qquad
  \bar\eta:Q_j\to Q_k,\qquad
  \operatorname{compBar}:Q_i\to Q_k
\]
be arbitrary holonomy data (no compatibility between
\(\operatorname{compBar}\) and \(\bar\eta\circ\bar\gamma\) is
assumed).  Then
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{Persists}(q_i,\gamma,q_j)
    \iff
    \operatorname{PersistenceObstructionEmpty}(q_i,\gamma,q_j),\\
  &\operatorname{SplitObstructionEmpty}(q_i,\gamma,q_j)
    \iff
    \operatorname{Persists}(q_i,\gamma,q_j),\\
  &\operatorname{ViablePersistence}(\gamma,q_j,\operatorname{viable})
    \iff
    \operatorname{DissolutionObstructionEmpty}
      (\gamma,q_j,\operatorname{viable}),\\
  &\operatorname{RelationValuedPersistence}(q_i,q_j,C)
    \iff
    \operatorname{RelationPersistenceObstructionEmpty}(q_i,q_j,C),\\
  &\operatorname{IdentityHolonomyCoherent}
      (\bar\gamma,\bar\eta,\operatorname{compBar})\\
  &\qquad{}\iff
    \operatorname{IdentityHolonomyDefectEmpty}
      (\bar\gamma,\bar\eta,\operatorname{compBar}),
\end{align*}
together with the comparison-status partition
\[
  \operatorname{ExactlyOnePersistenceComparisonStatus}
    (q_i,\gamma,q_j),
\]
and the retention and carrying conditions
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{RetainsOldIdentity}
      \bigl(q_i,\operatorname{persistenceExtension}(q_i,\gamma,q_j)\bigr),\\
  &\operatorname{CarriesLaterIdentity}
      \bigl(\operatorname{persistenceExtension}(q_i,\gamma,q_j),
        \gamma,q_j\bigr).
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F20}
Let \(H_0,H_1,H_s,H_t\) be history spaces with event readout
\(\varepsilon:H_0\to E\), continuation \(\gamma:H_0\to H_1\),
record readouts
\[
  \rho_1:H_1\to R_1,\qquad
  \rho_s:H_s\to R_s,\qquad
  \rho_t:H_t\to R_t,
\]
transport \(\theta:H_s\to H_t\), descended transport
\(\bar\theta:R_s\to R_t\), fact-value maps
\(d_s:R_s\to E_s\), \(d_t:R_t\to E_t\), update
\(u:E_s\to E_t\), and a packaging map \(C:H\to H\) on an auxiliary
carrier \(H\).  Define the record signature
\[
  s:=\rho_1\circ\gamma:H_0\to R_1,
\]
and assume that \(s\) and \(\rho_s\) are surjective.  Define
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{ev}}
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H_0^2:
      \rho_1(\gamma h)=\rho_1(\gamma h')
      \text{ and } \varepsilon(h)\ne\varepsilon(h')\},\\
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{red}}
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H_0^2:
      \varepsilon(h)=\varepsilon(h')
      \text{ and } \rho_1(\gamma h)\ne\rho_1(\gamma h')\},\\
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{rec}}
  &:=
  \{(x,y)\in H_s^2:
      \rho_s(x)=\rho_s(y)
      \text{ and } \rho_t(\theta x)\ne\rho_t(\theta y)\},\\
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{val}}
  &:=
  \{r\in R_s:
      d_t(\bar\theta r)\ne u(d_s r)\}.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{EventRecorded}(\varepsilon,\gamma,\rho_1)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\mathrm{ev}}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{RecordStable}(\rho_s,\theta,\rho_t)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\mathrm{rec}}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{FactValueStable}(\bar\theta,d_s,d_t,u)
  &\iff \mathcal O_{\mathrm{val}}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{StableFact}
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{ev}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{rec}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{val}}=\emptyset.
\end{align*}
together with the record-comparison status partition
\[
  \operatorname{ExactlyOneRecordComparisonStatus}
    (\varepsilon,\gamma,\rho_1),
\]
the retention and carrying conditions for the record-event extension
\(\langle\rho_1\circ\gamma,\varepsilon\rangle:H_0\to R_1\times E\),
\begin{align*}
  &\operatorname{RetainsRecord}
      \bigl(\rho_1\circ\gamma,
        \langle\rho_1\circ\gamma,\varepsilon\rangle\bigr),\\
  &\operatorname{CarriesEvent}
      \bigl(\langle\rho_1\circ\gamma,\varepsilon\rangle,
        \varepsilon\bigr),
\end{align*}
and the idempotent-packaging fixed-point property
\[
  \operatorname{IdempotentPackaging}(C)
  \Longrightarrow
  \forall h\in H,\ C(C(h))=C(h).
\]
The record-comparison status takes one of four values
(\emph{exact}, \emph{redundant}, \emph{ambiguous}, or
\emph{incomparable}) determined by the joint emptiness pattern of
\(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{ev}}\) and \(\mathcal O_{\mathrm{red}}\).

\label{thm:F22}
Let \(q:X\to Q\) be a source quotient, let
\(\beta:Y\to B\) be a boundary readout, let
\(U:X\times Y\to X'\) be an interface update, and let
\(q':X'\to Q'\) be the target quotient.  Assume \(q\), \(\beta\),
and \(q'\) are surjective.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_U
  :=
  \{((x,y),(x',y')) :
    q(x)=q(x'),\ \beta(y)=\beta(y'),\
    q'(U(x,y))\ne q'(U(x',y'))\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{InterfaceMediated}(q,\beta,U,q')
  &\iff \mathcal O_U=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar U:Q\times B\to Q'\ \text{with}\
    \bar U(q(x),\beta(y))=q'(U(x,y))\ \forall x,y,\\
  \mathcal O_U=\emptyset
  &\Longrightarrow
  \operatorname{BoundaryLeakageAbsent}\wedge
  \operatorname{InternalInsufficiencyAbsent},\\
  \operatorname{ActiveMediatedInfluence}(\bar U)
  &\iff \neg\operatorname{ExternallyInert}(\bar U).
\end{align*}

\(\operatorname{ResStable}\) and

source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:F26}
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a closure space with lawfulness predicate
\(\operatorname{Lawful}:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\), equivalence relation
\(\sim\) on lawful closures, moduli quotient
\(p:\mathcal C\to M\), readout \(r:\mathcal C\to V\), transport
\(T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C'\), and selected closure
\(c_0\in\mathcal C\).  Assume \(p\) is surjective on lawful
closures.  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ClosureObstructed}(\operatorname{Lawful})
  &\iff
  \neg\exists c\in\mathcal C,\ \operatorname{Lawful}(c),\\
  \operatorname{NontrivialModuli}(\operatorname{Lawful},\sim)
  &\iff
  \exists c,d\in\mathcal C,\,
    \operatorname{Lawful}(c)\wedge\operatorname{Lawful}(d)
    \wedge \neg(c\sim d),\\
  \operatorname{NecessaryReadout}(r)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar r:M\to V\ \text{with}\
    \bar r(p(c))=r(c)\quad
    \forall c\ \operatorname{Lawful}(c),\\
  \operatorname{ContingentReadout}(r)
  &\iff
  \exists c,d\in\mathcal C,\,
    \operatorname{Lawful}(c)\wedge\operatorname{Lawful}(d)
    \wedge p(c)\ne p(d)\wedge r(c)\ne r(d).
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:F29}
Let \(P\) be a presentation space with quotient
\(\pi:P\to\Pi\), let \(\sim\) be an equivalence relation compatible
with \(\pi\), let \(s:\Pi\to P\) be a section with
\(\pi(s(x))=x\), and let \(T:P\to V\) be a readout.  Let
\(\tau:\operatorname{Tuple}(P)\to\operatorname{Tuple}(\Pi)\) be the
tuple quotient, let \(R:\operatorname{Tuple}(P)\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be a
relation, and let a group \(G\) act on \(P\) and \(V\).  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{PresentationInvariant}(\pi,T)
  &\iff
  \forall p,p'\in P,\ \pi(p)=\pi(p')\Rightarrow T(p)=T(p')\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar T:\Pi\to V\ \text{with}\ \bar T\circ\pi=T,\\
  \operatorname{EquivalentPresentationInvariant}(\sim,T)
  &\iff
  \forall p,p'\in P,\ p\sim p'\Rightarrow T(p)=T(p'),\\
  \operatorname{PresentationRelationInvariant}(\tau,R)
  &\iff
  \forall x,y,\ \tau(x)=\tau(y)\Rightarrow (R(x)\leftrightarrow R(y)),\\
  \operatorname{GroupEquivariant}(T)
  &\iff
  \forall g\in G,\forall p\in P,\ T(g\cdot p)=g\cdot T(p).
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F30}
Let \(H\) be a history space with base readout \(b:H\to B\),
explanation readout \(e:H\to E\), target readout \(t:H\to T\),
continuation \(\kappa:H\to H'\), later explanation
\(e':H'\to E'\), and later target \(t':H'\to T'\).  Assume \(b\)
and \(e\) are surjective.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}
  :=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:b(h)=b(h')\ \text{and}\ e(h)\ne e(h')\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{tgt}}
  :=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:e(h)=e(h')\ \text{and}\ t(h)\ne t(h')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ExactExplanation}(b,e,t)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{src}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{tgt}}=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\alpha:B\to E,\ \exists\,\beta:E\to T,\
    \alpha\circ b=e\ \text{and}\ \beta\circ e=t,\\
  \operatorname{StrictCompression}(b,e)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\alpha:B\to E,\ \alpha\circ b=e
  \ \text{and}\ 
  \neg\exists\,\delta:E\to B,\ \delta\circ e=b.
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:F31}
Let \(q:H\to Q\) be a context quotient, let
\(\alpha:A\to\bar A\) be an intervention abstraction, let
\(\operatorname{Adm}:H\times A\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be admissibility, let
\(\Gamma:H\times A\to H'\) be a counterfactual route, let
\(q':H'\to R\) be a target quotient, and let
\(\tau:H'\to\mathrm{Bool}\) be target truth.  Define
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{adm}}
  :=
  \{((h,a),(h',a')) :
    q(h)=q(h'),\ \alpha(a)=\alpha(a'),\
    \operatorname{Adm}(h,a)\not\leftrightarrow
    \operatorname{Adm}(h',a')\},
\]
and
\[
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{cf}}
  :=
  \left\{
  \begin{array}{l}
    ((h,a),(h',a')) :
    q(h)=q(h'),\ \alpha(a)=\alpha(a'),\\
    \operatorname{Adm}(h,a),\ \operatorname{Adm}(h',a'),\\
    \tau(\Gamma(h,a))\ne\tau(\Gamma(h',a'))
  \end{array}
  \right\}.
\]
Write \(\operatorname{CFL}\) for the counterfactual-legitimacy
predicate for this data.  Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{CFL}(q,\alpha,\operatorname{Adm},\Gamma,q',\tau)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{adm}}=\emptyset
  \wedge
  \mathcal O_{\mathrm{cf}}=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \begin{gathered}
    \exists\,\bar\tau:Q\times\bar A\to\mathrm{Bool}
    \ \text{such that}\\
    \bar\tau(q(h),\alpha(a))=\tau(\Gamma(h,a))
    \ \text{for all admissible }(h,a).
  \end{gathered}
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F33}
Let \(H\) be a set of histories with an interior--exterior
decomposition \(H \cong I \times E\), and define
\[
  \pi : I \times E \longrightarrow B \times Q,
  \qquad
  \pi(i,e)=(\beta(i),\varepsilon(e)),
\]
where \(\beta:I\to B\) is the boundary readout and
\(\varepsilon:E\to Q\) is the exterior classifier. Assume \(\pi\) is
surjective, and let \(t:I\times E\to T\) be a declared target readout.
Then
\begin{align*}
  t \text{ descends through }\pi
  &\iff
  \forall (i,e),(i',e'),\
    \pi(i,e)=\pi(i',e')\Rightarrow t(i,e)=t(i',e')\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar t:B\times Q\to T\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar t\circ\pi=t .
\end{align*}
For a family \((t_\sigma)_{\sigma\in\Sigma}\), horizon sufficiency is
the pointwise conjunction of these equivalent conditions for every
\(\sigma\in\Sigma\).

\begin{theorem}[Information Loss Normal Form]\label{thm:F34}
Let \(H_0,H_1\) be source and later carriers with transport
\(\tau:H_0\to H_1\). Let \(\sigma:H_0\to I\) be source information,
\(\rho:H_1\to R\) a recovery quotient, \(q_0:H_0\to Q_0\) a source
quotient, \(q_1:H_1\to Q_1\) a later quotient, and
\(s:H_0\to S\) a declared signature. Assume that
\(\rho\circ\tau\), \(q_0\), and \(q_1\circ\tau\) are surjective onto
their images. Define
\[
  \mathcal O_\rho
  =\{(h,h'):\rho(\tau h)=\rho(\tau h')\ \text{and}\
      \sigma(h)\ne\sigma(h')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{Recoverable}(\sigma,\tau,\rho)
  &\iff \mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\\
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar\sigma:R\to I\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau=\sigma .
\end{align*}
Information loss is legitimate exactly when every declared later
identification made by \(\rho\circ\tau\) is invisible to \(\sigma\).
\end{theorem}
\footnote{\raggedright Verified in Lean as
\texttt{SelfReferenceLimits.\allowbreak{}InformationLoss.\allowbreak{}information\_loss\_normal\_form};
see \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\begin{proof}
Assume the named maps and the surjectivity of \(\rho\circ\tau\). If
\(\sigma=\bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau\), then
\[
  \rho(\tau h)=\rho(\tau h')
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \sigma(h)=\bar\sigma(\rho(\tau h))
           =\bar\sigma(\rho(\tau h'))=\sigma(h'),
\]
so \(\mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\). Conversely assume
\(\mathcal O_\rho=\emptyset\). For \(r\in R\) in the image of
\(\rho\circ\tau\), choose \(h\) with \(\rho(\tau h)=r\) and define
\[
  \bar\sigma(r):=\sigma(h).
\]
If \(h'\) is another choice, then \((h,h')\notin\mathcal O_\rho\), so
\(\sigma(h)=\sigma(h')\); hence \(\bar\sigma\) is well-defined and
\(\bar\sigma\circ\rho\circ\tau=\sigma\). If
\(\mathcal O_\rho\ne\emptyset\), some pair \(h,h'\) has the same
recovered class but different source information, which is precisely
loss across an access class.
\end{proof}

The famous physical instance is the black-hole information paradox
posed in \citet{Hawking1976BHThermodynamics}; the layer-agnostic
statement above records the descent obstruction abstracted from
that substrate.

\label{thm:F37}
Let \(H\) be a carrier with two access quotients
\(q_A:H\to Q_A\) and \(q_B:H\to Q_B\). A joint access is a quotient
\(j:H\to J\) together with maps \(a:J\to Q_A\) and \(b:J\to Q_B\)
satisfying
\[
  a\circ j=q_A,\qquad b\circ j=q_B .
\]
Assume \(q_A\) and \(q_B\) are separately admissible. Then
\begin{align*}
  q_A \perp_{\mathrm{acc}} q_B
  \iff
  \neg\exists (J: \mathrm{Type})(j:H\to J)(a:J\to Q_A)(b:J\to Q_B),\
  a\circ j=q_A\ \wedge\ b\circ j=q_B .
\end{align*}
Thus complementarity is precisely non-existence of an admissible joint
quotient carrying both accesses.

Let \(H_s,H_t\) be source and target history sets with continuation
\(\kappa:H_s\to H_t\). Let \(r_s:H_s\to R_s\) and
\(r_t:H_t\to R_t\) be surjective record quotients, and let
\(s_s:R_s\to S\), \(s_t:R_t\to S\) be status readouts into a preorder
\((S,\le_S)\). Then
\begin{align*}
  r_t\circ\kappa \text{ descends through } r_s
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar\kappa:R_s\to R_t\ \text{ such that }\
    \bar\kappa\circ r_s=r_t\circ\kappa,\\
  \operatorname{Arrow}(\kappa)
  &\iff

  \bar\kappa\circ r_s=r_t\circ\kappa
  \ \wedge\
  \forall x\in R_s,\ s_s(x)\le_S s_t(\bar\kappa x).
\end{align*}
The arrow is the monotone direction of the descended record transport.

\label{thm:F39}
Let \(q:H\to Q\) be a surjective access quotient with target readout
\(t:H\to T\).  Let \(q_F:H\to Q_F\) be a finer quotient and
\(q_C:H\to Q_C\) a coarsening, related by a factorization
\(c:Q_F\to Q_C\) with
\[
  c\circ q_F=q_C.
\]
Let \((\mathcal E,\le_E)\) be a preorder of entropy values, and let
\[
  E:\{\,q':H\to Q'\,\}\longrightarrow \mathcal E
\]
be an entropy functional assigning a fiber-volume value to every
declared quotient.  Suppose the apparatus declares a mixing
functional \(m\) and a combiner
\(\odot:\mathcal E\times\mathcal E\to\mathcal E\) satisfying the
chain-rule identity
\[
  E(q_C)=E(q_F)\odot m(q_F,q_C)
\]
and the combine-monotonicity condition
\[
  \forall a,b\in\mathcal E,\quad a\le_E a\odot b.
\]
Define the raw split-pair and target obstructions
\begin{align*}
  \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{raw}}
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:q(h)=q(h')\ \text{and}\ h\ne h'\},\\
  \mathcal O_q(t)
  &:=
  \{(h,h')\in H^2:q(h)=q(h')\ \text{and}\ t(h)\ne t(h')\}.
\end{align*}
Then
\begin{align*}
  E(q)=0
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_q^{\mathrm{raw}}=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{TargetEntropyZero}(q,t)
  &\iff
  t\ \text{descends through}\ q,\\
  \operatorname{TargetUnresolved}(q,t)
  &\iff
  \neg(t\ \text{descends through}\ q),\\
  \forall b\in Q_C,\ \forall h\in H,\quad
  q_C(h)=b
  &\iff
  \exists a\in Q_F,\ c(a)=b\ \wedge\ q_F(h)=a,\\
  E(q_F)
  &\le_E
  E(q_C).
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F42}
Let \(H\) be a set of objects with base map \(b:H\to B\), compression
map \(e:H\to E\), target readout \(t:H\to T\), and route updates
\(r_\gamma:H\to H\) for \(\gamma\in\Gamma\). Let
\(\operatorname{cost}:E\to C\) take values in a strict preorder
\((C,<)\). A compression \(e\) is closed for \(h\in H\) when \(t\) and
all \(e\circ r_\gamma\) descend through the \(e\)-class of \(h\). Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e,h)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_t(e,h)=\emptyset
  \ \wedge\
  \forall\gamma\in\Gamma,\ \mathcal O_\gamma(e,h)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{Irreducible}(h)
  &\iff
  \neg\exists e'\!,\
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e',h)
  \ \wedge\
  \operatorname{cost}(e')<\operatorname{cost}(e(h)).
\end{align*}

Let \(H\) be a set of objects with base map \(b:H\to B\), compression
map \(e:H\to E\), target readout \(t:H\to T\), and route updates
\(r_\gamma:H\to H\) for \(\gamma\in\Gamma\). Let
\(\operatorname{cost}:E\to C\) take values in a strict preorder
\((C,<)\). A compression \(e\) is closed for \(h\in H\) when \(t\) and
all \(e\circ r_\gamma\) descend through the \(e\)-class of \(h\). Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e,h)
  &\iff
  \mathcal O_t(e,h)=\emptyset
  \ \wedge\
  \forall\gamma\in\Gamma,\ \mathcal O_\gamma(e,h)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{Irreducible}(h)
  &\iff
  \neg\exists e'\!,\
  \operatorname{ClosedCompression}(e',h)
  \ \wedge\
  \operatorname{cost}(e')<\operatorname{cost}(e(h)).
\end{align*}
Irreducibility is therefore absence of a shorter closed description.

\label{thm:F44}
Let \(\mathcal C\) be a control space with quotient
\(c:\mathcal C\to C\), phase readout \(\varphi:\mathcal C\to\Phi\),
formedness predicate \(F:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and
neighborhood relation \(N(x,U,y)\). Let
\(S,M,U,R:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\) denote, respectively,
status-change, margin-vanishing, non-uniform response, and
residuals-statused. For a readout \(r:\mathcal C\to V\), define
\[
  \mathcal O_c(r)=
  \{(x,y):c(x)=c(y)\ \text{and}\ r(x)\ne r(y)\}.
\]
Then, for \(x,\ell,r_0\in\mathcal C\),
\begin{align*}
  r \text{ descends through }c
  &\iff \mathcal O_c(r)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{PhaseTransition}(\ell,r_0)
  &\iff \varphi(\ell)\ne\varphi(r_0),\\
  \operatorname{PhaseBoundary}(x)
  &\iff F(x)\ \wedge\
    \neg\exists U,\ \forall y,\ N(x,U,y)\Rightarrow \varphi(y)=\varphi(x),\\
  \operatorname{Critical}(x)
  &\iff \operatorname{PhaseBoundary}(x)\wedge (M(x)\vee U(x))\wedge R(x).
\end{align*}

target readout \(t:H\to T\), signature \(\sigma:H\to\Sigma\), update

\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{LocalToDomain}(\ell,t)
  &\iff \mathcal O_\ell(t)=\emptyset,\\

  \neg\exists \ell',\ \ell'\!<\ell\ \wedge\
  \operatorname{TargetFamilyLocal}(\ell',\sigma).

\label{thm:F47}
Let \(M\) be a moduli space, \(r:M\to V\) a readout, and
\(T:V\to\mathrm{Prop}\) a target-region predicate.  Let
\(\mathcal M\) be the carrier type of measure-record values, let
\(\mu:\mathrm{Pow}(M)\to\mathcal M\) be a measure record on subsets
of \(M\), let \(\mu_{\mathrm{tot}}\in\mathcal M\) be the total
measure, let \(\theta\) be a threshold, and let
\(\odot:\Theta\times\mathcal M\to\mathcal M\) be the declared
threshold scaling.  Let \(\operatorname{Pos}:\mathcal M\to
\mathrm{Prop}\) and \({\le_{\mathcal M}}\subseteq
\mathcal M\times\mathcal M\) be the declared positivity and order
predicates on the measure record.  Let \(\mathrm{sel}\in M\) be a
selected modulus, let \(\mathsf{selDec}\) be a selector-declared
predicate, and let
\(\mathsf{modDec},\mathsf{tgtDec},\mathsf{meaDec},\mathsf{thrDec},
\mathsf{presStat}\) be the five required apparatus-declaration
predicates.  Define the selector region
\[
  \Sigma(r,T):=\{m\in M:T(r(m))\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  m\in\Sigma(r,T)
  &\iff
  T(r(m)),\\
  \operatorname{Small}(\Sigma(r,T))
  &\iff
  \operatorname{Pos}(\mu(\Sigma(r,T)))
  \wedge
  \mu(\Sigma(r,T))\le_{\mathcal M}\theta\odot\mu_{\mathrm{tot}},\\
  \operatorname{Realized}(\Sigma(r,T),\mathrm{sel},\mathsf{selDec})
  &\iff
  \mathsf{selDec}
  \wedge
  \mathrm{sel}\in\Sigma(r,T)
  \wedge
  \operatorname{Small}(\Sigma(r,T)),\\
  \operatorname{TargetImpossible}(\Sigma(r,T))
  &\Longrightarrow
  \neg\operatorname{Realized}(\Sigma(r,T),\mathrm{sel},\mathsf{selDec}),\\
  \operatorname{WellTyped}
  &\iff
  \mathsf{modDec}\wedge\mathsf{tgtDec}\wedge\mathsf{meaDec}
  \wedge\mathsf{thrDec}\wedge\mathsf{presStat}.
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F48}
Let \(G\) be a set of global states with gluing quotient
\(\gamma:G\to\Gamma\), readout \(r:G\to V\), transport
\(\tau:G\to G'\), and target gluing quotient \(\gamma':G'\to\Gamma'\).
Assume \(\gamma\) is surjective, and define
\[
  \mathcal O_\gamma(r)=
  \{(g,g'):\gamma(g)=\gamma(g')\ \text{and}\ r(g)\ne r(g')\}.
\]
Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)
  &\iff \mathcal O_\gamma(r)=\emptyset,\\
  \operatorname{CompleteInvariant}(r)
  &\iff \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)\wedge
    \forall g,g',\ r(g)=r(g')\Rightarrow \gamma(g)=\gamma(g'),\\
  \operatorname{CoarseInvariant}(r)
  &\iff \operatorname{TopologicalReadout}(r)\wedge
    \exists g,g',\gamma(g)\ne\gamma(g')\wedge r(g)=r(g'),\\
  \operatorname{TransportDescends}(\tau)
  &\iff
    \exists\,\bar\tau:\Gamma\to\Gamma'\ \text{ with }\
    \bar\tau\circ\gamma=\gamma'\circ\tau .
\end{align*}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The famous physical instance of correlations that admit no local
common-source explanation is the Einstein--Podolsky--Rosen / Bell
situation \citep{Bell1964EPR}; the layer-agnostic statement below
records the descent-to-common-source obstruction abstracted from
that substrate.

\begin{theorem}[Common-Source / Nonlocal Correlation Normal Form]\label{thm:F49}
Let \(H\) be a history space with source quotient \(\sigma:H\to S\),
shared interface \(\iota:H\to I\), access quotients
\(q_A:H\to L_A\), \(q_B:H\to L_B\), and readouts
\(r_A:H\to A\), \(r_B:H\to B\). Let
\(\kappa:H\to K\) be the correlation readout. Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\bar r_A:S\to A,\bar r_B:S\to B,\
    \bar r_A\circ\sigma=r_A\ \wedge\ \bar r_B\circ\sigma=r_B,\\
  \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota)
  &\iff
  \exists\,\hat r_A:I\to A,\hat r_B:I\to B,\
    \hat r_A\circ\iota=r_A\ \wedge\ \hat r_B\circ\iota=r_B,\\
  \operatorname{LocallyExplainable}(\kappa)
  &\iff \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
    \vee \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota).
\end{align*}
If neither disjunct holds, the correlation is a statused nonlocal
residual.
\end{theorem}
\footnote{\raggedright Verified in Lean as
\texttt{SelfReferenceLimits.\allowbreak{}CommonSourceNonlocal.\allowbreak{}common\_source\_nonlocal\_correlation};
see \Cref{app:formalization}.}
\begin{proof}
Assume the source quotient \(\sigma\), interface \(\iota\), accesses
\(q_A,q_B\), and readouts \(r_A,r_B,\kappa\). If
\(\bar r_A\circ\sigma=r_A\) and \(\bar r_B\circ\sigma=r_B\), then both
local readouts depend only on the shared source class:
\[
  \sigma(h)=\sigma(h')\Rightarrow
  r_A(h)=r_A(h')\ \wedge\ r_B(h)=r_B(h').
\]
This is a common-source explanation. The interface case is identical
with \(\iota\) replacing \(\sigma\). Conversely, any explanation by a
common source or interface gives exactly such descended readouts. Thus
there are two local-explanation cases,
\[
  \operatorname{CommonSource}(\sigma)
  \quad\text{or}\quad
  \operatorname{InterfaceFactorization}(\iota),
\]
and failure of both leaves the correlation as a nonlocal residual.
\end{proof}

\label{thm:F50}
Let \(\mathcal X\) be a closure space with moduli quotient
\(\mu:\mathcal X\to M\), raw background \(b_0:\mathcal X\to B\),
descended background \(b:M\to B\), target \(t:M\to T\), and vacuum
criterion \(V\subseteq M\). Assume \(\mu\) is surjective. Then
\begin{align*}
  b_0 \text{ descends through }\mu
  &\iff
  \exists\,b:M\to B\ \text{ with } b\circ\mu=b_0,\\
  \operatorname{NecessaryBackground}(b)
  &\iff \forall m,m'\in M,\ b(m)=b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{BackgroundModuli}(b)
  &\iff \exists m,m'\in M,\ b(m)\ne b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{Vacuum}(m_\ast)
  &\iff V=\{m_\ast\}\ \wedge\ t(m_\ast)\ \text{is formed}.
\end{align*}

\label{thm:F50}
Let \(\mathcal X\) be a closure space with moduli quotient
\(\mu:\mathcal X\to M\), raw background \(b_0:\mathcal X\to B\),
descended background \(b:M\to B\), target \(t:M\to T\), and vacuum
criterion \(V\subseteq M\). Assume \(\mu\) is surjective. Then
\begin{align*}
  b_0 \text{ descends through }\mu
  &\iff
  \exists\,b:M\to B\ \text{ with } b\circ\mu=b_0,\\
  \operatorname{NecessaryBackground}(b)
  &\iff \forall m,m'\in M,\ b(m)=b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{BackgroundModuli}(b)
  &\iff \exists m,m'\in M,\ b(m)\ne b(m'),\\
  \operatorname{Vacuum}(m_\ast)
  &\iff V=\{m_\ast\}\ \wedge\ t(m_\ast)\ \text{is formed}.
\end{align*}
The necessary/moduli alternatives are exhaustive and disjoint.
