\label{thm:F52}
Let \(R\) be a residual type with predicates
\(\operatorname{hasStatus}:R\to\mathrm{Prop}\) and
\(\operatorname{adequate}:R\to\mathrm{Prop}\). Let \(D\) be a direction
type with predicates \(\operatorname{inScope}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\),
\(\operatorname{claimed}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and
\(\operatorname{namedOutside}:D\to\mathrm{Prop}\), and let
\[
  v\in\{\operatorname{accepted},\operatorname{open},\operatorname{refused}\}
\]
be a meta-audit verdict. Then
\begin{align*}
  \operatorname{ResidualCoverage}
  &\iff
  \forall r\in R,\ \operatorname{hasStatus}(r)\wedge\operatorname{adequate}(r),\\
  \operatorname{MetaCovered}(v)
  &\iff v=\operatorname{accepted},\\
  \operatorname{ScopedClosureComplete}
  &\iff
  \operatorname{formed}\wedge\operatorname{scopeDeclared}\wedge
  \operatorname{ResidualCoverage}\\
  &\qquad\wedge\
  \forall d\in D,\ \operatorname{claimed}(d)\Rightarrow
    \bigl(\operatorname{inScope}(d)\vee\operatorname{namedOutside}(d)\bigr),\\
  \operatorname{MetaComplete}
  &\iff \operatorname{ScopedClosureComplete}\wedge\operatorname{MetaCovered}(v).
\end{align*}

class of carriers, let
\(\operatorname{BareReal}_{\mathfrak S}:\mathcal C\to\mathrm{Prop}\)

  C\ne \mathrm{Cl}_{\mathfrak S}(C).
\]
Equivalently, the direct CER implication
\[
  \operatorname{BareReal}_{\mathfrak S}(C)
  \Longrightarrow

\]
fails in general.

Foundations I--III.  They are not six psychological faculties or six
biological mechanisms; they are typed structural moves.
\begin{center}
\small
\begin{tabularx}{0.94\textwidth}{@{}lX@{}}
\toprule
Role & Imported structural reading \\
\midrule
P1 & descent or lower-operator rewrite \\
P2 & representability and support gating \\
P3 & route mismatch, rerouting, or holonomy reconciliation \\
P4 & staging, sectors, refinement, or gluing \\
P5 & packaging, completion, and formed-object support \\
P6 & audit and accounting, including the constraint surface that governs
other moves \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabularx}
\end{center}
D4 defines \(\mathsf{RepairSort}=\{\mathrm{P1},\ldots,\mathrm{P5}\}\):
P6 is not emitted by \(\mathfrak R_S\) as a repair payload.  An E7 alarm may
rewrite the P6 accounting/constraint surface, but that rewrite remains typed
as audit governance rather than being smuggled into the P1--P5 generator.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:e4}
A lawful compilation candidate
\(R\leadsto K_{\ell}^{\rm compiled}\) requires a certified top-down channel,
a passing memory-only comparator, saturation strictness, and a carried
annotation or decompilation record.  The \texttt{compiled} case additionally
carries independent descent and post-compilation silence certificates.
Within the trained class those certificates remove the per-episode repair
demand:
\[
 \Delta(Q_{\ell}^{\rm compiled},F_{\mathcal C},r)=\varnothing.
\]
Outside that class, a compiled gate can create split-pair obstructions that
defeat descent on a supplied witness.  The formal theorem makes no
counterfactual claim that the formerly exposed repair would have statused or
avoided them.  Compilation may therefore trade recurrent audit cost for
scope-dependent brittleness when the declared out-of-class witness is
present.

The source catalog records a further consequence that is not part of the E7
Lean module.  Suppose viability-coupled positive excess persists across a
declared horizon, the preemption channel has finite carried capacity, and
the total discharge available to that channel is insufficient for the
credited alarm demand.  Then continued treatment of every occurrence as a
fresh currentization cannot remain a free operation.  The source program
allows three audited outcomes: the preemption channel saturates; the system
performs a carried threshold or constraint-set repair; or excess remains as
a statused pathology.  Threshold raising is lawful only when it is charged
to the carried ledger and the original threshold lineage remains available
to audit.  Otherwise the move is indistinguishable from E8.1 budget
inflation, where the report improves while the original-lineage blind spot
does not.

This corollary connects two already named limits without identifying them.
E2 bounds the depth and footprint of carried audit, while E7.1 concerns the
capacity of the preemption channel that acts on viability-coupled excess.
A general theorem translating the E2 carrier-capacity bound into the E7.1
discharge bound remains open.  The corollary is therefore
\emph{interpretation-grade}: its inputs and three outcomes are the
source-program statement, but no theorem in
\path|Laws.E7Alarm| proves their exhaustive partition.

The bridge is not an analyst's pairing of two time series.  It carries a
joint bridge record, a linked defect, source and target ledger entries, and
a shared discharge-comparator certificate, with the appropriate occurrence
carried by each system.  Challenge alignment is taxonomy-relative:
\[
\mathsf{SameTransportChallengeClass}(C_A,C_B)
\iff
\begin{cases}
C_A,C_B\text{ occur in one carried declared taxonomy},\\
\mathsf{taxonomyId}(C_A)=\mathsf{taxonomyId}(C_B),\\
\mathsf{classId}(C_A)=\mathsf{classId}(C_B).
\end{cases}
\]
Matching two informal names is insufficient.

For the receiver repair, let $q_B^-$ and $q_B^+$ be the before and installed
after quotients.  The linked reduction predicate is
\[
\begin{aligned}
\mathsf{TransportDeltaReduction}\iff{}&
\Delta(q_B^+,F_C,r_B)
\subseteq\Delta(q_B^-,F_C,r_B)\\
&{}\land
\exists x,x',\
\Delta(q_B^-,F_C,r_B;x,x')
\land\neg\Delta(q_B^+,F_C,r_B;x,x')\\
&{}\land
q_B^+\text{ is installed by the carried target move}.
\end{aligned}
\]
Consequently, receiver improvement on another class or after an unrelated
move cannot be borrowed by the transport claim.

conclusion: Promotion is passage to a richer layer — C from R , ordinals from N , the 2 -adics from the odd integers — via a recorded bridge. The SAU pattern (Strict Audited Utility): a promoted object U that does not descend may still legally solve a lower-layer problem, provided a selected boundary expression C(U) does descend to a lower-layer answer; the audit never licenses treating U itself as a lower-layer object . Throughout this paper we call that descended, natively checkable assertion the boundary certificate — the term is this paper's own, introduced here once (the F-series papers use per-role certificate vocabulary instead), and it is used in a fixed sense: the native inequality, equality, or finite record that promoted support is allowed to purchase. Every Cluster A law is a SAU specialization in which the promoted object is temporal — a future-valuation ledger, an ordinal escrow, a potential — and the boundary certificate is a descent or termination statement; the 2 -adic ghost -1 of is the canonical non-descending promoted object.

conclusion: passes four further gates inherited from the corpus's discipline: a precise recognition source making every Setup datum definite; a rebadge test requiring the candidate to differ from every existing law on at least one declared axis — for all thirteen laws here the differentiating axis is the same, a step-indexed, growing, adversarial, or rate-comparison witness schema that no static catalog row possesses, which is why an editing pass that accidentally deletes a temporal quantifier from a law's statement collapses the law into its cousin and fails the gate; nonclaim compatibility (a law that needs an unconditional version of a forbidden inference is dead); and a replication ladder on the instantiation table (at least one solved calibration plus at least one instance with genuine engagement beyond citation). expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section has no counterpart in Foundations~IV, and the addition is deliberate: the catalog's laws were
not invented and then illustrated, they were \emph{mined}, and the mining procedure is a first-class
contribution of this paper. The raw material is the class of eccentric problems --- Collatz,
Goodstein, Erd\H{o}s--Straus, Lychrel, Recam\'an, the angel problem, sandpiles, Langton's ant, Ducci,
Gilbreath, aperiodic tilings, Hadwiger--Nelson, Apollonian packings --- problems that are easy to
state, resistant in a characteristic way, and each equipped with a folklore argument that everyone
reaches for and that fails. The thesis of the method is that the folklore argument's failure is
structured: what it illegitimately assumes is a \emph{promoted object}, and what would repair it is a
\emph{descended certificate}, and the gap between the two, once it survives comparison against every
existing law of the corpus, is a new law.

For each problem, in order:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textbf{Identify the tempting almost-proof} --- the argument everyone reaches for that fails.
    The almost-proof reveals the illegal overread.
  \item \textbf{Name the promoted object the almost-proof secretly uses} --- an invariant measure on a
    completion, a fixed finite certificate package, a well-founded escrow. Typically the object does
    not descend to the native carrier.
  \item \textbf{State what a lawful descended certificate would be.} This fixes the boundary
    expression: the native, checkable assertion that promoted support is allowed to purchase
    (\Cref{sec:apparatus}).
  \item \textbf{Isolate the residual that survives every existing law.} Run the candidate against the
    full Foundations~IV catalog (exact statements, not summaries), the Foundations~V laws, the
    nonclaim register, and the AOR status list. What remains unhandled is the law seed --- and this
    step kills candidates as often as it produces them.
  \item \textbf{Find the siblings.} The seed is a law only if the same residual shape appears in at
    least three independent domains, at least one of them solved (the calibration instance).
    Otherwise it is a substrate observation, not a law.
\end{enumerate}
Admission then passes four further gates inherited from the corpus's discipline: a precise recognition
source making every Setup datum definite; a rebadge test requiring the candidate to differ from every
existing law on at least one declared axis --- for all thirteen laws here the differentiating axis is
the same, a step-indexed, growing, adversarial, or rate-comparison witness schema that no static
catalog row possesses, which is why an editing pass that accidentally deletes a temporal quantifier
from a law's statement collapses the law into its cousin and fails the gate; nonclaim compatibility
(a law that needs an unconditional version of a forbidden inference is dead); and a replication
ladder on the instantiation table (at least one solved calibration plus at least one instance with
genuine engagement beyond citation). The remainder of this section runs the protocol on four seeds:
two that became laws, and two that the protocol correctly killed.

\label{thm:G1b}
Assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G1-ghost-convergence]} for a computable neighborhood system $U_h(\Gamma)$ in
    $\widehat{X}$ with $\bigcap_h U_h(\Gamma) = \Gamma$: every infinite bad thread based at a
    nonterminal native point has a limit in $\widehat{X}$, every such limit lies in $\Gamma$, and
    hence for every $h$ the thread is eventually in $U_h(\Gamma)$;
  \item \textup{[H-G1-separation]} for every nonterminal native point $x$ there are computable
    $h(x)$ and $K(x)$, established by native certificates only, with
    \[
      T^{t}(x) \notin U_{h(x)}(\Gamma) \qquad \text{for every } t \ge K(x).
    \]
\end{itemize}
Then $\bigcap_k N_k = \varnothing$; by Part~(a), every nonterminal native point is live, and for each
fixed $x$ the bad-tail predicate $x \in N_k$ is eventually false. For Collatz both hypotheses are
unproved: they are named obligations, not evidence that the conjecture has been settled.

\label{thm:G5}
\textbf{No-go schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G5-unbounded-horizon]} for every fixed depth $m$ there are a step $j$ and states
    $y, z$ in the declared carrier with $q_m(y) = q_m(z)$ but different declared future probe values
    --- a nonempty step-indexed split-pair obstruction $\Delta(q_m, R_b^{\,j}, r_j) \neq \varnothing$.
\end{itemize}
Then no fixed-depth quotient $q_m$ is future-sufficient for the declared unbounded run: for every
$m$, the future probe fails to factor through $q_m$.

\textbf{Confinement schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G5-closed-pattern]} a declared regular or automatic language $\mathcal{P}$
    satisfies $R_b(\mathcal{P}) \subseteq \mathcal{P}$ (cyclically $R_b(P_i) \subseteq P_{i+1}$ when
    phase-indexed, with $\mathcal{P} = \bigcup_i P_i$), and no member of $\mathcal{P}$ satisfies the
    target predicate.
\end{itemize}
Then if some iterate $R_b^{\,N}(x)$ lies in $\mathcal{P}$, no later iterate satisfies the target:
closure gives $R_b^{\,N+t}(x) \in \mathcal{P}$ for every $t \ge 0$, and target-freeness gives
$\lnot\,\mathrm{Pal}_b(R_b^{\,N+t}(x))$ for every $t \ge 0$.

Both halves are conditional: the no-go does not by itself prove escape from the target, and the
confinement applies only after a concrete target-free closed language has been verified.

\label{thm:G6}
\textbf{Covering schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G6-dominant-pressure]} there are a finite exception set $E \subseteq X$, a cofinal
    exhaustion $W_1 \subseteq W_2 \subseteq \cdots$ with $\bigcup_M W_M = X \setminus E$, and for
    each $M$ a finite block decomposition of times after some $N_M$ such that whenever $H_n(W_M)$ is
    nonempty at the start of a block $I$, the audited inequality
    \[
      \sum_{i \in I} \rho_i(W_M) \;\ge\; 1 + \sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i(W_M)
    \]
    holds and the excess is charged to at least one distinct first visit in $H_n(W_M)$ during $I$.
\end{itemize}
Then every point of $X \setminus E$ is eventually visited: the orbit is cofinite-covering relative to
$E$.

\textbf{Hole-forming schema.} Assume
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G6-dominant-obstruction]} there are a target $y \in X$, a time $N$ with
    $y \notin V_N$, and a declared sequence of separating cuts $C_n(y)$ such that for every
    $n \ge N$ every legal path from $(x_n, S_n)$ to $y$ crosses $S_n$ or a certified blocked cut,
    with the quantitative excess $\sum_{i \in I} \gamma_i(C_i(y)) > \sum_{i \in I} \rho_i(C_i(y))$ on
    every later audit block, tied to the displayed cut rather than inferred from density.
\end{itemize}
Then $y$ is a permanent hole: $y \notin V_n$ for all $n \ge N$.

Both directions are schemas: no concrete system satisfies either hypothesis until its rate ledger and
witness cuts are supplied, and the two hypotheses can only conflict on a single target if the audit
record itself is inconsistent.

\label{thm:G8}
Let $(C, V, \{m_v\}, L)$ be a move system with initial configuration $x$, and assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G8]} (abelian compatibility) for every configuration $c$ and all \emph{distinct}
    sites $v \neq w$: if $L_v(c)$ and $L_w(c)$ both hold, then firing either move preserves legality
    of the other, the two composites agree,
    \[
      m_w(m_v(c)) \;=\; m_v(m_w(c)),
    \]
    and both two-step routes record the same counter increment $e_v + e_w$. The case $v = w$ is
    outside the scope of this hypothesis: \textup{[H-G8]} does not require a move to preserve its own
    legality after firing.
  \item \textup{[termination at $x$]} every maximal legal run from $x$ terminates.
\end{itemize}
Then:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Order-independent stabilization.} All legal terminating runs from $x$ end at the same
    stable configuration $x^{\circ}$.
  \item \emph{Odometer invariance.} All legal terminating runs from $x$ have the same counter vector
    $u_x \in \mathbb{N}^{V}$.
\end{enumerate}
If, in addition,
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G8-mono]} (least-action monotonicity) the move system carries a declared comparison
    structure under which stabilizing scripts are compared pointwise, legal move maps are compatible
    with the comparison, and adding available resource or delaying commuting legal moves cannot make a
    genuinely necessary firing disappear from every stabilizing script,
\end{itemize}
then the odometer is pointwise minimal among legally sufficient scripts: for every $n \in
\mathbb{N}^{V}$ whose prescribed multiset of moves is realized by some legal admissible stabilizing
order from $x$,
\[
  u_x(v) \;\le\; n(v) \qquad \text{for every } v \in V.
\]
This is a legal-versus-legal least-action statement. It does not compare the odometer against the
fully general Fey--Levine--Peres class of arbitrary nonnegative stabilizing scripts, which includes
force-firing scripts passing through illegal intermediate configurations.

\label{thm:G9}
Let a run of an extended local system carry the setup data above.

\textbf{Positive schema.} Assume:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textup{[H-G9-census]} the run carries an exact defect ledger, and there is a finite $N$ such
    that for all $n \ge N$ the unresolved defect measure is non-increasing after accounting for bound
    and absorbed defects: $|\mathrm{unresolved}_{n+1}| \le |\mathrm{unresolved}_n|$.
  \item \textup{[H-G9-absorb]} there are finite constants $N, T$ and a finite family of transporter
    records $\{R_j\}$ such that every defect still unresolved for $T$ steps after time $N$ is
    annihilated, bound into a finite non-moving composite, or assigned by the ledger to exactly one
    transporter record.
\end{itemize}
If the transporter-assigned persistent-defect set is nonempty and at least one assigned transporter
has displacement $d \neq 0$, then the run enters a certified transport regime: there is a finite time
$t_0$ and a finite nonempty family of transporter records covering every transporter-assigned
persistent defect after $t_0$, each record satisfying its recurrence-with-displacement equality on its
declared support. Persistent defects bound into stationary residue may coexist; the transport
certification rests on the moving subset. In the single-transporter or common-velocity case the
conclusion is eventual spatio-temporal periodicity modulo translation:
\[
  c_{\,t+\tau}\big|_{W+d} \;=\; \mathrm{shift}_d\!\left(c_t\big|_{W}\right)
  \qquad \text{for all certified } t \ge t_0.
\]
If instead all defects are eventually annihilated or resolved, with no persistent transporter-assigned
defect, the run is cleared or quiescent --- not transport-certified.

\textbf{Negative schema.} Separately, if the ledger exhibits unbounded unresolved creation ---
$\sup_n |\mathrm{unresolved}_n| = \infty$, or infinitely many creation events remain forever unmatched
by annihilation, binding, or absorption --- then the positive transport claim is blocked by the
proliferation ledger itself. Equivalently, such a ledger is incompatible with
\textup{[H-G9-census]}, so the positive schema's census obligation cannot be discharged; no
recurrence-with-displacement record may be inferred from finite local motion or holonomy language
alone.

\label{thm:currency-bridge}
\textbf{(A) C7 solvency.} Fix the G1 data $(T, <, A)$ and a nonterminal point $x$, and let
$\mathrm{badtail}_j(x) \in \{0, 1\}$ indicate membership $x \in N_j$ in the $j$-th bad-tail
membrane. Then pointwise liveness at $x$ --- some $k \ge 1$ with $V_k(x) > 0$ --- holds if and only
if $\mathrm{badtail}_j(x)$ is \textit{eventual\_zero}. Globalized over nonterminal points, this is
the status-language reading of \Cref{thm:G1}.

\textbf{(B) C6 transfinite escrow.} Fix the G2 data and a run satisfying the stage-coherence audit
over a well-founded escrow carrier, and let $\mathrm{notdone}_k \in \{0, 1\}$ indicate that no stage
$i \le k$ has reached the terminal set. Then --- classically, or constructively once a concrete
terminal witness is extracted --- there is a finite stage $K$ reaching the terminal set, and
$\mathrm{notdone}$ is \textit{eventual\_zero}.

\textbf{(C) C5 amortized potential.} Fix a G3-style run with nonnegative actual costs $a_i$,
nonnegative amortized costs $\widehat{a}_i$, nonnegative potential $\Phi$, and write
$A_n = \sum_{i \le n} a_i$, $H_n = \sum_{i \le n} \widehat{a}_i$, $\Phi_0 = \Phi(s_0)$, so that
$A_n \le H_n + \Phi_0$ by \Cref{thm:G3}. Then the status of the amortized-cost sequence converts
into a total-actual-cost bound:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \textit{asymptotic\_budgeted} ($\widehat{a}_i \le B$ for $i \ge J_0$) gives, for every
    $n \ge J_0$, $A_n \le \Phi_0 + H_{\mathrm{head}} + B\,(n - J_0 + 1)$ where
    $H_{\mathrm{head}} = \sum_{i < J_0} \widehat{a}_i$; in particular $A_n = O(n)$;
  \item \textit{summable} ($\sum_i \widehat{a}_i = S < \infty$) gives the uniform bound
    $A_n \le S + \Phi_0$ for every $n$: total actual cost over the infinite run is finite;
  \item \textit{contractive} reduces to the summable case by the geometric tail bound, with the
    explicit constant $A_n \le \Phi_0 + \sum_{i < J} \widehat{a}_i + \widehat{a}_J / (1 - q)$;
  \item \textit{eventual\_zero} ($\widehat{a}_i = 0$ for $i \ge J_0$) gives the fixed finite bound
    $A_n \le \Phi_0 + \sum_{i < J_0} \widehat{a}_i$ for every $n$.
\end{enumerate}

All results are stated for finite systems and deterministic lenses.
The theorem statements are collected in Section~\ref{sec:main-results}, and the later theorem-front sections refer back to those labels.
In one line each, the fronts are:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \emph{Arrow/DPI:} deterministic observation cannot increase forward--reverse path-space KL; equality holds for identity observation. (\Cref{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI})
  \item \emph{Protocol trap:} holonomy can produce apparent protocol structure without honest entropy production, under a stationary initialization scope. (\Cref{thm:NG_PROTOCOL_TRAP})
  \item \emph{Force implies cycles:} nontrivial force-like structure requires non-forest support (positive cycle rank). (\Cref{thm:NG_FORCE_FOREST})
  \item \emph{Null force under exactness:} if the log-ratio 1-form is exact (potential), cycle affinities vanish. (\Cref{thm:NG_FORCE_NULL})
  \item \emph{Closure deficit:} coarse closure deficit is a conditional-information obstruction characterized by a finite variational best macro kernel. (\Cref{thm:NG_MACRO_CLOSURE_DEFICIT})
  \item \emph{Objecthood (bounded):} strict contraction implies at most one fixed distribution; the theorem front addresses uniqueness and separation in the contractive total-variation regime. (\Cref{thm:NG_OBJECT_CONTRACTIVE})
  \item \emph{Idempotence no-ladder:} idempotent packaging stabilizes after one step (no iterate ladder). (\Cref{thm:NG_LADDER_IDEM})
  \item \emph{Bounded-interface no-ladder:} with a fixed finite interface, definability is bounded by $2^{|\mathrm{im}(f)|}$ and no unbounded predicate ladder can arise without leaving the interface scope. (\Cref{thm:NG_LADDER_BOUNDED_INTERFACE})
\end{itemize}

\label{thm:NG_MACRO_CLOSURE_DEFICIT}
Let $(\mathsf{X},P)$ be a finite Markov chain, let $\mu\in\Delta(\mathsf{X})$, let $\Pi:\mathsf{X}\to\mathsf{Y}$ be deterministic, and fix $\tau\ge 1$. For each $x\in\mathsf{X}$, define the packaged future law \[ p_x^{(\tau)}(y') := \Pr_{\mu,P}[\Pi(X_{t+\tau})=y' \mid X_t=x].\] For a candidate macro kernel $K:\mathsf{Y}\times\mathsf{Y}\to[0,1]$, define \[ \mathcal{L}_\tau(K) := \sum_{x\in \mathsf{X}} \mu(x)\,\mathrm{KL}\!\big(p_x^{(\tau)} \mid K_{\Pi(x)}\big).\] Define the closure deficit by \[ \mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi) := I\!\big(X_t;\Pi(X_{t+\tau})\,\big|\,\Pi(X_t)\big).\] Then the kernel \[ K^\star_y(y') := \Pr_{\mu,P}[\Pi(X_{t+\tau})=y' \mid \Pi(X_t)=y] \] satisfies \[ \mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi)=\min_K \mathcal{L}_\tau(K)=\mathcal{L}_\tau(K^\star).\] Moreover, if there exist $x,x'\in\mathsf{X}$ with $\Pi(x)=\Pi(x')$, $\mu(x)>0$, $\mu(x')>0$, and $p_x^{(\tau)}\neq p_{x'}^{(\tau)}$, then $\mathrm{CD}_\tau(\Pi)>0$.

caveats: Reuse requires an explicit identification of probability objects, conditional-information convention, and minimization domain.

\begin{proof}[Proof of Theorem~\ref{thm:NG_ARROW_DPI}]
Fix $T\ge 0$ and abbreviate $P := P_T^{\mu,K}\in\Delta(X^{T+1})$ and $Q := P_T^{\mu,K,\mathrm{rev}} = \mathrm{rev}_{\#}P$.
Apply Lemma~\ref{lem:deterministic_dpi_kl} to $\Omega=X^{T+1}$, $\Omega'=Y^{T+1}$ and $g=f^{(T)}$:
\[
D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\big(f^{(T)}_{\#}P \,\|\, f^{(T)}_{\#}Q\big)
\le
D_{\mathrm{KL}}(P\,\|\,Q).
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:rev_pushforward_commute}, $f^{(T)}_{\#}P = P_T^{\mu,K,f}$ and $f^{(T)}_{\#}Q = P_T^{\mu,K,f,\mathrm{rev}}$.
Therefore the left-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)$ and the right-hand side equals $\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$, proving
$\mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K;f)\le \mathcal{A}_T(\mu,K)$ as claimed.
\end{proof}

\label{lem:closure_kl_mixture}
Let $(w_i)_{i\in I}$ be nonnegative weights on a finite index set $I$, not all zero,
and let $(P_i)_{i\in I}$ be probability laws on a finite set $\Omega$.
Define
\[
W := \sum_{i\in I} w_i,
\qquad
R := \frac{1}{W}\sum_{i\in I} w_i P_i.
\]
Then for every probability law $Q$ on $\Omega$,
\[
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,Q\right)
=
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,R\right)
+
W\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(R\,\middle\|\,Q\right).
\]
In particular, $Q=R$ is a minimizer, and the minimum value is
\[
\sum_{i\in I} w_i\,D_{\mathrm{KL}}\!\left(P_i\,\middle\|\,R\right).
\]

Then $a(u,v)=\phi(v)-\phi(u)$ for every oriented edge $(u,v)\in\vec E$.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The first diagnostic layer is the structural defect \(\Xi_{SB}\): the
aggregate record of ways in which a scoped PreSB carrier has not yet
closed as an AOR carrier.  Splitting the defect into strata keeps the
failure mode visible, in the spirit of typed fault-and-failure
taxonomies in the dependable-computing literature
\citep{Avizienis2004Dependability}.  A missing observation typing, an
undeclared stage law, an unwitnessed constraint, an unannotated
rewrite, a missing holonomy transport, an unstatused residual, an
unregistered nonclaim, and an undischarged meta-audit obligation are
different audit failures, even when they all obstruct the same
conclusion that the carrier is audit-closed.  Strata are recorded as
finite multisets in the sense of \citet{Blizard1989Multiset}, so a
record may appear with multiplicity matching the carrier-field data
that creates it.

\begin{definition}[Structural defect $\Xi_{SB}$]\label{def:aor:xi-sb}
The \emph{structural defect} $\Xi_{SB}(\mathsf C)$ of a PreSB carrier
$\mathsf C$ is the disjoint sum of its eight defect strata,
\begin{align*}
  \Xi_{SB}(\mathsf C)
  \;=\;& \Sigma_{\mathrm{obs}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{stage}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{constraint}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{rewrite}}(\mathsf C) \\
  & {} \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{holonomy}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{nonclaim}}(\mathsf C) \sqcup \Sigma_{\mathrm{meta}}(\mathsf C),
\end{align*}
with the strata defined in \Cref{def:aor:sigma-obs}--\Cref{def:aor:sigma-meta}.
The carrier is AOR exactly when every stratum is empty.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:aor:cost-table-admissibility}
The base cost table of \Cref{def:aor:cost-table}, together with the
asymptotic companion rows used for refinement-chain discharge, satisfies
two admissibility properties:
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Strict descent.}  For every cost-table or asymptotic companion row
  \(\mathrm{Down}(a,s)=w\), the output multiset \(w\) is strictly less
  than the singleton multiset \(\{(a,s)\}\) in the Dershowitz--Manna
  multiset extension \citep{DershowitzManna1979Multiset} of the
  well-founded order on the status coordinate, where base statuses are
  ordered by the rank of \Cref{def:aor:aor-8-statuses}, \texttt{zero} is the unique
  minimum and \texttt{contractive}, \texttt{eventual\_zero},
  \texttt{summable}, and \texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted} ordered above
  \texttt{zero} but below the base non-terminal statuses \texttt{budgeted},
  \texttt{bridged}, \texttt{hidden}, \texttt{moduli}, \texttt{selected},
  \texttt{probabilistic}, \texttt{out\_of\_scope}, \texttt{nonclaim},
  \texttt{blocked}, \texttt{approved\_other}, with
  \texttt{summable}<\texttt{asymptotic\_budgeted} inside the asymptotic
  tier.  Concretely, every output element \((t',s')\in w\) satisfies
  \(s'<s\) in this status order; the primary type coordinate is
  unconstrained.
  \item \emph{Local diamond.}  For every record \(r\) with two distinct
  cost-table moves \(r\to r_1\) and \(r\to r_2\), there exists a common
  cost-table-reachable record \(r_*\) with \(r_1\to^* r_*\) and
  \(r_2\to^* r_*\).
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:aor:cascade-confluence}
The discharge relation on $\Sigma_{\mathrm{residual}}$ is locally confluent: if a residual
atom admits two distinct one-step discharges into records $r_1$ and
$r_2$, then there exists a record $r_3$ reached by further discharges
from both $r_1$ and $r_2$.  Together with termination
(\Cref{thm:aor:cascade-termination}), Newman's lemma
\citep{Newman1942Combinatorial} yields global confluence
\citep{Huet1980ConfluentReductions}: every cascade has a unique normal
form.

conclusion: The central result of this paper is a closure theorem for typed audit carriers. Every carrier in PreSB_ S admits a completion into the audit-closed full subcategory through the reflection Cl_ SB . The construction does not merely adjoin missing data; it makes audit closure a structural operation, so that records, routes, residuals, statuses, nonclaims, and meta-audits remain visible as typed fields rather than being collapsed into an external well-formedness assertion. In that setting, the chain AOR^ ref ⊆AOR^ casc ⊆AOR organizes ordinary record-level audit closure, finite cascade closure, and closure stable under refinement limits. The framework comprises four layers. The first is the closure-completion reflection and its universal property. The second is the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect Xi_ SB , which turns failure of audit closure into typed diagnostic data. The third is the residual layer: the thirteen-type atlas, with reciprocal local and global mismatch types, together with the status catalogue, cost records, downstream obligations, and cascade graphs tracing how residual atoms are paid. The fourth is the refinement layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit. Together they form a self-contained meta-theory of audit-closed carriers.

audit carriers.  Every carrier in $\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}$ admits a
completion into the audit-closed full subcategory through the
reflection $\mathrm{Cl}_{SB}\dashv\iota$.  The construction does not merely
adjoin missing data; it makes audit closure a structural operation,
so that records, routes, residuals, statuses, nonclaims, and
meta-audits remain visible as typed fields rather than being
collapsed into an external well-formedness assertion.  In that
setting, the chain
$\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}^{\mathrm{casc}}\subseteq\mathbf{AOR}$ organizes
ordinary record-level audit closure, finite cascade closure, and
closure stable under refinement limits.

The framework comprises four layers.  The first is the
closure-completion reflection and its universal property.  The second
is the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect $\Xi_{SB}$,
which turns failure of audit closure into typed diagnostic data.  The
third is the residual layer: the thirteen-type atlas, with reciprocal
local and global mismatch types, together with the status catalogue,
cost records, downstream obligations, and cascade graphs tracing how
residual atoms are paid.  The fourth is the refinement
layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish
finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit.
Together they form a self-contained meta-theory of audit-closed
carriers.

The central result of this paper is a closure theorem for typed
audit carriers.  Every carrier in $\PreSB_{\mathfrak S}$ admits a
completion into the audit-closed full subcategory through the
reflection $\ClSB\dashv\iota$.  The construction does not merely
adjoin missing data; it makes audit closure a structural operation,
so that records, routes, residuals, statuses, nonclaims, and
meta-audits remain visible as typed fields rather than being
collapsed into an external well-formedness assertion.  In that
setting, the chain
$\RefStableAOR\subseteq\CascadeStableAOR\subseteq\AOR$ organizes
ordinary record-level audit closure, finite cascade closure, and
closure stable under refinement limits.

The framework comprises four layers.  The first is the
closure-completion reflection and its universal property.  The second
is the eight-stratum decomposition of the structural defect $\XiSB$,
which turns failure of audit closure into typed diagnostic data.  The
third is the residual layer: the thirteen-type atlas, with reciprocal
local and global mismatch types, together with the status catalogue,
cost records, downstream obligations, and cascade graphs tracing how
residual atoms are paid.  The fourth is the refinement
layer, where directed chains and asymptotic statuses distinguish
finite discharge from discharge that only closes at a limit.
Together they form a self-contained meta-theory of audit-closed
carriers.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:p5}
The packaging map $E\colon Z\to Z$ of Definition~\ref{def:E} is idempotent, and
\[
  \operatorname{Fix}(E)\;=\;\operatorname{im}(E)\;=\;\{C(a): a\in\mathrm{HF}\}.
\]
The restricted lens $f\!\upharpoonright\!\operatorname{Fix}(E)\colon \operatorname{Fix}(E)\to\mathrm{HF}$ is a bijection, with inverse
$a\mapsto C(a)$. Writing $i\colon\operatorname{Fix}(E)\hookrightarrow Z$ for the inclusion and
$r\colon Z\to\operatorname{Fix}(E)$, $r(P):=E(P)$, one has
\[

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Theorem~\ref{thm:hfsat} left exactly one $\mathsf{ZF}$ axiom out of the free column: Infinity. We
now show this is not an accident of bookkeeping but a theorem. The boundary of the free part is
sharp from the inside: \emph{no} fixed finite packaging rule, however many times it is iterated
from a hereditarily finite seed, reaches an infinite set. Infinity is therefore the first place
the construction must be \emph{told to continue}---it is a change of rule, not a stronger use of
the old one. This is the saturation reading of \S\ref{sec:intro} realized at the scale of
$\mathrm{HF}$; the comparison with incompleteness remains meta-grade framing.

source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:translation}
There is an effective translation $\Phi\mapsto\Phi^\flat$ from $L_2$-sentences to
$\{\in\}$-sentences with
\[
  M_2\models\Phi\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad M_1\models\Phi^\flat.
\]
Consequently the rank-erasure is lossless: the shadow $(\HF,\in)$ determines the stage sort, the
stage order, and the rank map.

Every surjection f: Z→ X between finite sets admits a section, constructed without any choice principle (the least-index preimage); a section of f is the same datum as a prototype family for the lens. \begin{convention}[Imports]\label{conv:imports}
The following are imported by name and not reproved: the transfinite recursion building the
cumulative hierarchy $V_0=\varnothing$, $V_{\alpha+1}=\mathcal{P}(V_\alpha)$, $V_\lambda=\bigcup_{\beta
<\lambda}V_\beta$ \citep{Zermelo1930}; the standard stagewise verification of the $\mathsf{ZF}$
axioms in the cumulative hierarchy \citep[Ch.~6]{Jech2003}; the natural models $V_\kappa$
\citep{MontagueVaught1959}; the definability of the von Neumann rank in $\mathsf{ZF}$ (the
infinitary analogue of Theorem~\ref{thm:rankdef}); and the boundary witnesses named in
\S\ref{ssec:nonredundancy}. No item here is a consistency or large-cardinal existence statement.
\end{convention}

Assume \textbf{C-INF}, \textbf{C-POW}, \textbf{C-REPL} over the staged package layer, together
with the imports of Convention~\ref{conv:imports}. Then the rank-erased membership shadow of the
staged hierarchy satisfies every axiom of $\mathsf{ZF}$. If \textbf{C-SEL} is assumed in addition,
the shadow satisfies $\mathsf{ZFC}$.
\end{theorem}

Power set is formulated with Collection rather than merely Replacement; no naive
$H_\kappa$ assertion is used as an in-house proof.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:densitydefect}
Let $F(\mathcal D)=\{p:\text{no }q\le p\text{ lies in }\mathcal D\}$ be the failure set of a
family $\mathcal D$. Then
\[
  F(D_g)=\{g\},\qquad
  F(E_x)=\{p:B_x\subseteq\operatorname{dom} p,\ p\!\upharpoonright\! B_x\text{ constant}\}.
\]
That is, the only condition below which $D_g$ fails to be dense is the total condition $g$
itself, and $E_x$ fails exactly at the conditions that have already fixed the whole block to a
constant.

Over an infinite index set with finite conditions, $F(D_g)=\varnothing$ for every $g$, and

conclusion: The following classical facts are cited at strength, in relative-consistency form. (a) If ZF is consistent, so is ZFC+CH (the constructible inner-model packaging, ). (b) If ZF is consistent, so is ZFC+ (a generic-extension packaging adjoining _2 Cohen reals, ; the ccc cardinal-preservation analysis is part of the imported machinery, ). Read through Table : one substrate admits two lawful completions—an inner-model packaging and a generic-extension packaging—with CH true in the first and false in the second. The ground lens does not determine the continuum readout; its value varies across admissible packagings of the same substrate.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ch}
The following classical facts are cited at strength, in relative-consistency form. \textup{(a)}
If $\mathsf{ZF}$ is consistent, so is $\mathsf{ZFC}+\mathsf{CH}$ (the constructible inner-model
packaging, \citealp{Godel1938,Godel1940}). \textup{(b)} If $\mathsf{ZF}$ is consistent, so is
$\mathsf{ZFC}+\neg\mathsf{CH}$ (a generic-extension packaging adjoining $\aleph_2$ Cohen reals,
\citealp{Cohen1963}; the ccc cardinal-preservation analysis is part of the imported machinery,
\citealp[VII]{Kunen2011}). Read through
Table~\ref{tab:correspondence}: one substrate admits two lawful completions---an inner-model
packaging and a generic-extension packaging---with $\mathsf{CH}$ true in the first and false in
the second. The ground lens does not determine the continuum readout; its value varies across
admissible packagings of the same substrate.

conclusion: [style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31 ,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt] The finite-carrier regime. It licenses finite gates, finite transport, least-index sections, and finite diagnostics; it does not license any infinitary commitment. Admission of an inductive-stage completion. It is priced by Theorem . Admission of full subpackage completion at arbitrary stages. Its finite shadow is Corollary ; its infinitary totalization is purchased. Admission of unbounded descent transport for definable functional images. Its finite shadow is the transport clause used in Theorem . Admission of canonical lifts for arbitrary fibered lenses. It is identified with choice by Theorem . The forcing section's relative host hypothesis: a countable transitive ground model of ZFC , or a sufficiently large finite fragment. The imported classical generic-extension machinery for Cohen forcing. It is named wherever the argument uses the extension M[G] rather than only the in-house Rasiowa–Sikorski construction. The computational exhibits have pass/fail gates recorded in the JSON artifacts and validators. They test encodings and numerical predictions; they do not raise a finite diagnostic to theorem grade.

\begin{description}[style=multiline,leftmargin=!,labelwidth=0.31\textwidth,labelsep=0.8em,itemsep=3pt]
\item[\textbf{A\_FIN}.] The finite-carrier regime. It licenses finite gates, finite transport,
least-index sections, and finite diagnostics; it does not license any infinitary commitment.
\item[\textbf{C-INF}.] Admission of an inductive-stage completion. It is priced by
Theorem~\ref{thm:nonattain}.
\item[\textbf{C-POW}.] Admission of full subpackage completion at arbitrary stages. Its finite

Its finite shadow is the transport clause used in Theorem~\ref{thm:hfsat}.
\item[\textbf{C-SEL}.] Admission of canonical lifts for arbitrary fibered lenses. It is identified
with choice by Theorem~\ref{thm:choice}.
\item[\textbf{J1}.] The forcing section's relative host hypothesis: a countable transitive ground
model of $\mathsf{ZFC}$, or a sufficiently large finite fragment.
\item[\textbf{J2}.] The imported classical generic-extension machinery for Cohen forcing. It is
named wherever the argument uses the extension $M[G]$ rather than only the in-house
Rasiowa--Sikorski construction.
\item[Diagnostic gates.] The computational exhibits have pass/fail gates recorded in the JSON
artifacts and validators. They test encodings and numerical predictions; they do not raise a
finite diagnostic to theorem grade.
\end{description}

The framework packages an instantiation as a \emph{theory package}: a carrier (micro) space, a lens of observation, a completion/packaging rule, and an audit/defect principle \cite{SixBirdsFramework}.
For the mathematics instantiation we use the same shape, with ``audit'' interpreted as a nonnegative defect ledger (error and mismatch diagnostics).

\begin{definition}[Mathematics theory package]\label{def:math-theory-package}
A \emph{mathematics theory package} is a tuple
\[
\mathcal T \;=\; (Z,\ f,\ \Sigma_f,\ E,\ \mathcal D)
\]
where:
\begin{itemize}
  \item $Z$ is a carrier of discrete protocol objects at a chosen stage (e.g.\ grid functions, truncated sums/products, finite compositions, Cauchy sequences of rationals).
  \item $f:Z\to X$ is a \emph{lens} (a coarse description map). The induced definability structure $\Sigma_f$ is the family of predicates on $Z$ that are visible through $f$ (equivalently: constant on fibers of $f$).
  \item $E:\mathcal V\to\mathcal V$ is a \emph{completion/packaging endomap} on a chosen description space $\mathcal V$ associated to $Z$ (often idempotent or approximately idempotent in a specified norm). The fixed points of $E$ are the internally complete objects recognized by the theory at the chosen scale.
  \item $\mathcal D$ is a \emph{defect ledger}: a designated family of nonnegative diagnostics (error bounds, residual norms, route mismatch statistics) together with a monotonicity principle under refinement/coarsening. In this mathematics instantiation, $\mathcal D$ records feasibility (stability under refinement), not a thermodynamic arrow-of-time.
\end{itemize}
\end{definition}

\label{lem:finite-diff-leibniz}
Let $F$ be a field, let $h\in F$ with $h\neq 0$, and let $f,g:F\to F$.
Define $\delta_h f(x):=(f(x+h)-f(x))/h$.
Then for all $x\in F$,
\[
\delta_h(fg)(x)
\;=\;
\delta_h f(x)\, g(x)
\;+
\;f(x)\, \delta_h g(x)
\;+
\;h\,\delta_h f(x)\,\delta_h g(x).
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:derivation-determined-by-X}
Let $R$ be a commutative semiring and let $A:=R[X]$ be the polynomial ring.
An $R$-derivation $D:\mathrm{Derivation}(R,A,A)$ is uniquely determined by its value on the indeterminate $X\in A$.
Equivalently, evaluation on $X$ induces an $R$-linear equivalence
\[
\mathrm{Derivation}(R,R[X],R[X]) \;\simeq_{\ell[R]}\; R[X],
\qquad
D \longmapsto D(X),
\]
with inverse given (schematically) by ``multiply the formal derivative by a polynomial''.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
This exhibit is deliberately modest.
It does not claim that $\mathrm{Sym}$ is ``the right'' packaging, nor that the observed blow-up has direct implications for the zero set of $\zeta$.
Instead it instantiates the \textsc{SBT} logic:

\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Multiple routes exist} (additive vs multiplicative staging), hence \textbf{P3}\ applies.
  \item \textbf{Feasibility must be audited} by a ledger (\textbf{P6}): mismatch and error should shrink in stable regimes.
  \item \textbf{Staging matters} (\textbf{P4}): outside the domain of convergence, naive truncations are not compatible with the packaged object one hopes to define.
\end{itemize}

conclusion: Quantum relative entropy S(rho\|sigma) is the canonical audit for distinguishability of quantum states. A foundational monotonicity principle states that for any CPTP map Phi , S(rho\|sigma) S(Phi(rho)\|Phi(sigma)). This is the quantum data processing inequality (DPI): applying a channel cannot increase distinguishability. We cite standard sources for DPI and its variants . We stress that DPI itself is a standard theorem; our numerical suite is a regression test for the correctness and numerical stability of our implementations of quantum relative entropy and channel application (Appendix records the default trial counts and tolerances). The repository includes a numerical audit suite that samples random density matrices and random CPTP channels (mixtures of dephasing, depolarizing, and random Kraus families), and records the differences S(rho\|sigma) - S(Phi(rho)\|Phi(sigma)). Figure shows the distribution of these differences across random trials, and Table summarizes the experiment across dimensions.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Quantum relative entropy
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma)
\]
is the canonical audit for distinguishability of quantum states. A foundational monotonicity principle states that for any CPTP map $\Phi$,
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma) \ge S(\Phi(\rho)\|\Phi(\sigma)).
\]
This is the quantum data processing inequality (DPI): applying a channel cannot increase distinguishability.
We cite standard sources for DPI and its variants \citep{lindblad1975,petz1986,wilde2017}.
We stress that DPI itself is a standard theorem; our numerical suite is a regression test for the correctness and numerical stability of our implementations of quantum relative entropy and channel application (Appendix~\ref{app:sims} records the default trial counts and tolerances).

The repository includes a numerical audit suite that samples random density matrices and random CPTP channels (mixtures of dephasing, depolarizing, and random Kraus families), and records the differences
\[
  S(\rho\|\sigma) - S(\Phi(\rho)\|\Phi(\sigma)).
\]
Figure~\ref{fig:quantum-dpi-hist} shows the distribution of these differences across random trials, and Table~\ref{tab:quantum-dpi-summary} summarizes the experiment across dimensions.

conclusion: closes the loop, taking the extracted package back to a validated SAU certificate and to an accepted lower-layer claim. Read together, these results show that SAU is the normal form of strict audited promoted use, not a name chosen to make the central theorem true
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The main claim is that, in finite typed audited promoted-use traces, strict
mathematical usefulness---what we call \emph{Strict Audited Utility} (SAU),
formally defined in \Cref{sec:layers}---forces hidden non-descent paired with
audited boundary descent.  An \emph{audit} here is an explicit checkable
derivation connecting a promoted-layer computation back to a lower-layer
answer; a \emph{boundary} is the single derivation step at which descent
takes place.  We extract this pairing from strict useful traces rather than
posit it.

\Cref{sec:necessity} develops the necessity side.  An essential boundary
necessity theorem shows that any strict useful trace forces a non-descending
support and an audited descent expression at its boundary.  A boundary normal
form theorem shows that the boundary expression has a canonical reduced
shape: one primitive head and a defined support set.  A partial converse then
closes the loop, taking the extracted package back to a validated SAU
certificate and to an accepted lower-layer claim.  Read together, these
results show that SAU is the normal form of strict audited promoted use, not
a name chosen to make the central theorem true.

mathematical usefulness---what we call \emph{Strict Audited Utility} (SAU),
formally defined in \Cref{sec:layers}---forces hidden non-descent paired with
audited boundary descent.  An \emph{audit} here is an explicit checkable
derivation connecting a promoted-layer computation back to a lower-layer
answer; a \emph{boundary} is the single derivation step at which descent
takes place.  We extract this pairing from strict useful traces rather than
posit it.

\Cref{sec:necessity} develops the necessity side.  An essential boundary
necessity theorem shows that any strict useful trace forces a non-descending
support and an audited descent expression at its boundary.  A boundary normal
form theorem shows that the boundary expression has a canonical reduced
shape: one primitive head and a defined support set.  A partial converse then
closes the loop, taking the extracted package back to a validated SAU
certificate and to an accepted lower-layer claim.  Read together, these
results show that SAU is the normal form of strict audited promoted use, not
a name chosen to make the central theorem true.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:sau-essential-boundary-necessity}
Let \(\mathfrak T\) be a finite strict useful trace for a saturated lower problem profile \(\mathfrak P_0\).  Then there exist a hidden promoted subtrace \(H\), an audited boundary expression \(C_H(H)\), and a lower-visible boundary answer \(b^\sharp\) such that
\[
H\not\downarrow_{\mathcal T_0},
\qquad
C_H(H)\downarrow_B b^\sharp.
\]
Moreover, \(b^\sharp\) lies in the lower dependency cone of the final answer; hence there is a lower-visible audited continuation from \(b^\sharp\) to the final answer \(a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}\).

The necessity theorem gives an existence statement.  The normal-form step
compresses that data into a canonical shape: contract the hidden support to a
single node \(U_H\), retain the first audited boundary expression
\(C_H(U_H)\downarrow_B b^\sharp\), and append the lower-visible verifier from
\(b^\sharp\) to \(a^\sharp_{\mathfrak T}\).

\begin{definition}[SAU boundary normal form]
\label{def:sau-boundary-normal-form}
An accepted trace is in SAU boundary normal form when, after deleting irrelevant nodes outside the dependency cone of the final answer, it has the schematic shape
\[
\mathcal T_0
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }
\mathcal T_1,
\qquad
\left[U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp\right],
\]
possibly followed by a lower-visible verifier from \(a^\sharp\) to the final accepted answer.  In a multi-generator case this becomes
\[
\left[\vec U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
\vec C(\vec U)\downarrow_B \vec a^\sharp\right].
\]
Write
\[
\NF_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak T)
\]
for the boundary normal form obtained by contracting hidden promoted support and retaining the first audited lower-visible boundary.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:sau-necessity-soundness-chain}
For finite typed audited traces, the following implication chain holds:
\[
\operatorname{StrictUsefulTrace}(\mathfrak T,\mathfrak P_0)
\Longrightarrow
\exists\mathfrak C(\mathfrak T)\text{ with }\operatorname{ValSAU}(\mathfrak C(\mathfrak T))
\Longrightarrow
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted},
\]
provided the extracted package passes the inherited audit checks.
Equivalently, within this scope, strict useful mathematics has the normal form
\[
\boxed{
\text{non-descending promoted support}
\quad+\quad
\text{audited descending boundary}
}
\]
up to audit-equivalent compression.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{cor:sau-tautology-barrier}
The SAU framework is not only the sufficient condition
\[
\mathsf{SAU}\Rightarrow\operatorname{Useful}.
\]
For finite typed audited strict-use traces, the reverse extraction also holds:
\[
\operatorname{StrictUsefulTrace}
\Rightarrow
\exists\mathsf{SAU}\text{-shaped certificate}.
\]
Thus SAU is a normal form for strict audited promoted use, not merely a name for useful extensions.

\label{thm:sau-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak C\) be a validated raw SAU proof package for
\((\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp)\).  Then the following instrument-indexed claim is accepted:
\[
\Gamma;\mathcal T_0\leadsto\mathcal T_1;I_B
\vdash
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
More explicitly, the accepted claim has the following content:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lower-layer saturation.} No candidate at the fixed lower interface solves the problem:
\[
\forall s\in\mathsf{Cand}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(s))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Promoted answer.} The promoted calculation supplies a lower-layer accepted answer:
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness.} The promoted interface is not a relabeling of the lower interface:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,
\]
with explicit witness pair
\[
(s,s')\in\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1).
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent of the promoted structure.} The promoted structure itself is not accepted as lower-layer content:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent of the selected expression.} The expression selected from the promoted structure descends under the bridge:
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
\item \textbf{No overreading.} The accepted claim asserts only the audited lower descendant \(a^\sharp\), not the whole hidden promoted structure \(U\), at the lower layer.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, \(B_{0\to1}\) is a strictly useful promoted extension of \(\mathcal T_0\) for \(P\) in the sense recorded by the canonical useful-extension definition in \Cref{app:definitions}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:imag-minimal-real-linear-completion}
Let \(J\) be a real-linear hidden half-step satisfying
\[
J^2=-I.
\]
The minimal nonzero real-linear package carrying such a \(J\) is two-dimensional.  In that package, the real algebra generated by \(J\) is
\[
\mathbb R[J]=\{aI+bJ:a,b\in\mathbb R\},
\]
with multiplication
\[
(aI+bJ)(cI+dJ)=(ac-bd)I+(ad+bc)J.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb R[J]\cong \mathbb C
\]
under the map
\[
a+bi\longmapsto aI+bJ.
\]

The dual-number algebra is not an arbitrary choice.  Once one asks for a
commutative real algebra with a nonzero square-zero direction, the algebra

\begin{proposition}[Minimal square-zero real-algebra package]
\label{prop:jet-minimal-square-zero-package}
Let \(R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) be a commutative unital real algebra and let \(\eta\in R_{\mathrm{alg}}\) satisfy
\[
\eta^2=0,
\qquad
\eta\neq 0.
\]
Then the real subalgebra generated by \(1\) and \(\eta\) is canonically isomorphic to \(\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)\):
\[
\mathbb R[\eta]\cong \mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2).
\]
\end{proposition}

\label{thm:jet-sau-certificate}
The first-order dual-number package supplies a Strict Audited Utility certificate for the value-only derivative-extraction problem:
\[
\mathsf{Jet}\models\mathsf{SAU}.
\]
More explicitly, with
\[
\pi_0=\ev_x,
\qquad
\pi_1=j_x^1,
\qquad
U=\varepsilon,
\qquad
C(U;f)=[\varepsilon]f(x+\varepsilon),
\qquad
 a^\sharp=D_x,
\]
the following hold:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the lower profile is saturated:
\[
\operatorname{Sat}(\mathfrak P_{\mathsf{Jet},0});
\]
\item the promotion is strict:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing;
\]
\item the promoted direction is non-descending:
\[
\varepsilon\notin\mathbb R,
\qquad
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\operatorname{st},\id_{\mathbb R[\varepsilon]/(\varepsilon^2)})\neq\varnothing;
\]
\item the selected expression descends by coefficient audit:
\[
[\varepsilon]\circ j_x^1=D_x;
\]
\item the descended answer solves the lower problem:
\[
D_x\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P_{\mathsf{Jet}});
\]
\item the nonclaim register blocks the overread that \(\varepsilon\) is a real scalar or that the derivative was obtained from value alone.
\end{enumerate}

Thus the cohomology layer is strict relative to the purely local edge-admissibility interface.
\end{theorem}

For every witness
\[
\mathfrak W\in\{\mathfrak W_{\Imag},\mathfrak W_{\Jet},\mathfrak W_{\Galois},\mathfrak W_{\Coh}\},

U_{\mathfrak W}\not\downarrow_{\mathcal T_0}

\[

\begin{array}{c|c|c|c}
\text{case} & U_{\mathfrak W} & C_{\mathfrak W}(U_{\mathfrak W}) & a^\sharp_{\mathfrak W} \\

\Coh & a\text{ not globally potential-generated} & [a]\in H^1(\Gamma;k) & \text{descent decision / obstruction certificate.}
\end{array}
\)
}
\]

conclusion: Mathematical transfer at SAU strength is possible exactly at the profile level: a successful source case may suggest a reusable skeleton p , but a target case becomes accepted only when it independently validates an instance of p . Formally, for a source C_s , target C_t , and profile p , Inst_ SAU ( p, C_s) +Inst_ SAU ( p, C_t) implies Useful(B_s,P_s):accepted and Useful(B_t,P_t):accepted. But Inst_ SAU ( p, C_s) +Inst( p, C_t) without target validation does not license Useful(B_t,P_t):accepted .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:sau-transfer-profile-theorem}
Mathematical transfer at SAU strength is possible exactly at the profile level: a successful source case may suggest a reusable skeleton \(\mathfrak p\), but a target case becomes accepted only when it independently validates an instance of \(\mathfrak p\).  Formally, for a source \(\mathfrak C_s\), target \(\mathfrak C_t\), and profile \(\mathfrak p\),
\[
\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Useful}(B_s,P_s):\texttt{accepted}
\text{ and }
\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
But
\[
\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\operatorname{Inst}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\]
without target validation does not license \(\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}\).

This subsection records the appendix-bound certificate grammar that is not
duplicated in the body.  It starts with the role convention behind the six
certificate channels, then records the useful-extension and exact-six variants,

\begin{definition}[Six Birds role convention]
\label{def:sau-roles}
Throughout this paper the six primitive role labels, imported from Foundations~I \citep{TsiokosMathTheory}, are used with the following fixed meanings:
\begin{align*}
P_1 &= \text{descent/closure/rewrite/transport of content},\\
P_2 &= \text{representability/gating/admissibility},\\
P_3 &= \text{route mismatch/holonomy/path or protocol comparison},\\
P_4 &= \text{refinement/staging/gluing},\\
P_5 &= \text{packaging/completion/objecthood/idempotence},\\

\begin{definition}[Six Birds role convention]
\label{def:sau-roles}
Throughout this paper the six primitive role labels, imported from Foundations~I \citeFoundationsI, are used with the following fixed meanings:
\begin{align*}
P_1 &= \text{descent/closure/rewrite/transport of content},\\
P_2 &= \text{representability/gating/admissibility},\\
P_3 &= \text{route mismatch/holonomy/path or protocol comparison},\\
P_4 &= \text{refinement/staging/gluing},\\
P_5 &= \text{packaging/completion/objecthood/idempotence},\\
P_6 &= \text{audit/provenance/replay/drive certification}.
\end{align*}
A role label is not a total algebraic generator. It is a typed channel whose activation requires role-aligned witness data, threshold data, level data, visibility data, audit data, and an explicit nonclaim record.
\end{definition}

conclusion: every edge assignment on a tree descends to a global potential, up to the additive constant freedom on vertices
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{cor:coh-forest-vanishing}
If \(\Gamma\) is a finite tree, then
\[
H^1(\Gamma;k)=0.

\begin{definition}[SAU boundary normal form]
\label{def:sau-boundary-normal-form}
An accepted trace is in SAU boundary normal form when, after deleting irrelevant nodes outside the dependency cone of the final answer, it has the schematic shape
\[
\mathcal T_0
\xleftarrow{\ q\ }
\mathcal T_1,
\qquad
\left[U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp\right],
\]
possibly followed by a lower-visible verifier from \(a^\sharp\) to the final accepted answer.  In a multi-generator case this becomes
\[
\left[\vec U\not\downarrow_q,
\quad
\vec C(\vec U)\downarrow_B \vec a^\sharp\right].
\]
Write
\[
\NF_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak T)
\]
for the boundary normal form obtained by contracting hidden promoted support and retaining the first audited lower-visible boundary.
\end{definition}

\label{thm:sau-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak C\) be a validated raw SAU proof package for
\((\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp)\).  Then the following instrument-indexed claim is accepted:
\[
\Gamma;\mathcal T_0\leadsto\mathcal T_1;I_B
\vdash
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
More explicitly, the accepted claim has the following content:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lower-layer saturation.} No candidate at the fixed lower interface solves the problem:
\[
\forall s\in\mathsf{Cand}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(s))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Promoted answer.} The promoted calculation supplies a lower-layer accepted answer:
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness.} The promoted interface is not a relabeling of the lower interface:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,
\]
with explicit witness pair
\[
(s,s')\in\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1).
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent of the promoted structure.} The promoted structure itself is not accepted as lower-layer content:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent of the selected expression.} The expression selected from the promoted structure descends under the bridge:
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]

\label{thm:sau-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak C\) be a validated raw SAU proof package for
\((\mathfrak P_0,B_{0\to1},U,C,a^\sharp)\).  Then the following instrument-indexed claim is accepted:
\[
\Gamma;\mathcal T_0\leadsto\mathcal T_1;I_B
\vdash
\operatorname{Useful}(B_{0\to1},P):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
More explicitly, the accepted claim has the following content:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Lower-layer saturation.} No candidate at the fixed lower interface solves the problem:
\[
\forall s\in\mathsf{Cand}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(s))\neq\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Promoted answer.} The promoted calculation supplies a lower-layer accepted answer:
\[
a^\sharp\in\mathsf{Ans}_0(P),
\qquad
\mathsf{Eval}_{\Theta_0}(\delta_0(a^\sharp))=\texttt{pass}.
\]
\item \textbf{Strictness.} The promoted interface is not a relabeling of the lower interface:
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing,
\]
with explicit witness pair
\[
(s,s')\in\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1).
\]
\item \textbf{Non-descent of the promoted structure.} The promoted structure itself is not accepted as lower-layer content:
\[
U\not\downarrow_q.
\]
\item \textbf{Audited descent of the selected expression.} The expression selected from the promoted structure descends under the bridge:
\[
C(U)\downarrow_B a^\sharp.
\]
\item \textbf{No overreading.} The accepted claim asserts only the audited lower descendant \(a^\sharp\), not the whole hidden promoted structure \(U\), at the lower layer.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, \(B_{0\to1}\) is a strictly useful promoted extension of \(\mathcal T_0\) for \(P\) in the sense recorded by the canonical useful-extension definition in \Cref{app:definitions}.

source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:sau-basic-classification-soundness}
Let \(\mathfrak T\) be a finite strict useful trace whose reduced boundary is basic.  Then there exists a validated SAU certificate whose profile is classified by \(\mathcal R_{\Basic}\):
\[
\operatorname{StrictUsefulTrace}(\mathfrak T)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\BasicSAU(\Red(\mathfrak T))
\]
\[
\Longrightarrow
\exists \mathfrak C,\mathfrak p
\quad
\ValSAU(\mathfrak C)
\quad\text{and}\quad
\mathfrak p\in\Gen_{\mathrm{fin}}(\mathcal R_{\Basic}).
\]
Moreover,
\[
\Use(B,P):\texttt{accepted}
\]
is licensed only for the lower descendant selected by the classified boundary, not for the hidden support itself.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{cor:sau-classification-nontautological}
The classification theorem does not say that a bridge is useful because it has been named useful.  It says that, for finite strict useful traces whose boundary lies in the basic grammar, the necessity theorem first extracts a hidden-support/descending-boundary normal form, and the head-classification theorem then places that boundary in a typed registry.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:imag-minimal-real-linear-completion}
Let \(J\) be a real-linear hidden half-step satisfying
\[
J^2=-I.
\]
The minimal nonzero real-linear package carrying such a \(J\) is two-dimensional.  In that package, the real algebra generated by \(J\) is
\[
\mathbb R[J]=\{aI+bJ:a,b\in\mathbb R\},
\]
with multiplication
\[
(aI+bJ)(cI+dJ)=(ac-bd)I+(ad+bc)J.
\]
Consequently
\[
\mathbb R[J]\cong \mathbb C
\]
under the map
\[
a+bi\longmapsto aI+bJ.
\]

conclusion: Consequently, an element x∈ L descends to the base field exactly when it is fixed by every K -automorphism of L : x∈ K Longleftrightarrow sigma(x)=x for all sigma∈ G.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:gal-fixed-field-audit}
For the finite Galois extension \(L/K\),
\[
L^G=K,
\qquad
G=\operatorname{Gal}(L/K).
\]
Consequently, an element \(x\in L\) descends to the base field exactly when it is fixed by every \(K\)-automorphism of \(L\):
\[
x\in K
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\sigma(x)=x\text{ for all }\sigma\in G.
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:coh-triangle-witness}
Let \(\Gamma\) be the oriented triangle with edges
\[
e_{12}:v_1\to v_2,
\qquad
e_{23}:v_2\to v_3,
\qquad
e_{31}:v_3\to v_1.
\]
Define \(a\in C^1(\Gamma;k)\) by
\[
a(e_{12})=1,
\qquad
a(e_{23})=0,
\qquad
a(e_{31})=0.
\]
Then \(a\) does not descend to a global potential.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The cochain promotion is strict because the lower local interface forgets the
global obstruction class.  Two edge data can both be locally admissible while
only one carries a nonzero \(H^1\)-class.

\begin{theorem}[Strictness of cohomological promotion]
\label{thm:coh-strictness}
If \(H^1(\Gamma;k)\neq0\), then
\[
\delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(\pi_0,\pi_1)\neq\varnothing.
\]
Thus the cohomology layer is strict relative to the purely local edge-admissibility interface.
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:coh-obstruction-profile}
For a finite connected graph, the cohomology package has the obstruction-ledger profile:
\[
a\not\downarrow_{\mathrm{pot}}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
[a]\neq0
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\exists\gamma\text{ with }\oint_\gamma a\neq0.
\]
When \([a]=0\), the same package supplies a positive descent witness \(\phi\) with \(d_0\phi=a\).  When \([a]\neq0\), it supplies an audited obstruction certificate.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:sau-cross-imag-fields}
The witness \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Imag}}\) is SAU-complete.  Its six-field projection is:
\[
\begin{array}{ll}
\mathsf{SatW}:& \text{no same-layer }H:\{-1,0,1\}\to\{-1,0,1\}\text{ satisfies }H^2(y)=-y,\\[2mm]
\mathsf{StrictW}:& \delta_{\mathrm{fact}}(q,\operatorname{id}_{C_4})\neq\varnothing\text{, witnessed by }(i,-i),\\[2mm]
\mathsf{NonDescW}:& G\not\downarrow_q,\\[1mm]
\mathsf{DescW}:& G^2\downarrow_q F\text{, where }F(y)=-y,\\[1mm]
\mathsf{SolveW}:& F\text{ is the lower reversal required by the half-step problem},\\[1mm]
\mathsf{AuditW}:& q\text{, conjugation, norm, and the nonclaim }G\in\mathcal T_0\text{ is not asserted}.
\end{array}
\]
Consequently,
\[
\mathsf{Imag}\models\mathsf{SAU}.
\]

\end{array}
\]

\[
\mathsf{Jet}\models\mathsf{SAU}.

\label{lem:sau-cross-gal-fields}
The witness \(\mathfrak W_{\mathsf{Gal}}\) is SAU-complete.  Its six-field projection is:
\[

\end{array}
\]

\[
\mathsf{Gal}\models\mathsf{SAU}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:sau-transfer-profile-theorem}
Mathematical transfer at SAU strength is possible exactly at the profile level: a successful source case may suggest a reusable skeleton \(\mathfrak p\), but a target case becomes accepted only when it independently validates an instance of \(\mathfrak p\).  Formally, for a source \(\mathfrak C_s\), target \(\mathfrak C_t\), and profile \(\mathfrak p\),
\[
\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
\operatorname{Useful}(B_s,P_s):\texttt{accepted}
\text{ and }
\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}.
\]
But
\[
\Inst_{\mathsf{SAU}}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_s)
+\operatorname{Inst}(\mathfrak p,\mathfrak C_t)
\]
without target validation does not license \(\operatorname{Useful}(B_t,P_t):\texttt{accepted}\).

Throughout this paper the six primitive role labels are used with the following fixed meanings:
\[
P_1=\text{descent/closure/rewrite/transport of content},\qquad
P_2=\text{representability/gating/admissibility},
\]
\[
P_3=\text{route mismatch/holonomy/path or protocol comparison},\qquad
P_4=\text{refinement/staging/gluing},
\]
\[
P_5=\text{packaging/completion/objecthood/idempotence},\qquad
P_6=\text{audit/provenance/replay/drive certification}.
\]
A role label is not a total algebraic generator. It is a typed channel whose activation requires role-aligned witness data, threshold data, level data, visibility data, audit data, and an explicit nonclaim record.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:imag-linear-audit-channels}
In the real-linear completion \(\mathbb R[J]\cong\mathbb C\), define conjugation by
\[
\overline{aI+bJ}=aI-bJ.
\]
Then the fixed layer of conjugation is exactly the old real scalar layer:
\[
\operatorname{Fix}(\overline{\cdot})=\{aI:a\in\mathbb R\}\cong\mathbb R.
\]
Moreover,
\[
(aI+bJ)\overline{(aI+bJ)}=(a^2+b^2)I
\]
is a nonnegative real scalar audit.

The root \(\sqrt2\) does not descend to \(\mathbb Q\), but its invariant audits do:

\[

\]

(t-\sqrt2)(t+\sqrt2)=t^2-2\in\mathbb Q[t].
\]

The root \(\sqrt2\) does not descend to \(\mathbb Q\), but its invariant audits do:
\[
\Tr_{L/K}(\sqrt2)=\sqrt2+(-\sqrt2)=0\in\mathbb Q,
\]
\[
\Nm_{L/K}(\sqrt2)=\sqrt2(-\sqrt2)=-2\in\mathbb Q,
\]
and the orbit polynomial is
\[
(t-\sqrt2)(t+\sqrt2)=t^2-2\in\mathbb Q[t].
\]

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:csl-core}
Let \(\sigma\) be a computational substrate, let \(L\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\sigma\), and let \(L_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) be
the trace-fingerprint loop class on \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\).  Assume the six
structural premises (a)--(f) above.  Then the following four clauses
hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Dissolution.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) holds
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then for
  every loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and every history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\),
  \[
    \Mclass{\ell.h}\neq\Mclass{h}
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \Qclass{\ell.h}\neq\Qclass{h}.
  \]
  Equivalently, the M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry fails: every
  M-class change is accompanied by a Q-class change.

  \item \emph{Preservation.}  If \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\) fails
  and \((\sigma,L)\) has predictive witness content, then
  there exist a loop \(\ell\inL_{\mathrm{traceFP}}\) and a history
  \(h\inH_{\sigma}^{L}\) such that
  \[
    \LoopActionQ{\ell}{h}=\Qclass{h}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \LoopActionM{\ell}{h}\neq\Mclass{h}.
  \]
  The M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry holds.

  \item \emph{Degenerate.}  If \((\sigma,L)\) has no
  predictive witness content, then \(M_{\sigma}^{L}=Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) on the
  support of \(H_{\sigma}^{L}\), and the M-vs-Q distinction is vacuous.

  \item \emph{Strength-independence.}  Given the value of
  \(\operatorname{Exposure}(L,\sigma)\), the dissolution or preservation
  status of the loop-action asymmetry does not depend on the strength
  class \(\StrengthClass{k}\) of the coupling function used inside
  the lift's generation procedure.
\end{enumerate}

\label{lem:csl-core}
Let \(\Substrate\) be a computational substrate, let \(\Lift\) be an
autonomous lift on \(\Substrate\), and let \(\TraceFPLoopClass\) be
the trace-fingerprint loop class on \(\HistorySpace\).  Assume the six
structural premises (a)--(f) above.  Then the following four clauses
hold.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Dissolution.}  If \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\) holds
  and \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has predictive witness content, then for
  every loop \(\ell\in\TraceFPLoopClass\) and every history
  \(h\in\HistorySpace\),
  \[
    \Mclass{\ell.h}\neq\Mclass{h}
    \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
    \Qclass{\ell.h}\neq\Qclass{h}.
  \]
  Equivalently, the M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry fails: every
  M-class change is accompanied by a Q-class change.

  \item \emph{Preservation.}  If \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\) fails
  and \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has predictive witness content, then
  there exist a loop \(\ell\in\TraceFPLoopClass\) and a history
  \(h\in\HistorySpace\) such that
  \[
    \LoopActionQ{\ell}{h}=\Qclass{h}
    \qquad\text{and}\qquad
    \LoopActionM{\ell}{h}\neq\Mclass{h}.
  \]
  The M-vs-Q loop-action asymmetry holds.

  \item \emph{Degenerate.}  If \((\Substrate,\Lift)\) has no
  predictive witness content, then \(\Mquotient=\Qquotient\) on the
  support of \(\HistorySpace\), and the M-vs-Q distinction is vacuous.

  \item \emph{Strength-independence.}  Given the value of
  \(\Exposure(\Lift,\Substrate)\), the dissolution or preservation
  status of the loop-action asymmetry does not depend on the strength
  class \(\StrengthClass{k}\) of the coupling function used inside
  the lift's generation procedure.
\end{enumerate}

\label{prop:v-differential}
Within the typed substrate apparatus, the following four named
substrates admit autonomous lifts of the indicated exposure type.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{BSD substrate.}  The Birch--Swinnerton-Dyer substrate
  \citep{BirchSwinnertonDyer1965NotesII}, read here through
  elliptic-curve regulator content
  \citep{Silverman2009ArithmeticEllipticCurves}, admits autonomous
  lifts that are witness-content-exposing.

  \item \emph{NS substrate.}  The Navier--Stokes substrate
  \citep{Fefferman2006NavierStokesClay}, read here through
  weak-solution selection content \citep{Leray1934LiquideVisqueux},
  admits autonomous lifts that are witness-content-exposing.

  \item \emph{PvNP substrate.}  The \(P\)-versus-\(NP\) substrate
  \citep{Cook2000PNPClay}, read here through satisfying-assignment
  witness content for \(3\)-SAT \citep{Cook1971TheoremProving}, admits
  autonomous lifts that are trace-state-exposing but not
  witness-content-exposing under the polynomial-time current instrument.

  \item \emph{RH substrate.}  The Riemann-hypothesis substrate
  \citep{Bombieri2000RiemannClay}, read here through zeta-zero
  certificate content \citep{Conrey2003RiemannHypothesis}, admits
  autonomous lifts that are trace-state-exposing but not
  witness-content-exposing under the polynomial-time current instrument.
\end{enumerate}
In each case the lift's existence and its classification are
framework-internal facts about the substrate's adequacy-residual
machinery.  The classification records which exposure channel,
witness-content or trace-state, is available under the framework's
lawful instrument.

conclusion: The projection pi_ QP is not a bijection from Q_ sigma ^ L onto the standard class P . The obstruction has three parts. Histories versus languages. A Q_ sigma ^ L -class is a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance. A polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs. A single current class does not by itself define a language predicate over all input strings. Trace observables beyond decision output. The quotient Q_ sigma ^ L identifies histories by equality of all declared polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the decision bit. Two histories computing the same language may still be Q_ sigma ^ L -distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit bookkeeping observables differ. Machine multiplicity. Different polynomial-time machines may decide the same language while producing different Q_ sigma ^ L -observable histories on the same instance. These histories can map to different current classes but to the same language predicate.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:c1-not-bijective}
The projection \(\pi_{QP}\) is not a bijection from \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) onto
the standard class \(P\).  The obstruction has three parts.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Histories versus languages.}  A \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-class is
  a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance.  A
  polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs.  A
  single current class does not by itself define a language predicate
  over all input strings.

  \item \emph{Trace observables beyond decision output.}  The quotient
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\) identifies histories by equality of all declared
  polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the
  decision bit.  Two histories computing the same language may still be
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit
  bookkeeping observables differ.

  \item \emph{Machine multiplicity.}  Different polynomial-time
  machines may decide the same language while producing different
  \(Q_{\sigma}^{L}\)-observable histories on the same instance.  These
  histories can map to different current classes but to the same
  language predicate.
\end{enumerate}

source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:c1-not-bijective}
The projection \(\PiQP\) is not a bijection from \(\Qquotient\) onto
the standard class \(P\).  The obstruction has three parts.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Histories versus languages.}  A \(\Qquotient\)-class is
  a class of histories, possibly over a single bounded instance.  A
  polynomial-time decision predicate is a function on all inputs.  A
  single current class does not by itself define a language predicate
  over all input strings.

  \item \emph{Trace observables beyond decision output.}  The quotient
  \(\Qquotient\) identifies histories by equality of all declared
  polynomial-time current observables, not merely by equality of the
  decision bit.  Two histories computing the same language may still be
  \(\Qquotient\)-distinct because their trace, solver-prefix, or audit
  bookkeeping observables differ.

  \item \emph{Machine multiplicity.}  Different polynomial-time
  machines may decide the same language while producing different
  \(\Qquotient\)-observable histories on the same instance.  These
  histories can map to different current classes but to the same
  language predicate.
\end{enumerate}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The projection theorem gives the geometric meaning of the adequacy residual.
After rescaling by the square root of the audit energy, the native and
dissolving probes become ordinary linear maps in energy-scaled coordinates.  In
those coordinates, the residual is the dissolving readout after projecting away
the part already explained by the native probe range.  Positive
semidefiniteness of \(\Xi_C(D\mid L)\) follows directly from this formulation.

\begin{definition}[Energy-scaled probes and native-explanation projection]\label{def:xi:energy-scaled-probes}
The \emph{energy-scaled native and dissolving probes} are
\[
  T_L=L_0C_0^{-1/2},
  \qquad
  T_D=D_0C_0^{-1/2}.
\]
Here \(C_0^{1/2}\) is the unique positive square root of \(C_0\) on \(E_C\)
\citep{Higham2008Functions,Bhatia2007PositiveDefinite}.  The
\emph{native-explanation projection} \(P_L\) is the orthogonal projection in
\(E_C\) onto
\[
  \Ran(T_L^*)\subseteq E_C,
\]
the native probe range in the energy-scaled coordinate system.
\end{definition}
