In many applications the native data is not accepted all at once.  It is
assembled stage by stage: by refinement, enlargement, or passage to an
accepted stage.  At an accepted stage \(j\), we have a stage-local
instance of the framework from \Cref{sec:framework}: a carrier, an audit
energy \(C_j\), an exact package \(\Gamma_j\), a native probe family
\(L_j\) with its response space, and a routing map \(R_j\) into a common
response target.  The predictive currency at stage \(j\) is the
packaged native currency for these data, transported by \(R_j\).

Informally, the predictive currency is
\[
  \widehat K_j
  =R_jL_j\Gamma_j(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j)^\dagger
    \Gamma_j^*L_j^*R_j^*.
\]
The middle block
\[
  L_j\Gamma_j(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j)^\dagger\Gamma_j^*L_j^*
\]
is the stage-local instance of the packaged native currency
\(\K_{C_j,\Gamma_j}(L_j)\) from \Cref{sec:framework}; the outer
conjugation by \(R_j\) places that currency in the common response
space.  As before, this expression is variationally meaningful only
when \(L_j\Gamma_j\) is null-legal for the packaged audit
\(\Gamma_j^*C_j\Gamma_j\), which is the legal-quotient discipline of
\Cref{sec:framework} applied at stage \(j\).

source_wording_tex:
Each exactified carrier carries a carrier-side non-factorization certificate:
its native state space, transport law, and readout law do not factor through the
bridge-native \OldLayer{} description.  Equivalently, the carrier cannot be
reconstructed from old-layer data alone.  This is the carrier-level instance of
the foundations non-factorization condition for a strict extension
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}, applied to the exactified carrier structures
of \cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierExactification}.

The certificate is methodological.  It records why the \NewLayer{} carriers are
not reformulations of bridge-native data and supplies the structural
prerequisite for the final strict-extension verdict of \Cref{sec:final-gate}.
The descent-side statement that this non-factorization is preserved when
new-layer evidence is translated back to old-layer compatibility is separate
and is recorded in \Cref{subsec:non-factorization-preservation}.

conclusion: The readout slot gate consumes the source-backed threshold evidence of together with the PICA-bound source-policy contract fixed in . Its output is a strict-realization decision for the readout-agreement slot at the native H6 carrier level. This is a layer-local decision in the sense of the inherited slot-realization discipline : evidence attached to the new-layer carrier does not by itself upgrade the bridge-native H2 slot status, and the gate does not infer an active projection from threshold data without the intervening slot-realization check. Applied to the three carriers, the gate accepts strict realization of the readout-agreement slot on each carrier's native state space. The bridge-native H2 readout slot is unchanged by this acceptance and remains within the real-provisional non-factorization boundary. Strict realization of this one slot does not close the strict three-slot domain and does not license strict-test acceptance. The companion quadratic-witness and transition-witness slots are treated in , and the all-slot closure test is deferred to .

The all-slot gate consumes the three slot-realization results established in
\Cref{subsec:new-layer-readout-slot-gate,subsec:native-quadratic-witness-slot-construction,subsec:native-transition-witness-slot-construction}.
It returns closure of the H6 strict three-slot domain only when the
readout-agreement, quadratic-witness, and transition-witness slots are all
strict-realized on the same exactified carrier.  The gate therefore enforces
the status-family discipline of the foundations layer
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII}: realization at one slot does not imply
realization at another, and the conjunction is checked explicitly.  The
bridge-native H2 domain is not closed by this gate, which operates on
new-layer evidence under the layer-local attachment discipline fixed in
\Cref{subsec:threshold-attachment-requirements}.

On each of the three carriers, all three required slots are strict-realized on
the carrier's native state space.  The H6 strict three-slot domain is
therefore closed on each carrier.  This closes the slot-realization phase of
\Cref{sec:primary-results}; \Cref{subsec:native-strict-domain-table} records
the closed domain, and \Cref{subsec:strict-test-family-construction} begins the
separate test-family construction.  Domain closure is the structural
prerequisite for that construction, not a test-acceptance result.

conclusion: The admissibility gate applies the test-family discipline inherited from Paper 8 to the three candidates constructed in . It checks that each candidate is finite and that its predicates form an internally consistent partition of the closed H6 strict three-slot domain: mutual exclusivity prevents overlap between test alternatives, exhaustivity is evaluated against the closed domain of , readout-category coverage is evaluated against the readout-agreement slot on the carrier's native state space, and family structure checks that the predicates remain a single coherent test family rather than unrelated slotwise assertions. These checks remain within the finite-audited-interaction framework of . Each of the three constructed candidates satisfies the gate on its supporting carrier. Each meets the finiteness, mutual-exclusion, exhaustivity, readout-coverage, and family-structure requirements over its native strict three-slot domain. This gate passage is still not the acceptance declaration: the accepted strict test families are named only in .

This section records the schema-level support behind the gate logic of
Paper~9.  The formal layer consists of theorem schemas that codify the
discipline by which threshold attachment, slot realization, test-family
acceptance, descent compatibility, and the legality constraints of the final
gate are organized.  The schemas are inherited from the foundations layer
\cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsII} and follow the convention of Paper~8
\cite{Tsiokos2026CarrierToEvent}: formal support is a typed mirror of the gate
discipline, not an independent derivation of empirical content.

The schemas check legality and gate compatibility.  They do not prove that the
H6 carriers exist, that source-backed threshold evidence is present,
or that the controls pass; those empirical premises are supplied by the methods
and results sections \Cref{sec:methods,sec:primary-results,sec:secondary-results}.
The role of this section is conditional: if the empirical premises hold, then
the resulting claims obey the paper's internal discipline.  The schemas proceed
in order: source-policy admission required for threshold realization
(\Cref{subsec:schema-source-policy-threshold}), promotion versus carrier
exactification (\Cref{subsec:schema-promotion-not-exactification}),
exactified-carrier attachment licensing new-layer slots
(\Cref{subsec:schema-attachment-licenses-slot}), new-layer slots licensing
new-layer test-family reassembly (\Cref{subsec:schema-slots-license-tests}),
the real-provisional old layer blocking old-layer tests but not new-layer tests
(\Cref{subsec:schema-old-blocks-old-only}), unrealized required new-layer slots
blocking accepted new-layer strict tests
(\Cref{subsec:schema-unrealized-blocks-test}), and the boundary on what the
formal layer does not prove (\Cref{subsec:schema-legality-not-existence}).

conclusion: The final gate is an ordered case analysis over the upstream audits from . The principal positive case is reached when the native H6 strict domain closes, the strict test families on the new-layer carrier survive controls, and descent preserves old-layer compatibility without turning H2 into a strict-realized layer. Three weaker positive cases are reserved for incomplete new-layer evidence: a threshold-only case in which the new-layer readout slot is strict-realized but test-family reassembly is unavailable; a real-provisional case in which the route preserves or improves support without a completed threshold-and-slot gate; and a below-threshold or pending case. The same case analysis contains five blocking cases and two terminal negative cases. A blocker case obtains if promotion supplies no surviving object, if promotion survives but carrier exactification does not, if exactified threshold evidence cannot descend compatibly to the old layer, if source-policy admission blocks the source use, or if public-shadow safety blocks the route. A falsification case is legal only when neither old-layer nor new-layer threshold, readout, real-provisional, or below-threshold evidence remains. A separate implementation-failure case is reserved for malformed or unavailable artifacts, not for mathematical absence.

conclusion: The intrinsic promotion gate decides what kind of survivor the strengthening lane yields. The audited surviving candidate is intrinsic_naked_interface_witness_autonomous_protocol_lift , and its final promotion status is protocol_indexed_only. Two subordinate audits explain why the verdict stops there. The second-stage audit returns identity_only: only the identity proposal survives, and every nonidentity merge proposal collapses deterministic transport or witness retention, so the lane does not earn a deeper promoted object by merging away protocol distinctions. The signature-update audit returns indexed_signature_only, with the strongest blocking reason being that no overlap witness remains separated once coordinate tokens are stripped. The positive evidence disappears when protocol-coordinate indexing is removed.

The gate vocabulary used in \Cref{sec:final-gate-and-carrier-atlas} is best understood as
a controlled verdict ladder rather than as a single scalar score. At the law layer the
important statuses are \emph{lawful}, \emph{signature-only}, and \emph{collapse}. At the
compression layer the important statuses are \emph{faithful}, \emph{non-faithful}, and
\emph{not applicable}; the present paper uses only
\texttt{non\_faithful\_public\_compression} for the witness-to-public relation. At the
scope layer the main manuscript distinguishes \texttt{flagship\_only},
\texttt{cross\_seed}, \texttt{full\_core}, \texttt{support\_only}, and
\texttt{new\_surface\_candidate} rows.

The verdict layer is intentionally richer than ``carrier'' versus ``no carrier.'' Full
exactification, chart-only survival, descriptor/process-only survival, blocked lanes, and
protocol-indexed-only survival all belong to the same vocabulary. Ticket31 closes with the
verdict \texttt{protocol\_indexed\_carrier\_only}. That verdict should be read together
with the lawful witness row, the signature-only public shadow, the nearby-positive scope
limitations, and the scoped secondary flags. The gate vocabulary therefore preserves two
different kinds of positive statement at once: exactification at the refined witness level
and scoped survival at the lifted protocol-indexed level.

conclusion: Statements.lean and ProofKernel.lean together provide the theorem kernel referenced in Section 12. The kernel proves identity and composition for reductions, reflexive and transitive reducibility, and preservation lemmas for validity, readout, and transport under reduction. On top of that interface, it proves the main evidence-extraction lemmas from both full exactification evidence and protocol-indexed evidence. The theorem layer also encodes the gate's conservative implications. Full exactification evidence implies scoped positivity, transport closure and exactness, section honesty, protocol honesty, expansion honesty, cross-seed support, and non-reducibility. The theorem carrier_exactified_of_evidence packages this into the abstract exactification criterion. The protocol-indexed layer proves that protocol-indexed evidence yields a scoped positive carrier while still blocking any nonindexed promotion. Additional barrier lemmas show that fully exactified conclusions do not follow when cross-seed, section, or protocol barriers remain in force. Finally, CompressionContext supplies the abstract faithfulness implication used to formalize the witness/public-shadow split at theorem level.

conclusion: The prior carrier-exactification result is deliberately scoped: it is a carrier-exactification statement on the fixed Route A flagship support, not a public event package and not a public carrier theorem. Its lawful object is a refined same-branch witness; its public-side object is a coarse signature shadow. The relationship between the two is non-faithful: public signatures retain operational readout information but do not determine the refined law-bearing carrier data. In standard ontic/epistemic language , the public shadow is an epistemic image of the carrier; in Markov-chain language , the carrier-to-public map is lumpable only in a restricted sense. Throughout this paper we refer to these objects descriptively — the refined witness (lawful, carrier-side), the public signature shadow (coarse, readout-side), and the witness-to-shadow basis that relates them without supplying a faithful inverse. The corresponding machine-readable identifiers are listed once, in Appendix . Consequently the public shadow can supply public/readout-side predicates for later bridge records, but it cannot by itself supply lawful carrier structure or shared-event identity.

conclusion: The event-gate threshold construction attempt starts from the Theta component of the inherited event-bridge record. Methodologically, the intended criterion is conjunctive: one admissible event-level threshold statement is needed for each of the readout-agreement role, quadratic-witness role, and transition-witness role roles. Each role statement would have to bridge carrier-native strict-test data to an event-level threshold statement about the protocol-indexed comparisons carried by the record. The conjunction is well formed only if all three role statements are available. The required bridge is the per-role bridge-level law basis. The construction attempt does not succeed on the current H6 PICA artifacts. The role bases needed for the three threshold statements are not constructible from the present substrate, so the conjunctive threshold criterion cannot be assembled. This is the methods-level constructive non-definability finding: the missing ingredient is not unnamed or vague, but a named missing subobject with a specified role in the construction. The unbuilt component is separated from the strict-test-accepted H6 PICA substrate.

conclusion: The final-gate decision is an ordered case analysis over the series-canonical seven-outcome enumeration. The first case, event_package_accepted , would require accepted event-level records, an event-package candidate, and a promoted package. It is excluded by the rung decomposition in : the protocol-indexed event-level rung produces zero accepted event-level records, so no candidate or promoted package exists. The second case, lifted_package_accepted , would require a weakened lifted-package path on the paper-10-new substrate. It is also excluded, because the per-role bridge-level law basis obstruction is upstream of any full or lifted package shape. The third case, event_package_provisional , would require an admissible event-package candidate whose acceptance is qualified by stated provisos. Paper 10 has no such candidate: provisos can limit an otherwise constructed package, but they cannot replace the missing subobject isolated in . The fourth case, event_package_inapplicable , would apply if event-package construction were outside the paper's scope. That condition fails because the paper is explicitly organized around the strict-test-to-event-package attempt on fixed H6 PICA support.

The second case, \textsc{lifted\_package\_accepted}, would require a weakened lifted-package path on the paper-10-new substrate.  It is also excluded, because the per-role bridge-level law basis obstruction is upstream of any full or lifted package shape.

The Lean kernel contains 14 theorem schemas, summarized in the body at \Cref{subsec:theorem-schemas}.  This appendix records their Lean-side form without reproducing all fourteen declarations.  The schemas follow the inherited formal-kernel convention of the series: they state typed conditional structure, not empirical witness existence \citep{Tsiokos2026RecombinationWitnesses}.  The grouping below is therefore representative rather than exhaustive; the unlisted schemas fall into the same three families and differ only in the concrete gate or boundary object they protect.  The first thematic group is definitional.  A representative example is \texttt{strict\_refinement\_witness\_schema}, with input \(w : \texttt{StrictRefinementWitness}\) and output \( \texttt{StrictRefinementExists}\;w \leftrightarrow w.\texttt{coarserIdentifies} \wedge w.\texttt{finerDistinguishes}\). The Lean development for Paper~10 establishes schema legality and conditional proof structure; it does not establish empirical witness existence.  The empirical content of the paper is supplied by the artifact pipeline: \Cref{sec:methods} records the construction methods and gate attempts, \Cref{sec:primary-results} records the paper-10-new positive construction and constructive non-definability finding, and \Cref{sec:secondary-results} records the audit certificate and bookkeeping coverage.  Lean-level inhabitation, where present, shows that a typed implication or definition is formally well behaved.  It does not by itself show that the corresponding artifact record exists, that a threshold criterion is constructible from the current substrate, or that an event-package object has been produced.

This boundary is protected by the same anti-claim discipline stated methodologically in \Cref{subsec:no-shortcut-discipline} and structurally in \Cref{subsec:no-empirical-hardcoding-discipline}.  Empirical artifacts are not hardcoded as theorems; H2 transfer is not installed as an axiom; and Paper~10 positives are not obtained by silently upgrading Paper~9 results.  These flags make the formal appendix a companion to the manuscript rather than an alternative evidentiary source.  The appendix therefore closes with the same division used throughout the paper: Lean certifies schema form and proof boundaries, while empirical claims rest on audited artifacts and manuscript-level admissibility arguments.

Its role is interpretive: it identifies the abstract no-interference regime, proves that strict refinement obstructs that regime, and supplies one theorem-backed concrete positive instance for an aligned Lean model of the strongest promoted family. It is not a formalization of the full benchmark runtime. The supporting formal development is implemented in Lean . At the level of mathematical form, quotient descent, factorization through quotients, and state separation by observables are standard patterns; see, for example, . Under these assumptions, the Lean development proves the following backbone results.

source_wording_tex:
There is a concrete aligned finite model for the promoted family \(n5\_d1\_w1of4\_3of4\) with named assemblages \(B_L\) and \(B_R\) such that
\[
B_L \equiv^{\mathrm{bw}} B_R
\quad\text{but}\quad
B_L \not\equiv^{\mathrm{rec}} B_R.
\]
Equivalently, the aligned model admits a strict-refinement witness. By the preceding corollary, no global branchwise factorization layer can hold for that aligned model.

\claimref{FINDING.trap\_epsilon\_invariance}{671a28b4a4a9d812a1a6cb6e0083fc23ac01360c6ef5f6327b99de6560c153c2}
The declared trap weight family multiplies every trap's base weight by a common per-$\epsilon$
scalar. Since $\pi_k \propto 1/w_k$ depends only on weight \emph{ratios}, that scalar cancels
exactly: the trap stationary distribution is $\epsilon$-invariant (proved in exact Fraction
arithmetic; regression-tested). The declared temperature action therefore governs relaxation
\emph{rate} only, never the relaxation \emph{target}. This is known in substance in the trap-model
literature
\cite{bouchaud-1992,monthus-bouchaud-1996,diezemann-heuer-2011,bertin-bouchaud-drouffe-godreche-2003}:
the standard convention is a per-trap Arrhenius factor $w_k(T) \propto e^{-E_k/T}$, under which
different traps rescale by different temperature-dependent factors and the equilibrium genuinely
shifts --- exactly the mechanism used to produce Kovacs memory in trap models
\cite{diezemann-heuer-2011,bertin-bouchaud-drouffe-godreche-2003}. Our multiplicative-scalar
choice was made deliberately to keep every computation exactly rational; the invariance is its
elementary, proven consequence. It is filed here as a design caveat because it has a concrete
downstream cost, paid honestly in \S\ref{sec:gt7}: a Kovacs protocol cannot start the trap family
below its post-jump equilibrium, so the trap column of the transfer scoreboard is structurally
unobservable.

conclusion: FINDING.lean_collapse c70185334829fe8ad9f879a2288e90efe3d24700b8eeb5593f2de05341b62a51 Attempting to instantiate the numeric Kovacs witness in the core produced a theorem instead. For every instance of RouteTransportCore, the observe_push coherence field, combined with CurrentEventEquiv's universal quantification over events, forces current equivalence to imply future-predictive equivalence (current_implies_future_GENERIC); consequently non-vacuous PredictiveWitness, StrictRefinement, and LoopAsymmetry instances cannot be constructed in this core at all (predictiveWitness_impossible_GENERIC and its strict-refinement companion; machine-checked, sorry-free). The mechanism: the core's naturality axiom lets every future event be pulled back to a current event, so agreement on all current events silently includes agreement on all pulled-back futures. This is a genuine scope-boundary result about the formal core's expressiveness — strictly stronger than paper [A]'s own declared boundary — and it is structurally an instance of a known pattern rather than an isolated fact: it has the proof shape of Markov-chain strong lumpability (a local one-step coherence condition propagating an equivalence to all future times), and the collapse is exactly biextensional collapse in the Chu-space sense , with pullEvent playing the Chu transform's naturality condition. The instructive contrast is computational mechanics' causal-state framework , where current agreement generally does not imply future agreement: the collapse here is forced by this core's axiom, not a generic feature of prediction.

\label{thm:predictive-transport}
For every admissible continuation $\gamma\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to j}$, pushing representatives along $\gamma$ descends to a well-defined predictive transport
\[
T^{M}_{\gamma} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_j.
\]
It also descends to a mixed map
\[
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma} :
\PredictiveQ_i \to \CurrentQ_j,
\qquad
[h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}\longmapsto
[\operatorname{push}_{\gamma}h]_{\CurrentEquiv_j},
\]
and these maps form the commutation triangle
\[
\pi_j \circ T^{M}_{\gamma}
=
\widehat T^{M\toQ}_{\gamma}.
\]
For a fixed source interface $i$, current-event equivalence is stable under every outgoing push if and only if $i$ is flat:
\[
\bigl(h\CurrentEquiv_i h'\Longrightarrow h\FutureEquiv_i h'\bigr)
\quad\text{for all }h,h'\in\Histories_i.
\]
Thus current-quotient transport induced by representative push along every outgoing continuation is available exactly in the flat case, not as part of an arbitrary route transport package.

\label{thm:reachable-factorization}
Let $s : \Histories_i \to S$ be any future-sufficient state abstraction at interface $i$. Then on the reachable image
\[
\operatorname{Reach}(s) := \{\,s(h) : h\in\Histories_i\,\},
\]
there exists a factor map
\[
f : \operatorname{Reach}(s) \to \PredictiveQ_i
\]
such that
\[
f(s(h)) = [h]_{\FutureEquiv_i}
\qquad
\text{for all } h\in\Histories_i.
\]
Moreover, this factorization is unique on the reachable image: if two maps from $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$ to $\PredictiveQ_i$ agree with the predictive quotient on all histories, then they agree everywhere on $\operatorname{Reach}(s)$.

\label{thm:loop-asymmetry}
Let $\ell\in\mathcal{C}_{i\to i}$ be a loop at interface $i$. Then $\ell$ induces the predictive endomorphism
\[
L^{M}_{\ell} : \PredictiveQ_i \to \PredictiveQ_i.
\]
Suppose current triviality holds at representative level,
\[
\operatorname{push}_{\ell}h \CurrentEquiv_i h
\qquad\text{for every }h\in\Histories_i,
\]
while $L^{M}_{\ell}$ is nontrivial. Then there exists a predictive class $q\in\PredictiveQ_i$ such that
\[
L^{M}_{\ell}(q)\neq q
\qquad\text{but}\qquad
\pi_i\bigl(L^{M}_{\ell}(q)\bigr)=\pi_i(q).
\]

Assume:
(i) \(S\) is reversible with respect to a stationary distribution \(s\) on \(\Phi\); and
(ii) each \(K_\phi\) is reversible with respect to a \emph{common} stationary distribution \(\pi\) on \(X\).
Then the product measure \(\mu(x,\phi):=\pi(x)s(\phi)\) is stationary for \(P\), and \(P\) is reversible with respect to \(\mu\).
Indeed, write \(P=\alpha P_{\mathrm{phase}}+(1-\alpha)P_{\mathrm{state}}\), where
\(P_{\mathrm{phase}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{x'=x}S(\phi,\phi')\) and
\(P_{\mathrm{state}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{\phi'=\phi}K_\phi(x,x')\).
For \(\mu(x,\phi)=\pi(x)s(\phi)\), detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{phase}}\) reduces (on the support \(x=x'\)) to \(s(\phi)S(\phi,\phi')=s(\phi')S(\phi',\phi)\), and detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{state}}\) reduces (on the support \(\phi=\phi'\)) to \(\pi(x)K_\phi(x,x')=\pi(x')K_\phi(x',x)\). Since both components satisfy detailed balance with respect to \(\mu\), their convex combination \(P\) does as well.
The assumption of a common stationary \(\pi\) is essential: if the conditional kernels had different equilibria, state updates could contribute nonzero entropy production even with a reversible clock.
Consequently,
\[
\mathrm{EPR}(P,\mu)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Sigma_T(\mu)=0\ \ \text{for all }T\ge 1.
\]

(i) \(S\) is reversible with respect to a stationary distribution \(s\) on \(\Phi\); and
(ii) each \(K_\phi\) is reversible with respect to a \emph{common} stationary distribution \(\pi\) on \(X\).
Then the product measure \(\mu(x,\phi):=\pi(x)s(\phi)\) is stationary for \(P\), and \(P\) is reversible with respect to \(\mu\).
Indeed, write \(P=\alpha P_{\mathrm{phase}}+(1-\alpha)P_{\mathrm{state}}\), where
\(P_{\mathrm{phase}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{x'=x}S(\phi,\phi')\) and
\(P_{\mathrm{state}}((x,\phi),(x',\phi'))=\mathbf{1}_{\phi'=\phi}K_\phi(x,x')\).
For \(\mu(x,\phi)=\pi(x)s(\phi)\), detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{phase}}\) reduces (on the support \(x=x'\)) to \(s(\phi)S(\phi,\phi')=s(\phi')S(\phi',\phi)\), and detailed balance for \(P_{\mathrm{state}}\) reduces (on the support \(\phi=\phi'\)) to \(\pi(x)K_\phi(x,x')=\pi(x')K_\phi(x',x)\). Since both components satisfy detailed balance with respect to \(\mu\), their convex combination \(P\) does as well.
The assumption of a common stationary \(\pi\) is essential: if the conditional kernels had different equilibria, state updates could contribute nonzero entropy production even with a reversible clock.
Consequently,
\[
\mathrm{EPR}(P,\mu)=0
\qquad\text{and}\qquad
\Sigma_T(\mu)=0\ \ \text{for all }T\ge 1.
\]

Let \(P\) be the lifted kernel~\eqref{eq:lifted_kernel} on \(Z=X\times\Phi\), and suppose each \(K_\phi\) is reversible with respect to a common stationary \(\pi\) on \(X\) while \(S\) has stationary distribution \(s\) on \(\Phi\).
Then the entropy production of the lifted chain decomposes as
\[
\mathrm{EPR}(P,\pi\times s)
=
\alpha\,\mathrm{EPR}(S,s)
+
(1-\alpha)\sum_{\phi\in\Phi} s(\phi)\,\mathrm{EPR}(K_\phi,\pi).
\]
This follows by splitting the edge-sum in \eqref{eq:epr} into disjoint transitions that change only \(\phi\) (phase updates) versus only \(x\) (state updates), which do not overlap in~\eqref{eq:lifted_kernel}.
In our construction \(\mathrm{EPR}(K_\phi,\pi)=0\) for all \(\phi\), so the arrow audit is entirely attributable to clock drive:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:epr_clock_only}
\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{lifted}}=\alpha\,\mathrm{EPR}_{\mathrm{clock}}.
\end{equation}
This gives a precise sense in which protocol holonomy alone is not an arrow-of-time certificate: without clock drive (or external scheduling), the audit vanishes.

For every context \(c\in\mathcal{C}\), the event algebra

This section states the main result: the duality-confinement
membrane theorem, also called the master theorem.  It takes the
apparatus built in the preceding sections and turns a sequence of
domination records into fixed-locus confinement.  The input is
algebraic and trace-theoretic---\(A_{X}\) is dominated by positive
bounds \(B_n\) whose traces tend to zero---and the output is
geometric: visible mass is confined to \(\Fix(J)\).  In framework
terms, this is the apparatus theorem for the SDTC structural law
\(\Gamma_{\mathrm{SDTC}}\): it does not derive the recognition source, only the
mathematical consequence once the source has supplied the required
sequence.

\begin{theorem}[Duality-confinement membrane theorem\protect\footnote{Verified in the Lean formalization at the typed positive-cone level; see App~\ref{app:formalization}.}]
\label{thm:duality_confinement:master-theorem}
Let \(\hat{\mathfrak{X}}\) be an involutive object ledger with carrier \(X\),
involution \(J\), measure \(\mu\), anti-invariant readout
\(\psi_{-}\), and anti-invariant ledger \(A_{X}\).  Assume that
\(\psi_{-}\) is qualitatively separating.  Suppose there is a sequence
of positive cone elements \(B_n\) such that
\[
  A_{X}\preceq B_n
  \qquad (n=1,2,\ldots)
\]
and
\[
  \trace B_n\to0
  \qquad (n\to\infty).
\]
Then \(A_{X}=0\) in the typed positive cone.  Consequently,
\[
  \mu\bigl(X\setminus\Fix(J)\bigr)=0.
\]
\end{theorem}

membrane theorem, also called the master theorem.  It takes the
apparatus built in the preceding sections and turns a sequence of
domination records into fixed-locus confinement.  The input is
algebraic and trace-theoretic---\(\AX\) is dominated by positive
bounds \(B_n\) whose traces tend to zero---and the output is
geometric: visible mass is confined to \(\Fix(J)\).  In framework
terms, this is the apparatus theorem for the SDTC structural law
\(\GamSDTC\): it does not derive the recognition source, only the
mathematical consequence once the source has supplied the required

\begin{theorem}[Duality-confinement membrane theorem\protect\footnote{Verified in the Lean formalization at the typed positive-cone level; see App~\ref{app:formalization}.}]
\label{thm:duality_confinement:master-theorem}
Let \(\IOL\) be an involutive object ledger with carrier \(X\),
involution \(J\), measure \(\mu\), anti-invariant readout
\(\psim\), and anti-invariant ledger \(\AX\).  Assume that
\(\psim\) is qualitatively separating.  Suppose there is a sequence
of positive cone elements \(B_n\) such that
\[
  \AX\preceq B_n
  \qquad (n=1,2,\ldots)
\]
and
\[
  \trace B_n\to0

trace budget tends to zero.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The main result of this paper is not a final exponent-level universality classification. It is a primitive taxonomy and observable separation of layer-birth classes. Within the Six-Birds framework, the experimentally accessible low-complexity births are organized by activation of $P5$, $P6_{\mathrm{drive}}$, and $P4$, and the four corresponding canonical classes can be instantiated and separated in a common measured observable space. That is the level at which the evidence is now strongest, and it is the level at which the paper should be read.

The most mature part of that result is the Class-I / Class-II contrast. Both classes exhibit structural birth, but only Class-II carries a robust directed-circulation signal at structural birth. The empirical separation is therefore not merely taxonomic by declaration. It is enforced by a validated observable channel: affinity. The no-fake-arrow controls make that point especially important. Reversible controls do not get spuriously promoted into the driven class, while hidden-schedule protocol-trap constructions do produce the expected driven-positive signal under naive handling. This is precisely the kind of evidential discipline that a primitive taxonomy needs if it is to be more than nomenclature.

conclusion: treats holonomy as a constrained non-axis rather than a missing success
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Several of the project's most useful outcomes are negative in form. They do not undermine the paper's main claims; they define their scope. This appendix records the most important of those constraints so that the main text does not have to carry them in full detail.

The first is the holonomy result. The project tested whether route mismatch could function as a clean crossover field and found that it could not. The initial construction produced affinity contamination, and the refined construction eliminated the contamination without producing a meaningful boundary-shift effect. This should not be read as an unsuccessful side experiment. It is an empirical confirmation of a structural point already built into the primitive framework: $P3$ is diagnostically important, but it is not a directionality certificate on its own. Whenever the route-mismatch channel appeared to generate a class-relevant effect, it did so by coupling into the drive channel rather than by standing independently. The paper therefore treats holonomy as a constrained non-axis rather than a missing success.

conclusion: The continuous substrate evolves by the full six-mechanism update law x↦ F(x), x∈ S_ aud . This trajectory is the source of the mathematical structures we study, but it is not itself the theorem object. A theorem stated directly about raw trajectories would be too tied to the simulation-level presentation and would not distinguish between: the cocycle-level object visible through the base theory, the packaged fixed-point structure visible only after completion, and the extension relation between those two levels. What the paper needs is an object that remembers both the closed thermodynamic structure already present at the cocycle level and the new packaged strata created by completion.

conclusion: the cocycle-pressure object of the base theory T_0 is closed on the audited shell
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:cocycle-pressure}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class from Section~\ref{sec:lawfulness}, and let \(a_n(s;x)\) be the selector-weighted operator growth observable associated with the base cocycle theory \(T_0\). Define
\[
\Phi_n(s):=\sup_{x\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}} a_n(s;x).
\]
Assume the shell-stable hypotheses of the lawfulness theoremlet, together with the shell-uniform cocycle bounds and bounded-error comparison estimates required by the Fekete-sup route. Then the following hold on the audited shell.

\begin{enumerate}
    \item The pressure object
    \[
    P_{T_0}(s)=\lim_{n\to\infty}\frac{1}{n}\log \Phi_n(s)
    \]
    exists on the relevant parameter window.
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) is finite and nondegenerate on that window.
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) is monotone in \(s\).
    \item \(P_{T_0}(s)\) has enough regularity to support a later root-based thermodynamic theorem.
\end{enumerate}

Therefore the cocycle-pressure object of the base theory \(T_0\) is closed on the audited shell.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:strict-extension}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class, let
\[
\pi_0:\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\to \mathcal{O}_0
\]
be the cocycle-level object map of the base theory \(T_0\), and let
\[
\pi_1:\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\to \mathcal{O}_1
\]
be the packaged-object map defined by the completion theory \(T_1\). Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item the cocycle-pressure theory \(T_0\) is closed on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the completion endomap is well-defined on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item saturation of the completion dynamics occurs on the audited shell,
    \item material \(P4\leftarrow P5\) forcing produces new packaged strata after saturation,
    \item and the cocycle-level theory exhibits macro-admissibility obstruction on the packaged future.
\end{enumerate}
Then \(T_1\) is a strict theory extension of \(T_0\) on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\). Equivalently, there is no factorization
\[
\pi_1=\phi\circ \pi_0
\qquad \text{on } \mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}
\]
for any map \(\phi:\mathcal{O}_0\to\mathcal{O}_1\).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:conditional-disintegration}
Let \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\) be the audited shell-stable class, let \(P_{T_0}(s)\) be the closed cocycle pressure object of the base theory \(T_0\), and let \(\mathcal{F}(x)\) be the persistent packaged strata of the extended theory \(T_1\) with weights \(w_{\Sigma}(x)\). Define
\[
\Delta_{T_0\to T_1}(s)
:=
P_{T_0}(s)
-
\sum_{\Sigma\in\mathcal{F}(x)} w_{\Sigma}(x)\,P_{\Sigma}(s).
\]
Assume:
\begin{enumerate}
    \item the cocycle pressure object of \(T_0\) is closed on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the packaged-object theory \(T_1\) is well-defined on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item the strict theory-extension theoremlet holds on \(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{aud}}\),
    \item and the package-conditioned pressure profiles are well-defined on the audited shell.
\end{enumerate}
Then the weighted package-conditioned pressure gap is nontrivial on the audited shell. Equivalently, the cocycle-level pressure is not sufficient for the packaged future, and the thermodynamic consequence of the extension is a nontrivial conditional pressure disintegration.

conclusion: shows exactly where it aligns with those quantities and where it does not. The result is a more informative scientific object than either a closure-only ranking or an EI-only ranking
expanded_source_wording_tex:
The most direct packaging-space support for the paper's comparison thesis is the EI slice itself. Figure~\ref{fig:packaging_ei_slice} plots EI against closure while encoding objecthood and budget. What it shows is exactly the relationship the atlas view predicts: EI is informative but not dispositive. Some of the highest-EI packagings are trivial as macro-objects; some of the most scientifically useful packagings have only moderate EI but much better closure or objecthood properties. The right interpretation is not that EI is wrong. It is that EI is one coordinate projection of packaging quality.

That point matters because it lets the paper treat causal-emergence-style quantities constructively rather than polemically \cite{hoel2013causal,hoel2017map,rosas2020reconciling}. The atlas does not dismiss effective information. It computes it, places it on the same packaging-space rows as closure, objecthood, novelty, directionality retention, and budget, and then shows exactly where it aligns with those quantities and where it does not. The result is a more informative scientific object than either a closure-only ranking or an EI-only ranking.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
Realizability alone does not turn a language into a machine: we also want a notion of normal form and mutual simulation.
The appropriate equivalence notion is \emph{packaging equivalence} induced by idempotent(-like) endomaps (\Cref{def:packeq}).
The Lean appendix mechanizes the corresponding algebra: idempotent splitting (fixed points, inclusion/retraction), packaging equivalence as an equivalence relation, and lens saturation as a closure operator (\Cref{app:lean}).

\begin{theorem}[Compilation to $\mathcal S_{\min}$ up to packaging equivalence]
\label{thm:normal-form}
Let $\mathcal S$ be a substrate that realizes P1--P6 without smuggling in the sense of \Cref{def:no-smuggling}.
Assume further that the realized operators are finitary (state and registers can be encoded in a finite carrier) and autonomous once all protocol state is represented.
Then there exists a substrate $\mathcal M\in\mathcal S_{\min}$ and an encoding of $\mathcal S$ into $\mathcal M$ such that:
\begin{enumerate}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item the lens/refinement structure of $\mathcal S$ is simulated by deterministic lenses on $\mathcal M$,
  \item packaging in $\mathcal S$ is simulated by internal packaging endomaps on $\mathcal M$ up to packaging equivalence, and
  \item admissible audits in $\mathcal S$ are represented by intrinsic audits on $\mathcal M$ (in particular, directionality audits respect monotonicity under coarse-graining).
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, if two compilations choose the same canonical prototype-selection scheme for each lens (e.g.\ uniform-on-fiber) and the same auditing conventions, then they are mutually simulable up to packaging equivalence via packaging-respecting maps in the sense of \Cref{def:pack-morphism}.
\end{theorem}

hypotheses.text: The following substrate features are necessary (up to equivalent internal encodings) to realize the corresponding primitives without smuggling: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.35em] Autonomy requires phase-in-state (P3). If a substrate permits staged protocols but does not represent protocol state internally, then stroboscopic composition can produce apparent arrows of time that vanish once the dynamics is made autonomous by lifting state. Therefore, any autonomous semantics for protocols must encode phase-in-state (or an equivalent internal mechanism). Genuine arrows require internal drive (P6 drive ). Autonomy plus staging does not imply directionality. In an autonomous lifted model with reversible internal phase dynamics, protocol-induced arrows can disappear ( Sigma_T 0 ). To obtain a genuine arrow in an autonomous substrate, one needs internal drive detectable by a nonzero affinity class (ACC cycle integrals). Audits must be monotone under coarse-graining (P6). There exist processes with real micro irreversibility but macro observations whose path law is reversal-invariant ( Sigma_T^ macro =0 ). Any audit that reports increased directionality after coarse-graining violates limited-access semantics and is therefore smuggled. Packaging must be an internal (approximate) idempotent endomap (P5). Without an internal endomap e (or closure operator) that induces packaging equivalence x _e y iff e(x)=e(y) , there is no internal notion of ``same packaged object'' and no internal fixed-point criterion for stability. Declaring macrostates by fiat is smuggling. Route mismatch is distinct from directionality (P3 vs.\ P6). Packaging along different refinement routes can yield a measurable holonomy defect (route mismatch), even when directionality audits obey data processing

conclusion: We begin with the controlled finite-state benchmark in which the exact object CD_tau(Pi) is available by construction. The benchmark consists of four families: exactly lumpable chains , perturbed-lumpable chains with heterogeneity parameter alpha ∈ \ 0,0.2,0.5\ , metastable block chains with escape parameter p_ out ∈ \ 0.02,0.08,0.20\ , and hidden-type chains with within-fiber type strength in \ 0.1,0.5,0.9\ . Across these 17 staged conditions we compute the exact closure deficit, the intrinsic term, the decomposition residual, and both uniform- and stationary-lift route mismatch. The benchmark behaves exactly as predicts on the closed cases. The exactly lumpable constructions collapse to machine zero at both staging depths: at tau=1 , for example, the benchmark gives CD_1(Pi)=4.34× 10^ -17 and RM^ uniform _1(Pi)=5.29× 10^ -17 . The decomposition identity is numerically stable throughout the sweep, with maximum absolute residual 2.87× 10^ -16 over all rows. In this sense the benchmark serves as a calibration device: the exact object vanishes when it should vanish, and the numerical implementation does not introduce visible leakage.

The decomposition identity is numerically stable throughout the sweep, with maximum absolute residual $2.87\times 10^{-16}$ over all rows. In this sense the benchmark serves as a calibration device: the exact object vanishes when it should vanish, and the numerical implementation does not introduce visible leakage.

conclusion: The controlled Markov benchmark established what unresolved closure is. The complementary question is what it costs to buy the missing distinctions back once the current package has already failed to stabilize them. To expose that accounting side directly, we fix the strongest hidden-type benchmark and measure the budgeted randomness curve Rand_B empirically using packaged predictors of increasing memory order. The empirical curve is reported in the feasible-class sense of : at budget B=L , we plot the best held-out log loss available among predictors of order at most L . This matters because sparse higher-order contexts can make the raw loss of a particular order- L fit fluctuate upward in finite data, whereas the feasible-class quantity itself should never worsen when the admissible predictor class strictly expands.

Hashing provides an engineered version of the same logic in a deterministic many-to-one map. A truncated digest $H_n : \{0,1\}^m \to \{0,1\}^n$ does not create new entropy; it packages a large input space into a short stable record and leaves preimage identification to whatever budget the observer can afford \citep{rogaway2004cryptographichashfunctionbasics}. We therefore examine three input regimes on small safe truncations: a uniform high-entropy source, a low-entropy synthetic dictionary of size $256$, and a fifty-fifty medium mixture of dictionary and out-of-dictionary inputs.

In the uniform regime, the familiar one-wayness heuristic appears exactly where it should: in the small-success region $q/2^n \le 0.25$, empirical inversion success tracks the line $q/2^n$ with mean absolute deviation $3.70\times 10^{-3}$. \Cref{fig:hashing-inversion} plots empirical success against $q/2^n$ directly. For example, at $n=16$ and budget $q=256$, the empirical success rate is $6.67\times 10^{-3}$ against the simple baseline $256/2^{16}=3.91\times 10^{-3}$. In this regime, the digest is effectively random-looking relative to the bounded inversion budget, even though the map is fully deterministic.

In the uniform regime, the familiar one-wayness heuristic appears exactly where it should: in the small-success region $q/2^n \le 0.25$, empirical inversion success tracks the line $q/2^n$ with mean absolute deviation $3.70\times 10^{-3}$. \Cref{fig:hashing-inversion} plots empirical success against $q/2^n$ directly. For example, at $n=16$ and budget $q=256$, the empirical success rate is $6.67\times 10^{-3}$ against the simple baseline $256/2^{16}=3.91\times 10^{-3}$. In this regime, the digest is effectively random-looking relative to the bounded inversion budget, even though the map is fully deterministic.

This appendix records the representation-learning result that we treat as auxiliary rather than core evidence \citep{tishby1999bottleneck,geiger2015optimalkullbackleibleraggregation}. The experiment asks whether increasing representational budget, measured by the number of learned clusters $k$, automatically reduces predictive non-closure when packaging is learned from observations rather than supplied by construction. It does not.

We generate observation sequences from the hidden-type process used earlier and learn $k$-means partitions on those observations for $k \in \{2,4,8\}$ \citep{macqueen1967somemethods}. For each learned packaging we then evaluate the resulting packaged sequence by held-out first- and second-order predictive log loss and by the empirical conditional mutual information
\[
\widehat I(X_t;Y_{t+1}\mid Y_t),
\]
computed from the joint sequence of hidden microstates and learned packaged labels. In this appendix we report the \emph{raw} empirical conditional mutual information, not the normalized version used only for diagnostics during development.

conclusion: Formal theories of consciousness are difficult to compare, and difficult to trust, partly because three different kinds of claim routinely travel in one sentence: mathematical claims about a formal structure, empirical claims about how that structure meets observation, and ontological claims about what the structure's satisfaction would be. The field has begun to treat this as a foundational problem rather than a stylistic one. General frameworks for mathematical models of consciousness ask what a model must declare before it says anything ; formal work on testability shows that inference procedures and prediction data can interact so badly that a theory becomes unfalsifiable or trivially falsified ; and large adversarial collaborations have demonstrated how much machinery is needed to test even two well-resourced theories against each other, without producing a definitive verdict . Landscape reviews count theory families by the dozen . In such a field, a paper's first obligation is to say exactly what kind of claim each of its sentences makes. This paper takes that obligation as its organizing principle. It presents an architecture for consciousness built from standard finite mathematics: finite carriers, lenses, quotients, refinements, closure operators, viability kernels, and audited promotion between description layers. Around that architecture it assembles a catalog of exact finite results, a small set of machine-checked kernels, and one explicitly priced ontological bridge. Every scientific sentence in the paper is assigned to one of four claim lanes, defined in Section : structural results [S] (theorems and exact finite constructions), recognition bridges [R] (proposed interpretive mappings, never derivations), ontological implications [O] (conditional on named postulates), and open targets [OPEN] . The lane discipline is not decoration; it is enforced by a sentence-level claim ledger in the artifact, and the paper's central negative rule is that no amount of [S] material ever implies an [O] conclusion without the named purchases.

\begin{theorem}[Exact forcing and minimal restoration; T1]
\label{thm:t1}
\textsf{[S]} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade on the exact T1-L1 carrier; conditional
family schema beyond it. \emph{Scope:} the declared twelve-state deadline
carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Public exhaustion.} Every $q$-measurable feedback policy has an
empty deadline viability kernel: $K_{\mathrm{viab}}(q) = \emptyset$, by exhaustive
enumeration of all public-lens policies.
\item \textbf{Predictive restoration.} The five-class continuation-law
abstraction $L$ restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive
quotient $M = q \times L$ restores exactly the same ten states:
$K_{\mathrm{viab}}(L) = K_{\mathrm{viab}}(M)$, $|K_{\mathrm{viab}}(M)| = 10$, certified by a separate
nine-class search and a refinement audit.
\item \textbf{Unique minimal repair.} Among all $64$ refinements of the
public lens, the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement is the
seven-class quotient $\Pi_*$ that splits exactly the public fiber $p=1$;
every closure-restoring refinement splits that fiber, and the maximal
refinement that leaves $p=1$ unsplit has empty kernel.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Assumptions:} deadline active; live, resettable, non-publicly-definable
phase. \emph{Nonclaim:} this does not show that all bounded self-predicting
systems must form selves, and it is not an empirical result about any actual
system.
\end{theorem}

Here $p=1$ is a public \emph{position coordinate} value naming the fiber the
minimal refinement splits; it is not a probability, and not a refinement
parameter.

\gradeS{} \emph{Grade:} theorem-grade on the exact T1-L1 carrier; conditional
family schema beyond it. \emph{Scope:} the declared twelve-state deadline
carrier, its action family, and its lens. On this carrier:
\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{Public exhaustion.} Every $q$-measurable feedback policy has an
empty deadline viability kernel: $\Kviab(q) = \emptyset$, by exhaustive
enumeration of all public-lens policies.
\item \textbf{Predictive restoration.} The five-class continuation-law
abstraction $L$ restores a ten-state kernel, and the canonical predictive
quotient $M = q \times L$ restores exactly the same ten states:
$\Kviab(L) = \Kviab(M)$, $|\Kviab(M)| = 10$, certified by a separate
nine-class search and a refinement audit.
\item \textbf{Unique minimal repair.} Among all $64$ refinements of the
public lens, the unique minimal closure-restoring refinement is the
seven-class quotient $\Pi_*$ that splits exactly the public fiber $p=1$;
every closure-restoring refinement splits that fiber, and the maximal
refinement that leaves $p=1$ unsplit has empty kernel.
\end{enumerate}
\emph{Assumptions:} deadline active; live, resettable, non-publicly-definable
phase. \emph{Nonclaim:} this does not show that all bounded self-predicting
systems must form selves, and it is not an empirical result about any actual
system.

declared deterministic support, bounded observer budgets, declared generator
provenance. \emph{Nonclaim:} no ontic indeterminacy, no metaphysical
freedom, no disproof of every libertarian view.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Lawfulness} (framing). Choices are readouts of the run; no
spontaneity primitive is added.
\item \emph{External underivability} (theorem-grade toy instantiation). A
bounded public observer at budget $B$ can face positive priced residue:
same-summary states with different deterministic choices. The exact scores at
budgets $0,1,2$ are $1, 1, 1/2$, non-increasing, with a split witness at every

self-model is a bounded packaging; a complete same-level self-audit
classifies \texttt{undefined\_circular} (an out-of-scope variant:
\texttt{outside\_scope}), and the self-model summary has its own
same-summary/different-choice split pair.
\item \emph{Authorship} (direct instantiation of no-fake-arrow audits).
Directionality is credited to the agent only when it survives the
protocol-trap and data-processing nulls and one common credit rule returns
\emph{self}: genuine autonomous drive has unequal exact self-channel cycle
products $8/27$ versus $1/27$; the externally scheduled apparent arrow has
unequal \emph{other}-channel products ($0$ versus $16/81$), a real arrow
credited to other rather than to self; and after schedule internalization the lifted kernel decomposes
exactly into clock and content channels, both balanced ($0$ versus $0$ on
credited products; canonical lifted cycle $1/324$ each way), so the same rule
returns \emph{none}. Deterministic coarsening of the blocked case leaves
equal path fluxes ($1/27$ each way): observation does not create affinity.
\item \emph{Libertarianism foreclosed} (foreclosure argument). The positive
residue of clauses 2--3 is bounded-observer ignorance under declared
packaging and budget, not substrate spontaneity.
\item \emph{Deflation foreclosed} \textsf{[O]}-flavored. ``Only a lower-layer
event'' commits the factorization error: once the layer is strict, the layer
claim cannot be replaced by a base-layer paraphrase without losing the
certificate, as T3 establishes. This is a foreclosure argument with an
ontological flavor, not a Tier~S theorem.
\end{enumerate}

The experienced-present proxy is the package's stabilized (order, tick, arrow) triple, with width the closure timescale tau . The single mechanism advance = b/(b+1) at budget b=2 gives exact progress 2/3 and tick rate 2/9 ; the funded nine-step trace has six advances, two completed wraps, and a monotone ledger with Delta A = 2 > 0 ; the unfunded control ( b=0 ) stalls exactly ( 0 progress, 0 ticks, constant trace, no arrow). No single global ``now'' is guaranteed across sub-closures: the noncommuting protocol pair (rotation, swap) has holonomy defect 1 and the commuting control ( R , R^2 ) defect 0 , so path-dependent local time translations admit no global potential. Nonclaim: no universal specious-present width, no physical time or spacetime, and holonomy is never a directionality certificate.

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade finite duality core. Scope: one exact rational linear program over a three-action policy simplex with two maintenance budgets. At binding budgets b=(2,2) : optimum value 76/11 , both constraints tight, exact local duals lambda = (24/11, 14/11) . Slack regime at b=(5,1) : lambda_1 = 0 exactly. Tightening the first budget across (4,3,2,3/2) recomputes lambda_1 = (0, 4/3, 24/11, 24/11) , non-decreasing. Proxy discipline: a declared row-permuted proxy cost yields unstable recovered proxy prices across two environment phases ( 4 and 0 ), while the true LP is phase-independent by construction; a planted dual certificate with positive price on a slack constraint violates complementary slackness and is rejected. Viability tie: the kernel is nonempty when both budgets meet their thresholds and empty when either is underfunded by 1/11 . Nonclaim: shadow-price duality is standard mathematics, and none of these values generalizes to actual subjects.

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade induced-kernel construction and exact audit; the geometry-birth grade is audit-only. Scope: the corrected 32-state micro-carrier (eight hues, two chroma, two texture levels), packaging lens forgetting texture, staged twice. The lens descends the symmetric micro kernel to a 16-point macro kernel P = U P^2 C with exact lift consistency UC = I ; texture is deliberately macro-relevant (a sluggish grain multiplies move rates by 1/2 ), so prototype content is operational, not decorative. The exact max-product path similarity gives warm-neighbor similarity 43/270 versus cool-target 1/810 , so the warm neighbor is strictly nearer; d = - D is the additive distance on positive support. Audits, all exact: closure defect 13441/52488 (the swapped-prototype incoherent control: 2619989/3499200 , strictly larger); prototype stability maximum 2/3 , mean 13801/25920 ; all 256 ordered pairs connected; all 16^3 multiplicative triangle checks pass; route mismatch 0 . A texture-0 point-prototype lift preserves UC=I yet changes the induced object and is rejected: lift consistency alone does not certify prototype content. A local signature table is chroma-favored at hues 0,3,7 , balanced at 1,5,6 , hue-favored at 2,4 ; a hand-declared signature-change transport has loop residue 0 on the balanced plateau and 1 at the warm/cool boundary, with multiplicative residual ratios 180/169 (plateau) and 102/59 (boundary), both above one and strictly ordered. Nonclaim: no smallness threshold adjudicates the audits (only the computed controls do); the full geometry-birth checklist (fitted inter-scale distortion, dimension diagnostics, and curvature via neighborhood-MDS/Procrustes transport) is not implemented; geometry is layer-relative; and the recovered similarity is descended structure, never the hidden experience.

conclusion: [S] Grade: theorem-grade exact finite construction; the broader quality-space rigidification principle is schema-grade. Scope: an eight-state fiber bundle, |Q| = 4 public classes with two fiber points each, declared descents. Define the descent-fixing gauge group G = \ sigma ∈ Aut(M) : pisigma = pi and dsigma = d for every admissible descent d\ . Spectrum inversion is a lawful distinct possibility exactly to the extent that G is nontrivial. Exact enumeration: |Aut|=40320 automorphisms of the support, 16 projection-fixing, and G = \ id, global swap\ Z_2 in the symmetric case; adding one declared, descent-visible discrimination-density orientation (calibrated by T12's landed local signature at one public class) recomputes G = \ id\ . Route transport between two isomorphic fibers shows the same contrast: two admissible transports symmetric, exactly one rigidified. Nonclaim: no claim that any particular quality space has nontrivial G ; the rigidifier is a modeled assumption, not a measurement; and if richer quality spaces always rigidify, the inverted spectrum dissolves, which is an allowed outcome.

conclusion: [S] Grade: schema plus exact correspondences. Scope: a three-state maintenance carrier with a threaded record accumulator (credit accrues 1/8 after a nonempty kernel to a cap of 1/4 , decays 1/8 after an empty one) over the budget grid \ 0, 1/4, 1/2, 3/4, 1\ . Existence-boundary labels are modeled as viability collapses, that is, as crossings of K_ viab =∅ under the declared ledger, and the finite prediction is threefold. Graded: kernel sizes pass through intermediate islands, up-sweep [0,0,1,2,3] , down-sweep [3,3,2,1,0] . Hysteretic: the up-sweep first-nonempty threshold is 1/2 while the primed down-sweep last-nonempty threshold is 1/4 ; recovery and collapse thresholds differ because the mechanism carries record state, not because thresholds were tabled separately. Clause-decomposable: C1-style persistence can coexist with collapsed C7 binding (covert-awareness pattern) or collapsed C6 temporal closure (timeless pattern), by importing the respective controls; full collapse zeroes all three. Robustness is conditional, not universal: a weaker accumulator rule loses strict hysteresis and a stronger one never re-crosses on the tested grid. Nonclaim: no claim that actual loss or recovery of consciousness is hysteretic, and any external measure of closure depth would need its own descent audit, and none is given.

conclusion: [Combination gate; T15] [S] Grade: schema with an exact one-carrier construction. Scope: one joint-package carrier with live states diagonal/crossed and a dead exit. Combination into a joint subject is certified only when the joint family passes both gates on the joint carrier: (i) C7 joint strict refinement, where the exact witness has K_ bw = (2) , R_ rec = (1,1) ; and (ii) C3 joint reflexivity, where per-action refinement of the joint public lens terminates at the pairing-valued predictive quotient, trajectory 1 → 2 → 2 , and that quotient carries the viability-relevant joint coordinate (public-lens kernel \ diagonal \ versus terminal-lens kernel \ diagonal, crossed \ ). Aggregation is exactly the collapsed R_ rec = K_ bw interface with no forced joint self-coordinate. The subject boundary is gate-determined by the surviving promoted carrier, not by a topological surface or by summing micro-packages. Interface contrast on the same states: the subject interface hides pairing (exposure false); the collective-ledger interface publishes it (exposure true), failing C4 by design, an institution-shaped control. Nonclaim: no general verdict about real collectives, and aggregation of local contents is never sufficient: it is the collapsed regime.

\label{thm:t17o}
\textsf{[O]} \emph{Grade:} axiom-relative conditional schema, mechanized.
\emph{Scope:} arbitrary carrier type $X$ and package $\mathrm{pkg}$;
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}$ and $\mathrm{Realized}$ are caller-supplied
predicate parameters. Assume:
\begin{itemize}
\item[(H1)] \emph{certificate soundness}: every simplified certificate is
sound for lawful audited closure,
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X,
\mathrm{pkg})$, an unproved schema premise that is neither A1 nor A2; and
\item[(H2)] \emph{A1}: lawful audited closure is realization,
$\mathrm{ClosureComplete}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow
\mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$.
\end{itemize}
Then every simplified-certified package is realized:
$\mathrm{Cert}_{\mathrm{simp}}(X, \mathrm{pkg}) \Rightarrow \mathrm{Realized}(X, \mathrm{pkg})$,
uniformly in the carrier type. \emph{Nonclaim:} neither premise is proved;
no A2 transport or invariance theorem exists (the universal carrier parameter
is A2's only footprint, not a proof step); no package is realized
unconditionally; and no candidate is certified.

The qualitative picture is straightforward: [leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em] Increasing noise p_ flip makes it harder to keep u=0 in the robust-support sense: all nonzero-probability successors must remain safe. Increasing repair cost shrinks the feasible action set A_ feas (s) (Section ), eventually making it impossible to guarantee repair when damage occurs. Because we use successor-support (almost-sure under the modeled kernel) semantics, K can be nonempty under noise only when there exists at least one feasible action whose transition support avoids unsafe states (e.g., repair actions that restore u=0 with probability 1 in the model); if all actions admit any unsafe successor with nonzero probability, the robust kernel collapses by design. \subsection{Result: a collapse boundary in $(p_{\mathrm{flip}}, \mathrm{cost})$ space}
Figure~\ref{fig:sweep_heatmaps} shows the two heatmaps. The qualitative picture is straightforward:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item Increasing noise $p_{\mathrm{flip}}$ makes it harder to keep $u=0$ in the robust-support sense: all nonzero-probability successors must remain safe.
  \item Increasing repair cost shrinks the feasible action set $A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)$ (Section~\ref{sec:engine}), eventually making it impossible to guarantee repair when damage occurs.
\end{itemize}
Because we use successor-support (almost-sure under the modeled kernel) semantics, $\mathcal{K}$ can be nonempty under noise only when there exists at least one feasible action whose transition support avoids unsafe states (e.g., repair actions that restore $u=0$ with probability 1 in the model); if all actions admit any unsafe successor with nonzero probability, the robust kernel collapses by design.
The combined effect produces a region where $|\mathcal{K}|$ collapses to $0$ (no policy can keep the system safe-and-coherent for all support outcomes), and a complementary region where $|\mathcal{K}|$ remains substantial. Empowerment collapses along the same boundary because a nontrivial action channel requires an induced layer that persists: without viability, there is no stable domain on which actions are meaningful.

source_wording_tex:
Figure~\ref{fig:sweep_heatmaps} shows the two heatmaps. The qualitative picture is straightforward:
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item Increasing noise $p_{\mathrm{flip}}$ makes it harder to keep $u=0$ in the robust-support sense: all nonzero-probability successors must remain safe.
  \item Increasing repair cost shrinks the feasible action set $A_{\mathrm{feas}}(s)$ (Section~\ref{sec:engine}), eventually making it impossible to guarantee repair when damage occurs.
\end{itemize}
Because we use successor-support (almost-sure under the modeled kernel) semantics, $\K$ can be nonempty under noise only when there exists at least one feasible action whose transition support avoids unsafe states (e.g., repair actions that restore $u=0$ with probability 1 in the model); if all actions admit any unsafe successor with nonzero probability, the robust kernel collapses by design.
The combined effect produces a region where $|\K|$ collapses to $0$ (no policy can keep the system safe-and-coherent for all support outcomes), and a complementary region where $|\K|$ remains substantial. Empowerment collapses along the same boundary because a nontrivial action channel requires an induced layer that persists: without viability, there is no stable domain on which actions are meaningful.

Quantitatively, over this grid we observe:
\[
|\K| \in [0.0,\ 56.0],
\qquad
\text{median }\Emp_{\mathrm{feas}} \in [0.0,\ 2.321928094887362]\ \text{bits}.
\]
(The empowerment maximum is approximately $\log_2 5 \approx 2.322$ bits in this configuration.)

All experiment outputs live under \texttt{results/} and are machine-checkable. JSON artifacts are required to include (possibly with type-specific naming for multi-config comparisons):
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*, itemsep=0.25em]
  \item \textbf{Configuration identity:} a \texttt{config} dictionary and its \texttt{config\_hash}, where the hash is a stable JSON hash of the config.
  \item \textbf{Metrics payload:} a \texttt{metrics} dictionary (or a type-specific payload for traces/sweeps) containing the quantitative outputs used in the paper.
  \item \textbf{Provenance:} a timestamp field (e.g., \texttt{created\_at\_utc}) and a \texttt{versions} dictionary (Python, NumPy, Matplotlib as applicable).
\end{itemize}
Filenames also encode hashes when appropriate, so that a plot or table can be traced to a configuration without opening the file.

For paper-facing stability, we export stable-named assets (figures and generated tables) into \texttt{paper/figures/} and \texttt{paper/generated/}. The file \texttt{paper/generated/numbers.json} collects the key scalars cited in the exhibits (e.g., idempotence defect at $\tau=2$, empowerment arrays, and learning medians) together with the hashes of the runs they were extracted from.

conclusion: Three runtime objects carry the measurable status of a candidate layer. The closure-deficit statistic CD_ tau is a conditional-information residual statistic at lookahead tau that measures unresolved structure under the current quotient : positive values indicate that recoverable structure remains outside the layer, while values bounded near zero indicate that the quotient is consistent with the corpus at the declared lookahead . The idempotence/self-consistency defect delta_ tau,f is a fixed-point gap for the layer's own quotient map at lookahead tau through readout f , measuring how closely the empirical data satisfy the idempotence relation introduced above . Schematically, the diagnostics separate residual structure from self-consistency: CD_ tau > 0 implies unresolved structure, delta_ tau,f 0 implies empirical self-consistency. Where states an exact idempotent map, the empirical estimator allows a small positive delta_ tau,f deviation and reports it in the audit log rather than hiding it. The symbol StrictExtCert denotes the strict-extension certificate, a typed witness object that licenses adding a candidate as a new layer in the ladder . A candidate is committed only after the gate panel emits this certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with the gate mechanics described in and formal definitions deferred to .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Three runtime objects carry the measurable status of a candidate layer. The closure-deficit statistic $\mathrm{CD}_{\tau}$ is a conditional-information residual statistic at lookahead $\tau$ that measures unresolved structure under the current quotient \cite{CoverThomas1991Information,Tishby2000Bottleneck}: positive values indicate that recoverable structure remains outside the layer, while values bounded near zero indicate that the quotient is consistent with the corpus at the declared lookahead \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}. The idempotence/self-consistency defect $\delta_{\tau,f}$ is a fixed-point gap for the layer's own quotient map at lookahead $\tau$ through readout $f$, measuring how closely the empirical data satisfy the idempotence relation introduced above \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}. Schematically, the diagnostics separate residual structure from self-consistency:
\[
\mathrm{CD}_{\tau} > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{unresolved structure}, \qquad
\delta_{\tau,f} \approx 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{empirical self-consistency}.
\]
Where \Cref{subsec:audited-layers} states an exact idempotent map, the empirical estimator allows a small positive $\delta_{\tau,f}$ deviation and reports it in the audit log rather than hiding it. The symbol $\mathsf{StrictExtCert}$ denotes the strict-extension certificate, a typed witness object that licenses adding a candidate as a new layer in the ladder \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}. A candidate is committed only after the gate panel emits this certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with the gate mechanics described in \Cref{sec:methods} and formal definitions deferred to \Cref{app:definitions}.

Three runtime objects carry the measurable status of a candidate layer. The closure-deficit statistic $\CDtau$ is a conditional-information residual statistic at lookahead $\tau$ that measures unresolved structure under the current quotient \cite{CoverThomas1991Information,Tishby2000Bottleneck}: positive values indicate that recoverable structure remains outside the layer, while values bounded near zero indicate that the quotient is consistent with the corpus at the declared lookahead \cite{Tsiokos2026NoGo}. The idempotence/self-consistency defect $\IDef$ is a fixed-point gap for the layer's own quotient map at lookahead $\tau$ through readout $f$, measuring how closely the empirical data satisfy the idempotence relation introduced above \cite{Tsiokos2026FoundationsI}. Schematically, the diagnostics separate residual structure from self-consistency:
\[
\CDtau > 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{unresolved structure}, \qquad
\IDef \approx 0 \;\Rightarrow\; \text{empirical self-consistency}.
\]
Where \Cref{subsec:audited-layers} states an exact idempotent map, the empirical estimator allows a small positive $\IDef$ deviation and reports it in the audit log rather than hiding it. The symbol $\strictcert$ denotes the strict-extension certificate, a typed witness object that licenses adding a candidate as a new layer in the ladder \cite{Tsiokos2026CantorShell}. A candidate is committed only after the gate panel emits this certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with the gate mechanics described in \Cref{sec:methods} and formal definitions deferred to \Cref{app:definitions}.

conclusion: Candidate layers enter the LTM ledger through a six-gate promotion panel, not through an unconstrained score threshold. The conjunctive panel is in the spirit of verifier-based and process-supervised pipelines that license outputs only after explicit per-step checks pass . The gates are descent, stability, control, no-smuggling, legibility, and strict factorization failure: respectively, residual reduction, quotient robustness, falsification evidence, audit-scope compliance, audit-log reconstructability, and a parent-identified/candidate-distinguished witness pair . The panel is conjunctive: all six gates must pass before the runtime commits the candidate and emits a strict-extension certificate; otherwise the runtime records a typed defect or remains silent, with evaluator details in , notation in , and empirical outcomes in .

conclusion: The readout path is capped by the same nonclaim discipline as layer promotion . When the audited path does not produce a committed answer, for example because no current layer's quotient covers the requested microstate at sufficient confidence, the runtime does not promote fallback statistics into a stronger claim. Instead, it either emits a provisional or silent claim with a typed defect record, or refuses to emit a token claim. The structural posture is the abstention / reject-option discipline familiar from selective classification , paired with the reliability concern that motivates calibration in modern neural networks . At pass end, a halt-verdict classifier reports the final status as accepted, provisional, blocked, outside-scope, failed-audit, absent-with-record, or below-threshold . expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{prop:gap-residual-decomposition}
Let \(\ensuremath{K^\star}\) be the closed base law, the best autonomous
stage-vocabulary kernel \(P(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid Y_t^\Pi)\), and let the canonical
institution \(\ensuremath{M}\) refine the stage package.  On the declared carrier,
\[
\CD{\Pi}{\tau}=\Gap{\Pi}{\tau}+\ResidualEnt{\Pi}{\tau},
\]
where
\[
\Gap{\Pi}{\tau}
 =
\mathbb E\!\left[
\ensuremath{D_{\mathrm{KL}}}\!\left(
P(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid \ensuremath{M})
\middle\| \ensuremath{K^\star}(\cdot\mid Y_t^\Pi)
\right)\right]
\]
is the expected Kullback--Leibler gain obtained by conditioning on the
institution, and
\[
\ResidualEnt{\Pi}{\tau}=H(Y^+_{t,\tau}\mid \ensuremath{M})
\]
is the residual future uncertainty left after conditioning on the institution.

conclusion: The previous subsections describe what the institutional state does. The last question is whether it is admissible as a promoted layer object, rather than a modeler's relabeling of the old stage vocabulary. The imported promotion standard supplies a gate battery for this purpose . In plain terms, the object must pass: well-formedness, meaning that the promotion claim is a typed record with its source, target, maps, evidence, and scope specified; descent, meaning that the induced macro update is independent of the representative history chosen inside a class; stability, meaning that the object is a fixed point of the declared refinement operation; control of content, meaning that the target layer is not used circularly to certify its own novelty; no-smuggling, meaning that specifications and public labels are declared before the searches that use them; visibility, meaning that the distinguishing content is exhibited on a legible finite slice; audit, meaning that the evidence is reproducibly recomputable; and strictness, meaning that the promoted refinement does not factor through the old vocabulary. The first gate is well-formedness of the promotion record, not predictive sufficiency in the sense used earlier. [Promotion certificate] On the declared carrier, the canonical institutional package M=P_ passes all eight imported promotion gates. The strictness gate passes in the strict sense: the promoted refinement has a nonempty factorization defect relative to the stage vocabulary, witnessed by the split pairs of .

conclusion: A certificate, in the sense used here, is a finite package of obligations and evidence. It is meant to prevent a higher-level object from being accepted merely because it has been renamed. The imported strict-extension framework specifies the obligations for certifying that a higher vocabulary is a genuine strict extension of a lower one . For the repeated-game setting, the relevant obligations are: a closed base law for the lower layer, meaning the best autonomous predictor available in the stage vocabulary; saturation of the higher vocabulary, meaning a predictive refinement fixed point; non-factorization, witnessed by split pairs whose distinctions are not definable from below; an exact quantitative price for omitting the higher layer, given by positive closure deficit and the gap–residual decomposition; material forcing, when a declared extension lets the higher layer feed back into play; and admissibility of the promoted object, checked by the gate battery described in . [Strict-extension certificate on the declared carrier] On the declared finite carrier, the canonical institutional state M=P_ is a certified strict extension of the stage game. The closed base law and exact price are supplied by ; non-factorization is supplied by ; saturation is supplied by ; material forcing is supplied, relative to its declared label-feedback extension, by ; and admissibility is supplied by the promotion certificate .

specifies the obligations for certifying that a higher vocabulary is a genuine
strict extension of a lower one \citep{Tsiokos2026CantorShell,Tsiokos2026FoundationsI,Tsiokos2026FoundationsII,Tsiokos2026FoundationsIII,Tsiokos2026OneMetaTheory}.

for the lower layer, meaning the best autonomous predictor available in the
stage vocabulary; saturation of the higher vocabulary, meaning a predictive
refinement fixed point; non-factorization, witnessed by split pairs whose
distinctions are not definable from below; an exact quantitative price for
omitting the higher layer, given by positive closure deficit and the
