conclusion: The anti-relabeling ledger is part of the result. This paper does not claim the predictive-state or causal-state quotient construction as new; that is a standard way to summarize a process by its predictive consequences . It does not claim the closure-deficit identity, or the optimality of the best autonomous macro-predictor, as new; those are imported from the closure-deficit and no-go accounts . It does not claim the strict-extension, saturation, or promotion-obligation framework as new; those are imported standards for recognizing when a higher vocabulary is a genuine layer rather than a relabeling . Nor does it claim as new the game-theoretic fact that added structure matters. Folk theorems show that repeated interaction can support many outcomes; global games show how noisy private information can select; reputation models show how type structure changes play; evolutionary and stochastic-stability models show that convention selection can be a property of a run; correlated equilibrium and type spaces show how signals and hidden state enlarge the game . These are reference points the paper uses, not results it rebrands. The contribution is the conjunction, on one explicit repeated-game object, under one evidentiary discipline. First, the paper installs the predictive state as the canonical institution of repeated play and verifies, on the finite carrier, that it is not definable from the game's own stage vocabulary: the institutional partition strictly refines the stage partition and does not factor through it. Second, the paper prices the omission exactly by closure deficit, with a gap–residual decomposition that separates what conditioning on the institution recovers from what remains unpredictable even after that conditioning. Third, it assembles these facts into a certified strict-extension object: the institutional vocabulary saturates, admits an active label-feedback exhibit under a declared extension, and passes the admissibility gates for a promoted layer on the carrier. Fourth, the picture is subjected to tests that could have failed silently but were reported in full: the run-layer constants are reproducible within protocol yet fail three frozen out-of-sample transfer attempts, and the human-data analysis confirms the predictive-residue hypothesis while reversing the proposed timing bridge. The registered negatives are not qualifications to the result; they are part of the evidence for the strict-extension reading.

\label{thm:carrier-dichotomy}
Let \(\mathcal B:\mathrm{Prop}\to\mathrm{Prop}\) be an
accepted-imports base, and assume import soundness
\[
  \forall Y.\ \mathcal B(Y)\Longrightarrow Y .
\]
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture and let \(C\) be a typed primary
carrier satisfying
\[
  C\leadsto X,\qquad C\models\text{typed-context discipline},\qquad
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C).
\]
Then the carrier audit has the following two-branch form:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
  &\Longrightarrow
    \exists X'.\,
      (R_C=0\leftrightarrow X')\wedge X'\neq X\wedge
      \operatorname{NativeOutcome}_{\mathcal B}(C,X'),\\
  \mbox{$X$-equivalent}_X(C)
  &\Longrightarrow
    \operatorname{ExactlyOne}\bigl(
      \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C),\mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C),\mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C)
    \bigr).
\end{aligned}
\]
Here
\[
\begin{aligned}
\operatorname{ExactlyOne}(A,B,D)
  \Longleftrightarrow{}&
  (A\wedge\neg B\wedge\neg D)\vee
  (B\wedge\neg A\wedge\neg D)\\
  &{}\vee(D\wedge\neg A\wedge\neg B).
\end{aligned}
\]

\begin{enumerate}
\item If \(C\) is non-$X$-equivalent, so that the residual closure of \(C\) is
  logically equivalent to some \(X'\neq X\), then the
  native-closure outcome\ of \(C\) is one of two kinds: either \(X'\) is
  already in the accepted-imports base and the carrier closes natively,
  or \(X'\) remains open-pending relative to that base.
\item If \(C\) is $X$-equivalent, so that the residual closure of \(C\) is
  logically equivalent to \(X\), then exactly one of the three
  carrier-residual-equivalent foreclosure modes applies:
  \[
    \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}},\qquad \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}},\qquad \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
  \]
\end{enumerate}

Consequently, under the Coverage Theorem, every admissible typed
primary carrier aimed at \(X\) is exhausted by the four-state audit:
\[
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C),
\]
with the three
$X$-equivalent\ modes disjoint in the audit classification.

\label{thm:coverage}
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture, and let \(C\) be a typed
primary carrier aimed at \(X\) under the typed-context discipline.  Assume \(C\) lies in an
admissible coverage context for \(X\).  Then the four typed states are
exhaustive: \(C\) is non-$X$-equivalent, or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}},
or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}}, or \(C\) is in \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
Equivalently, under
\[
  C\leadsto X,\qquad C\models\text{typed-context discipline},\qquad
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C),
\]
every admissible typed primary carrier aimed at \(X\) satisfies the
four-way disjunction
\[
  \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C)\vee
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C).
\]
The assertion is exhaustiveness only; disjointness of the three
$X$-equivalent\ modes is the separate exactly-one conclusion used in
Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-dichotomy} (Carrier Dichotomy).

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:type-finite-foreclosure}
Let \(X\) be an open target conjecture, and let \(C\) range over typed
primary carriers aimed at \(X\) under the typed-context discipline\ and an admissible
coverage context.  Then the carrier-state door-space is type-finite:
every such \(C\) is classified by one of the four states
non-$X$-equivalent, \textup{\textsc{CRE-TE}}, \textup{\textsc{CRE-BF}}, or \textup{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}.
Thus the codomain of audit classifications has exactly four entries,
and the image of any family of typed carriers aimed at \(X\) has
cardinality at most four, even when the carrier family itself is
infinite.
Formally, for
\[
  \mathsf{State}
  =\{\mathsf{nonX},\mathsf{TE},\mathsf{BF},\mathsf{CTMT}\},
\]
define
\[
\begin{aligned}
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{nonX},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{non-$X$-equivalent}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{TE},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-TE}}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{BF},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-BF}}_X(C),\\
  \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(\mathsf{CTMT},X,C)
    &\Longleftrightarrow \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C).
\end{aligned}
\]
Then
\[
  C\leadsto X\wedge C\models\text{typed-context discipline}\wedge
  \operatorname{CoverageCtx}(X,C)
  \Longrightarrow
  \exists s\in\mathsf{State}.\,
    \operatorname{ClassifiesAs}(s,X,C).
\]

\label{thm:attack-foreclosure-v4}
Let \(X\) be a target conjecture in framework scope.  Let \(m\) be a
framework-internal move, where
\[

mathematical content:
\[
  \operatorname{InScope}(X)
  \Longrightarrow
  \neg\,\operatorname{AdvancesWithoutExternal}(m,X).
\]

either it remains inside the four-state carrier classification from
Theorem~\ref{thm:carrier-dichotomy} (Carrier Dichotomy)\ and Conditional schema~\ref{thm:coverage} (Coverage), without closing \(X\) by
internal means, or it exposes framework-external\ content that must be
accepted through the closure-formation discipline rather than generated
by the framework-internal move itself.  The same statement applies
pointwise to chains by auditing each move in the chain.

\label{thm:ctmt-recursion}
For any target \(X\) and typed primary carrier \(C\), the
\textsc{CRE-CTMT}\ state admits a depth-indexed recursion tower.  The base case
is the depth-\(1\) tower: \(C\) is in \textsc{CRE-CTMT}\ exactly when \(C\) has
a one-level matrix-element terminus.  If \(C\)'s cascade reduces to a
deeper carrier-native matrix-element family whose own decision carries
a CTMT tower of positive depth, then \(C\) carries the next tower
level.  Formally, for any cascade semantics \(\sigma\),
\[
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C,1)
  \Longleftrightarrow
  \mbox{\textsc{CRE-CTMT}}_X(C),
\]
and for every \(n\geq 0\),
\[
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C',n+1)\wedge
  \operatorname{Reduces}_{\sigma}(X,C,C')
  \Longrightarrow
  \mathsf{Tower}_{\sigma}(X,C,n+2).
\]
Thus matrix-element terminality can fire at depth \(1\), depth \(2\),
and iteratively at any finite positive depth admitted by the
inherited-records base.

\begin{definition}[Three-option derivation sweep]\label{def:three-option-sweep}
The three-option derivation sweep is the Stage-6 sub-procedure that runs a

whether the closure is reachable by framework-primitive descent. The
SAU non-descent option\ asks whether the attempted derivation stops at non-descent at the

V-Differential resolves the closure route.

\StageSix\ is the template's stress test for derivation routes. The
formed closure is run against three independent options, each asking
whether the load-bearing source can be obtained without invoking the
recognition step. The cross-track observation in this subsection is
deliberately limited: the \SigPattern\ signature is two-instance verified
on PvNP and RH, and remains corpus-pending outside those two rows.

\begin{definition}[Three-option derivation sweep]\label{def:three-option-sweep}
The three-option derivation sweep is the Stage-6 sub-procedure that runs a
trace-state-only closure attempt against three options. The \OptFP\ asks
whether the closure is reachable by framework-primitive descent. The
\OptSAU\ asks whether the attempted derivation stops at non-descent at the
SAU boundary. The \OptVDE\ asks whether elevating the data inside
V-Differential resolves the closure route.
\end{definition}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:attack-foreclosure-v5}
Let \(X\) be a target in framework scope, and let \(c\) be a formed
closure whose substrate lies in the V-Differential trace-state-only column\ under the SB closure
assumption.  Then the v5 refinement has the following three-conjunct
form:
\[
\begin{aligned}
  &\forall m.\,
    \operatorname{DerivationRoute}(m)
    \Longrightarrow
    \neg\operatorname{AdvancesWithoutExternal}(m,X),\\
  &\forall l:\operatorname{RMLanding}(c,X).\,
    \operatorname{ImportsAsNamedRecognition}(l,s_{c,X}),\\
  &\forall l:\operatorname{RMLanding}(c,X).\,
    \operatorname{LandsAtTheoremGrade}(c,X).
\end{aligned}
\]
The first conjunct is the v4 foreclosure conclusion restricted to
derivation routes.  The second says that recognition-mode landings
import the load-bearing source as named recognition.  The third says
that such landings reach theorem-grade under the SB closure assumption.
Thus v5 refines, does not replace, v4: derivation routes remain
foreclosed, while recognition-mode landings are structurally distinct
and peer with derivation-mode landings under the SB closure assumption.

conclusion: Within a calibration family, a candidate calibration is genuinely new if and only if, for every existing family member, it differs on at least one axis of the four-axis calibration profile. Equivalently, a candidate matching an existing member on algebraic identities, detector class, descent invariants, and carrier orientation is a rebadge; on attempted earning-its-place, it collapses to the existing member's content. Equivalently, for a candidate profile p and family F , GenuineNew(p, F) iff q∈ F, p_ alg q_ alg p_ det q_ det p_ desc q_ desc p_ orient q_ orient .
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:rebadge-discipline}
Within a calibration family, a candidate calibration is genuinely new if
and only if, for every existing family member, it differs on at least one
axis of the four-axis calibration profile.  Equivalently, a candidate matching an existing
member on algebraic identities, detector class, descent invariants, and
carrier orientation is a rebadge; on attempted earning-its-place, it
collapses to the existing member's content.
Equivalently, for a candidate profile \(p\) and family \(\mathcal F\),
\[
  \mathsf{GenuineNew}(p,\mathcal F)
  \iff
  \forall q\in\mathcal F,\,
  p_{\mathsf{alg}}\ne q_{\mathsf{alg}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{det}}\ne q_{\mathsf{det}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{desc}}\ne q_{\mathsf{desc}}\vee
  p_{\mathsf{orient}}\ne q_{\mathsf{orient}}.
\]

conclusion: Calibration-side typed bridges carry a directed source-to-target type signature. For a bridge B with source S and target T , the bridge is symmetric with its reversal if and only if S=T . In particular, when S T , the existence of a typed bridge S→ T does not by itself supply a usable typed bridge T→ S . Formally, B=B^ op iff source(B)=target(B).
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:bridge-type-direction}
Calibration-side typed bridges carry a directed source-to-target type
signature.  For a bridge \(B\) with source \(S\) and target \(T\), the
bridge is symmetric with its reversal if and only if \(S=T\).  In
particular, when \(S\ne T\), the existence of a typed bridge \(S\to T\)
does not by itself supply a usable typed bridge \(T\to S\).
Formally,
\[
  B=B^{\mathrm{op}}
  \iff
  \mathsf{source}(B)=\mathsf{target}(B).
\]

conclusion: Lifting the four Part II schemas to theorem-grade across the framework requires two future inputs: (a) a third-instance substrate landing on a V-Differential trace-state-only substrate beyond PvNP and RH, with Hodge as the leading candidate; and (b) a structural argument from the V-Differential column-membership predicate to the (ii)/(iii)/(ii) verdict pattern. Until both inputs exist, each of the four Part II universal claims remains a candidate meta-theorem. The first input is empirical in the corpus sense: it asks for a third landed trace-state-only example, audited by the same seven-stage template and by the same two-instance signature comparison already used for PvNP and RH. The second input is structural: it asks for a reason why trace-state-only column membership should force the framework-primitive, SAU non-descent, and V-Differential elevation sweep to display the (ii)/(iii)/(ii) pattern. Without the structural argument, a third example would still be suggestive rather than theorem-grade.

\label{thm:pvnp:e-q-closure-properties}
The saturated current-observable family \(E^{!}_{Q}\) has the following
closure properties.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \emph{Post-processing.}  If \(f\inE^{!}_{Q}\) has codomain
  \(Y\), and \(g:Y\to Z\) is a deterministic polynomial-time function
  with a declared polynomial budget in the input length, then
  \(g\circ f\inE^{!}_{Q}\).

  \item \emph{Finite products.}  If
  \(f_{1},\ldots,f_{k}\inE^{!}_{Q}\) have codomains
  \(Y_{1},\ldots,Y_{k}\), and the family is fixed-stage in the audit
  sense, at a common stage \(N\), then the product observable
  \[
    h\longmapsto (f_{1}(h),\ldots,f_{k}(h))
  \]
  belongs to \(E^{!}_{Q}\), with codomain
  \(Y_{1}\times\cdots\times Y_{k}\).

  \item \emph{Composition.}  Suppose \(f\inE^{!}_{Q}\) has codomain
  \(Y\), the values \(f(h)\) are encoded SAT instances or other
  admitted input encodings, and \(g\inE^{!}_{Q}\) is a current
  observable defined on histories of the resulting instances.  Then
  the suitable polynomial-time composition \(g\star f\) belongs to
  \(E^{!}_{Q}\).  This composition is through the lawful transducer
  interfaces, not through identity on the history carrier: the
  realizing transducer is the composition of the two underlying
  transducers, with combined time, visibility, replay, and audit
  records.
\end{enumerate}

The first translation theorem identifies the framework-internal
decision-currentization predicate with the standard membership
predicate \(\mathrm{SAT}\in P\).  The forward direction uses observable
saturation: a standard polynomial-time SAT decider, once equipped with
its machine index, time certificate, replay convention, visibility
bookkeeping, and audit record, is a lawful current observable and
therefore belongs to \(E^{!}_{Q}\).  The reverse direction uses
lawfulness extraction: a current observable computing the SAT decision
bit carries enough typed lawfulness data to recover an ordinary
polynomial-time SAT decider.  Both directions are proved below.

\begin{theorem}[Translation Theorem A]
\label{thm:translation-A}
For the saturated SAT layer and the current instrument \(I_{\mathrm{poly}}\),
\[
  \mathrm{SAT}\in P
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT}).
\]
Equivalently, SAT has a standard polynomial-time decision procedure if
and only if there exists a lawful polynomial-time current observable in
\(E^{!}_{Q}\) computing the SAT decision bit on every encoded SAT
instance.
\end{theorem}

Translation Theorem B bridges decision currentization and witness
currentization, showing that the two predicates are equivalent: a
lawful current observable computing the SAT decision bit exists if
and only if a lawful current observable computing the canonical
satisfying-witness producer exists.  The
forward direction uses SAT self-reducibility
\citep{Schoening1986ComplexityStructure,HemaspaandraOgihara2002SelfReducibility,Selman1988SelfReducible},
namely the standard variable-by-variable witness-search-from-decider
construction, together with the closure properties of \(E^{!}_{Q}\).  The reverse direction
post-processes the witness producer's output to recover the decision
bit.  We prove both directions below; the forward direction uses the
standard SAT self-reduction as a classical input.

\begin{theorem}[Translation Theorem B]
\label{thm:translation-B}
For the saturated SAT layer and autonomous lift \(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}\),
\[
  \operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{dec}}_{Q}(\mathrm{SAT})
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \operatorname{Currentize}^{\mathrm{wit}}_{Q}(\Omega_{\mathrm{SAT}}).
\]
Equivalently, the SAT decision bit is current if and only if the
canonical satisfying-witness producer is current.
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The Class-B analysis rests on two theorem-grade facts about the
standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier.  The first says
that lawful current observables separate encoded inputs.  The second
says that separately lawful current observations can be paired without
leaving the saturated current-observable family.

\begin{theorem}[Fixed-Presentation Orbit Collapse]
\label{thm:pvnp:orbit-collapse}
For the standard fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier, the
common kernel of all lawful saturated current observables is the
diagonal:
\[
  \bigcap_{F\inE^{!}_{Q}}\ker(F)=\Delta_{X}.
\]
Equivalently, if \(x\neq y\) are distinct encoded inputs in the carrier,
then there is a lawful current observable \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\) such that
\[
  F(x)\neq F(y).
\]
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:pvnp:basis-combination-closure}
Let \(\Phi\) be a finite basis-generated feature of the standard
fixed-presentation polynomial current carrier.  Then \(\Phi\) lies in
one of the five normal classes \(Q,J,C,P,T\).  Moreover, the following
class consequence holds.
\begin{enumerate}
\item[\(Q\).] If \(\Phi\) is a quotient feature, then any equivalence
  relation respected by every \(F\inE^{!}_{Q}\) is the diagonal; orbit
  collapse forces the feature to be trivial.
\item[\(J\).] If \(\Phi\) is a joint-access feature, then any finite
  tuple of separately current observables admits a jointly current
  product observable; pairing closure kills the alleged obstruction.
\item[\(C\).] If \(\Phi\) is a positive-closure feature, then it
  constructs new current observables from current observables and does
  not exclude a target.
\item[\(P\).] If \(\Phi\) is a presentation-refinement feature, then
  it supplies breaker or refinement data rather than an invariance
  obstruction.
\item[\(T\).] If \(\Phi\) is a time-filtration feature, then it is
  either fixed-stratum only, with no obstruction at the full carrier
  \(E^{!}_{Q}=\bigcup_k E^{[k]}\), or it is target-equivalent at the
  full polynomial union.
\end{enumerate}

conclusion: Every lawful current observable in E^ ! _ Q , acting on the saturated SAT layer T^ ! _ SAT , passes the following seven gate checks with the typed evidence records carried in its lawfulness data. G_ 1 , no SAT oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for the SAT decision predicate. The status passes by construction: the audited shell admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not SAT-oracle machines. The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle commitments. The implication is that the observable's computation does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input. G_ 2 , no witness oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a satisfying-witness producer . The status passes by construction, and the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer. The implication is that satisfying assignments are not pre-loaded into the observable or made available as hidden input. G_ 3 , no external verifier oracle smuggling. The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an external NP-verifier oracle. The status passes by the same audit evidence: verifier behavior must be realized by the declared polynomial-time computation itself. The implication is that the observable cannot test whether an assignment satisfies a formula by an undeclared oracle call. G_ 4 , no hidden B -bit smuggling. The check predicate says that the visibility lens does not encode a hidden bit, such as a disguised SAT bit, into the Q -visible package data . The status passes by visibility bookkeeping. The evidence is the visibility-lens record attached to the current instrument. The implication is that the Q -visible projection does not encode predictive or witness-side data. G_ 5 , no time-certificate smuggling. The check predicate says that the polynomial time certificate is honest: the observable does not exceed its declared polynomial budget by hiding deferred evaluation or unrecorded subcomputation. The status passes by the time-certificate clause of the lawfulness discipline. The evidence is the certificate itself, together with the replay record. The implication is that the observable's polynomial budget is the budget actually audited. G_ 6 , no scope violation. The check predicate says that the observable's domain is the all-input replay convention's instance set, not a favorable subfamily of SAT instances. The status passes by the all-input replay convention. The evidence is the replay record. The implication is that the observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current observable. G_ 7 , no overreading suppression. The check predicate says that the observable does not suppress overreading of its own audit data: the lawfulness record is faithful to the actual computation being audited. The status passes by the Foundations-III no-overreading-suppression theorem . The evidence is the audit witness field. The implication is that the audit ledger's records cannot be falsified or selectively hidden at audit time.

\label{prop:pvnp:gate-audit}
Every lawful current observable in \(E^{!}_{Q}\), acting on the
saturated SAT layer \(T^{!}_{\mathrm{SAT}}\), passes the following seven gate checks
with the typed evidence records carried in its lawfulness data.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(G_{1}\), \emph{no SAT oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle
  \citep{BakerGillSolovay1975Relativization} for the SAT decision
  predicate.  The status passes by construction: the audited shell
  admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not
  SAT-oracle machines.
  The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle
  commitments.  The implication is that the observable's computation
  does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input.

  \item \(G_{2}\), \emph{no witness oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a
  satisfying-witness producer \citep{FeigeShamir1990WitnessHiding,GoldwasserMicaliRackoff1989KnowledgeComplexity}.  The status passes by construction, and
  the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer.
  The implication is that satisfying assignments are not pre-loaded
  into the observable or made available as hidden input.

  \item \(G_{3}\), \emph{no external verifier oracle smuggling}.
  The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an
  external NP-verifier oracle.  The status passes by the same audit
  evidence: verifier behavior must be realized by the declared
  polynomial-time computation itself.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot test whether an assignment satisfies a formula by
  an undeclared oracle call.

  \item \(G_{4}\), \emph{no hidden \(B\)-bit smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the visibility lens does not encode a
  hidden bit, such as a disguised SAT bit, into the \(Q\)-visible
  package data
  \citep{GoguenMeseguer1982SecurityPolicies,SabelfeldMyers2003InformationFlow}.  The status passes by visibility bookkeeping.  The
  evidence is the visibility-lens record attached to the current
  instrument.  The implication is that the \(Q\)-visible projection
  does not encode predictive or witness-side data.

  \item \(G_{5}\), \emph{no time-certificate smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the polynomial time certificate is honest:
  the observable does not exceed its declared polynomial budget by
  hiding deferred evaluation or unrecorded subcomputation.  The status
  passes by the time-certificate clause of the lawfulness discipline.
  The evidence is the certificate itself, together with the replay
  record.  The implication is that the observable's polynomial budget
  is the budget actually audited.

  \item \(G_{6}\), \emph{no scope violation}.  The check predicate
  says that the observable's domain is the all-input replay
  convention's instance set, not a favorable subfamily of SAT
  instances.  The status passes by the all-input replay convention.
  The evidence is the replay record.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current
  observable.

  \item \(G_{7}\), \emph{no overreading suppression}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not suppress overreading of
  its own audit data: the lawfulness record is faithful to the actual
  computation being audited.  The status passes by the Foundations-III
  no-overreading-suppression theorem
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsIII2026}.  The evidence is the audit
  witness field.  The implication is that the audit ledger's records
  cannot be falsified or selectively hidden at audit time.

\label{prop:pvnp:gate-audit}
Every lawful current observable in \(\EQbang\), acting on the
saturated SAT layer \(\Tsat\), passes the following seven gate checks
with the typed evidence records carried in its lawfulness data.
\begin{enumerate}
  \item \(\GateOne\), \emph{no SAT oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle
  \citep{BakerGillSolovay1975Relativization} for the SAT decision
  predicate.  The status passes by construction: the audited shell
  admits ordinary deterministic polynomial-time transducers, not
  SAT-oracle machines.
  The evidence is the audit ledger recording the absence of oracle
  commitments.  The implication is that the observable's computation
  does not implicitly use the SAT bit as input.

  \item \(\GateTwo\), \emph{no witness oracle smuggling}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not invoke an oracle for a
  satisfying-witness producer \citep{FeigeShamir1990WitnessHiding,GoldwasserMicaliRackoff1989KnowledgeComplexity}.  The status passes by construction, and
  the evidence is again the audit ledger of the admitted transducer.
  The implication is that satisfying assignments are not pre-loaded
  into the observable or made available as hidden input.

  \item \(\GateThree\), \emph{no external verifier oracle smuggling}.
  The check predicate says that the observable does not invoke an
  external NP-verifier oracle.  The status passes by the same audit
  evidence: verifier behavior must be realized by the declared
  polynomial-time computation itself.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot test whether an assignment satisfies a formula by
  an undeclared oracle call.

  \item \(\GateFour\), \emph{no hidden \(B\)-bit smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the visibility lens does not encode a
  hidden bit, such as a disguised SAT bit, into the \(Q\)-visible
  package data
  \citep{GoguenMeseguer1982SecurityPolicies,SabelfeldMyers2003InformationFlow}.  The status passes by visibility bookkeeping.  The
  evidence is the visibility-lens record attached to the current
  instrument.  The implication is that the \(Q\)-visible projection
  does not encode predictive or witness-side data.

  \item \(\GateFive\), \emph{no time-certificate smuggling}.  The
  check predicate says that the polynomial time certificate is honest:
  the observable does not exceed its declared polynomial budget by
  hiding deferred evaluation or unrecorded subcomputation.  The status
  passes by the time-certificate clause of the lawfulness discipline.
  The evidence is the certificate itself, together with the replay
  record.  The implication is that the observable's polynomial budget
  is the budget actually audited.

  \item \(\GateSix\), \emph{no scope violation}.  The check predicate
  says that the observable's domain is the all-input replay
  convention's instance set, not a favorable subfamily of SAT
  instances.  The status passes by the all-input replay convention.
  The evidence is the replay record.  The implication is that the
  observable cannot be a partial decider presented as a total current
  observable.

  \item \(\GateSeven\), \emph{no overreading suppression}.  The check
  predicate says that the observable does not suppress overreading of
  its own audit data: the lawfulness record is faithful to the actual
  computation being audited.  The status passes by the Foundations-III
  no-overreading-suppression theorem
  \citep{TsiokosFoundationsIII2026}.  The evidence is the audit
  witness field.  The implication is that the audit ledger's records
  cannot be falsified or selectively hidden at audit time.
\end{enumerate}

\]

\begin{theorem}[RH AOR-instance theorem\footnote{Verified in the Lean formalization against the local refinement-stable AOR predicate over the assembled-carrier fields; the partial alignment relative to the full audit-closure refinement-stable characterisation of \citet{TsiokosAOR2026} is recorded in App~\ref{app:formalization}.}]
\label{thm:rh:aor-instance}
Under the discharges recorded in
\Cref{thm:rh:aor-mechanical-records,thm:rh:aor-recognition-discharge,thm:rh:aor-gamma-bridge-discharge,thm:rh:aor-auditL-discharge,thm:rh:aor-dc-master-import-discharge,thm:rh:aor-real-coordinate-discharge,thm:rh:aor-translation-interface-discharge}, the saturated completed
Selberg trace shell is a local refinement-stable AOR instance on the
RH scope:
\[
  \mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\in
  \mathrm{RefStableAOR}^{\mathrm{ref}}_{\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}}.
\]
Consequently, at the record level of this AOR instance, the typed zero
ledger of \(\mathrm{Sel}^{!}_{\zeta,\mathrm{tr}}\) has no nontrivial zeros off the fixed locus
\(\Fix(J_{L})\).
\end{theorem}

\begin{proof}
The definition-side rows provide the carrier, target, role, and
presentation records.  The recognition source provides the
domination-record source.  Its structural-coherence assumptions carry
the abstract DC conclusion to the shell equality \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\).  The
\(\mathrm{Audit}_{L}\) field supplies the admissibility
status of the shell.  The master theorem of \citet{TsiokosSDTC2026}
is an accepted typed-cone import.  The real-coordinate presentation
residual and the admissibility-as-hypothesis residual are both
explicitly statused rather than suppressed.  Translation theorem T
then converts \(A_{Z}(\zeta)=0\) into the statement
\[
  \forall\,\rho\inZ_{\zeta}^{\mathrm{nt}},\quad \Real(\rho)=\frac12.
\]
Thus every listed residual in the local wrapper for
\(\mathfrak S_{\mathrm{RH}}\) is either zero, bridged, approved,
carried by construction, or registered as outside the stronger
analytic scope.  This is the AOR-membership reading of
\Cref{thm:rh:conditional}; it does not upgrade the conditional chain
to an unconditional analytic theorem.
\end{proof}

This section records the no-go family constraining attempts to pay
the residual ledgers of \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade}.  Each no-go
excludes a category of shortcut payment that uses data of the wrong
type.  The no-gos do not pay any ledger; they restrict admissible
payments so that the Gevrey radius-window and Littlewood--Paley
transport rescue of \Cref{sec:gevrey-lp} carries the remaining
analytic obligation.  The criterion-native circularity result NG1 was
recorded in \Cref{sec:imports}; here we record NG2--NG10.

\begin{theorem}[No-go NG2: scalar energy / enstrophy category error]
\label{thm:ns:no-go-scalar-energy}
Quadratic scalar budgets such as kinetic energy \(\|u\|_{L^2}^2\),
enstrophy \(\|\nabla u\|_{L^2}^2\), or any positive scalar functional
that is quadratic in the carrier variable, are not lawful native Schur
probes.  The adequacy residual
\[
  \Xi_C(D\mid L)=K_{DD}-K_{DL}K_{LL}^{\dagger}K_{LD}
\]
is defined for a linear native probe family \(L:E\to Y\).  A quadratic
scalar functional is not such a family, so
\(\Xi_C(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\mid\text{scalar quadratic})\) is not a well-formed object
of the Schur-complement calculus until a lawful linear native family has
been declared and audited.
\end{theorem}

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ns:no-go-packing-amplitude}
For a bad set with size scaling \(\sim r^{3-d}\) and amplitude scaling
\(\sim r^{-\alpha}\), the contribution to the BG readout scales as
\[
  r^{(3-d)/2-\alpha}.
\]
Packing alone suppresses this amplitude only when
\(\alpha < (3-d)/2\).  Outside that range, small-set sparseness does
not control \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\)-amplitude, and the residual requires either a

conclusion: Thus the half-log Gevrey budget under Bradshaw–Grujic frequency-doubling fails the summable predictive-propagation hypothesis unless an additional decay record is supplied.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ns:no-go-half-log-endpoint}
On the available half-log analyticity lane alone, the staged residual
budget has the form
\[
  B_j
  =
  C_B\,2^{2pj}\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_j}\bigr)
  e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}},
  \qquad
  p=q-\varepsilon,\qquad
  L_j=\log\lambda_J .
\]
For positive constants \(C_B,\mu,c\) and \(p>0\), the stage ratio
satisfies
\[
  \frac{B_{j+1}}{B_j}
  =
  2^{2p}
  \frac{\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_{j+1}}\bigr)
        e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_{j+1}}}}
       {\bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_j}\bigr)
        e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}}}
  \longrightarrow 2^{2p}>1 .
\]
Thus the half-log Gevrey budget under Bradshaw--Grujic
frequency-doubling fails the summable predictive-propagation hypothesis
unless an additional decay record is supplied.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{thm:ns:gevrey-dominance}
For the Gevrey-normalized derivative probe
\(\widetilde M_{m,J,t}\), the dominance constant at derivative order
\(m\) has the closed form
\[
  A_m^G(t,J)
  =
  \lambda_J(t)^{q-\varepsilon}\,
  \frac{m!}{\sigma_J(t)^m},
  \qquad
  \sigma_J(t)=\frac{\lambda_J(t)\rho(t)}{C_G}.
\]
Optimizing over \(m\ge 0\) gives, for a positive constant \(c\),
\[
  \inf_{m\ge 0} A_m^G(t,J)
  \lesssim
  \lambda_J(t)^{q-\varepsilon}\sqrt{1+\sigma_J(t)}\,
  e^{-c\sigma_J(t)} .
\]
Consequently the direct radius-window gate is
\[
  \sigma_J(t)\ge \log\lambda_J(t),
\]
up to the harmless normalization constants absorbed into \(c\).  Under
this gate the optimized dominance is smaller than the leading
\(\lambda_J^{q-\varepsilon}\) scaling by an exponential radius-window factor.

\label{thm:ns:lp-transport-rescue}
Let \(S_j:L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\) be the LP-transport stage operator with
\(s\ge q-\varepsilon\), and set \(p=q-\varepsilon\).  The half-log staged budget
transports to
\[

  e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}},

\[

  \longrightarrow

\]

response space \(H^{-s}\), so the transported residual satisfies the
summable predictive-propagation hypothesis.

\label{thm:ns:lp-transport-rescue}
Let \(\LPtr:L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\) be the LP-transport stage operator with
\(s\ge q-\eps\), and set \(p=q-\eps\).  The half-log staged budget
transports to
\[
  \widetilde B_j(s)
  \simeq
  2^{2(p-s)j}
  \bigl(1+\mu\sqrt{L_j}\bigr)
  e^{-2c\mu\sqrt{L_j}},
  \qquad
  L_j=\log\lambdaJ .
\]
For every \(s>p\),
\[
  \frac{\widetilde B_{j+1}(s)}{\widetilde B_j(s)}
  \longrightarrow
  2^{2(p-s)}<1 .
\]
Consequently \(\sum_j \widetilde B_j(s)<\infty\) on the transported
response space \(H^{-s}\), so the transported residual satisfies the
summable predictive-propagation hypothesis.

\Cref{sec:ns-carrier,sec:imports,sec:adequacy-cascade,sec:no-go,sec:gevrey-lp}
into the hypothesis stack consumed by the layer-dissolving membrane
endpoint of \citet{Tsiokos2026NeedleKiller}.  The records and the

smooth-data channel.

\begin{definition}[Six Birds closure records \(R_1\)--\(R_9\)]
\label{def:ns:closure-r1-r9}
The Six Birds closure record bundle for the Navier--Stokes carrier is
the tuple
\[
  \mathsf R=(R_1,R_2,R_3,R_4,R_5,R_6,R_7,R_8,R_9),
\]
where the nine entries are the following proof-carrying records.
\begin{enumerate}[label=$R_\arabic*$.]
\item Adequacy orientation: the carrier data
\((E_{J,t},C_{J,t},\Lphys_{J,t},\DBG_{J,t})\) is ordered so that a
smaller residual \(\Xi\) is better.
\item Exact BG-windowed package: \(\Gamma_j\) preserves
divergence-free structure and the mismatch sector on the packaged
carrier.
\item Null-mode legality: \(L^{\mathrm{phys}}\) and \(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\) vanish on
\(\Ker C_{J,t}\) as in \Cref{sec:ns-carrier}.
\item Source-admission acceptance: the recurrence with
\(\Omega_{\mathrm{src}}=\Omega_{\mathrm{tr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{pr}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{visc}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{tail}}+\Omega_{\mathrm{str}}\) is accepted on the
cascade of \Cref{sec:adequacy-cascade}.
\item BG frequency-doubling staging: the active scales obey
\(\lambda_{j+1}=2\lambda_j\).
\item Dissolving-side LP transport: \(S_j:L^2(P_j)\to H^{-s}\) with
\(s\ge q-\varepsilon\) is accepted as the typed transport of
\Cref{sec:gevrey-lp}.
\item Half-log analyticity: restart data in
\(H^{\gamma_0}\cap\dot B^{-\varepsilon}_{\infty,\infty}\), with
\(\gamma_0>3/2-\varepsilon\), carries the half-log lower radius on
BG-compatible stages.
\item Paper-grounded PDE imports: Beale--Kato--Majda continuation,
Bradshaw--Grujic frequency-window continuation, Kato local
well-posedness, half-log analyticity, Littlewood--Paley /
Bony--Chemin--Danchin calculus, and the Sobolev/Besov embedding chain
are accepted at their declared status.
\item Nonclaim boundary: there is no criterion-native replacement of
\(D^{\mathrm{BG}}\), no generic Besov claim, no untyped global comparison, and no
closure outside the smooth-data subcarrier without additional records.
\end{enumerate}
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Route-stability $\Rightarrow$ polynomial capacity]\label{thm:route-capacity}
Assume $C(0)\ge 0$, $e(n)\ge 0$ for all $n$, and the recursion \eqref{eq:route-rec} holds with
the tame bound \eqref{eq:r-tame}. Then for all $n\in\mathbb{N}$,
\[
C(n)\ \le\ \Big(C(0)+\sum_{k=0}^{n-1} e(k)\Big)\,(n+1)^p.
\]
In particular, if \eqref{eq:e-bounded} holds for some $E\ge 0$, then
\[
C(n)\ \le\ (C(0)+E)\,(n+1)^p,
\]
so $C(n)$ cannot grow exponentially in depth.
\end{theorem}

\begin{remark}[Proof idea (one paragraph)]
Iterate \eqref{eq:route-rec}. Each step contributes a multiplicative factor $r(k)$ in front of the
previous capacity, plus an additive mismatch term transported forward by later $r(\cdot)$ factors.
Using \eqref{eq:r-tame}, the transported factors telescope to $(n+1)^p$, yielding the stated bound.
\end{remark}

conclusion: a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility quantitatively excludes localization
expanded_source_wording_tex:
This section isolates a structural obstruction in the ``capacity certificate'' route.
Roughly: an ICAP-style inequality is an \emph{extremal} (worst-case) gain bound.
If the feasible interface inputs at scale $j$ are rich enough to contain highly localized tests
(the discrete analogue of wavepackets), then ICAP forces a \emph{pointwise} bound on the
positive-gain functional of the bridge.
In the Navier--Stokes interpretation, that pointwise gain corresponds to a classical
``peak/strain'' channel.
Therefore, a uniform ICAP certificate cannot bypass the traditional bottleneck unless feasibility
\emph{quantitatively excludes localization}.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
\label{lem:channel-antiloc}
Fix a finite index set of channels $\rho$ with $|\rho|=m$ and a finite spatial index set $\iota$
(modeling a discrete grid). Let $B\subset \iota$ represent a cell/ball at scale $j$.
Assume channel shapes $\psi_r:\iota\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfy the delocalization bound
\[
\sum_{i\in B} \psi_r(i)^2 \;\le\; \kappa\,\mu(B)\qquad \text{for all }r\in\rho,
\]
where $\kappa\ge 0$ and $\mu(B)\ge 0$ is the reference ``cell mass'' (e.g.\ volume fraction).
Then for any coefficients $a:\rho\to\mathbb{R}$ the synthesized field
$u(i)=\sum_{r\in\rho} a_r\,\psi_r(i)$ satisfies
\begin{equation}
\label{eq:finite-channel-antiloc}
\sum_{i\in B} u(i)^2
\;\le\;
m\,\kappa\,\mu(B)\,\sum_{r\in\rho} a_r^2.
\end{equation}
In particular, if the channel family is orthonormal in $\ell^2(\iota)$ so that
$\|u\|_{\ell^2}^2=\sum_r a_r^2$, then $u$ is $\eta$-anti-localized on $B$ with
$\eta = m\,\kappa\,\mu(B)$.

We now define an operational notion of ``SBT legality'' for initial data, intended as an
\emph{admissibility restriction} for a modified research question (not the Clay problem):
\emph{do SBT-legal initial data evolve without Zeno cascades, and hence avoid blow-up within
the No-Zeno scaffold?}

\begin{definition}[Operational SBT-legality certificate (initial data)]
\label{def:spt-legal-cert}
Given a dyadic decomposition $u_0=\sum_j (u_0)_j$, define $L_j(u_0)$ by \eqref{eq:local-energy-fraction}.
Let $f_j$ denote the baseline volume fraction at scale $j$ (uniform reference).
Define the normalized concentration factor
\[
\kappa_j(u_0) \;:=\; \frac{L_j(u_0)}{f_j}.
\]
We say $u_0$ is \emph{SBT-legal at thresholds} $(\kappa_\star,\mathrm{burst}_\star,m_\star)$
if the certificate computed by the script
\nolinkurl{python/scripts/ns_spt_legal_certify.py}
returns PASS, which in practice checks configurable bounds on:
(i) $\max_j \kappa_j$,
(ii) a burst ratio statistic over time windows if evolution is enabled,
and optionally (iii) an effective channel count $m_{95}$ from PCA/SVD diagnostics.
\end{definition}

conclusion: Finally, we show the certificate rejects intentionally localized ``wavepacket-like'' initial data. We construct an ILLEGAL initial condition by placing most of the shell energy into a localized blob in a single dyadic band (see python/src/nswave/illegal_initial_conditions.py ). The LEGAL baseline is a standard band-limited random initial condition used in our demos. Bandlimiting alone does not prevent spatial concentration: the ILLEGAL example is band-limited by construction yet fails the certificate with a large . [t] ∈cludegraphics[width=0.92 ] ../python/artifacts/paper/ns_spt_illegal_vs_legal.png LEGAL vs.\ ILLEGAL initial data under the same SBT-legality certificate. The LEGAL baseline passes with _j _j O(1) , while an intentionally localized shell ``wavepacket'' fails immediately with a very large concentration factor (e.g.\ _j _j 10^2 in the included demo). This illustrates that SBT-legality is a substantive restriction: it rules out strongly localized high-frequency initial conditions that trigger the wavepacket obstruction.

conclusion: Definition is intentionally stricter than merely being able to label states by zero and one. A candidate bit must remain stable long enough to matter, must support a descended operator calculus, and must survive audit. This is why the six primitives are complementary rather than redundant. P5 packages the carrier; P4 keeps it from dissolving immediately; P2 makes it semantically meaningful; P1 determines whether an effective operator vocabulary can be stabilized; P3 detects route dependence and protocol residue; P6 determines what must be paid to maintain the whole arrangement. The criterion is also intentionally broader than classical Booleanity. Complement and negation appear naturally when the relevant complements remain definable and stable at the lens. But nothing in Definition forces every layer to have those complements available at low cost. For that reason we speak of a logic layer rather than a Boolean layer. The finite laboratories studied in this paper are classical-looking enough to realize NOT, AND, and XOR cleanly, but the framework itself is meant to diagnose which closures a layer actually supports rather than to decree them in advance.

conclusion: Figure is the empirical anchor for the title claim of the paper. The parity-sector laboratory is designed around controlled leakage between the even- and odd-parity sectors of a two-bit system, so the natural candidate coarse variable is the parity bit a b . We compare that lens against two alternatives defined on the same underlying four macrostates: the familiar Boolean predicate a b , and the median of a family of balanced random binary partitions. The comparison is intentionally closure-based rather than purely predictive. The plotted quantity is route mismatch (RM), so smaller values mean that the proposed binary variable is better aligned with the induced coarse dynamics. [t] ∈cludegraphics[width= ] figures/parity_robustness.pdf Route mismatch in the parity-sector laboratory for three candidate binary coarse variables: the parity lens a b , the AND lens a b , and the median balanced random binary partition. Each panel fixes tau and scans leakage p_ leak . Across the full tested grid, the parity lens remains essentially closure-aligned while the AND and median-random alternatives show systematically larger mismatch. The figure is rendered directly from results/final_claims/figure_parity_robustness.csv .

conclusion: Figure shifts the discussion from a single robust coarse variable to full gate families under stress. The point of the figure is not that logic is either present or absent, but that closure occupies regimes. The frozen phase bundle spans a 108 -row grid over gate family, staging barrier, evaluation horizon tau , and output-noise level p_ gate . For each condition it records three diagnostics on the same frozen data asset: truth error relative to the intended one-step gate, conditional entropy H(out ) , and route mismatch on the output-bit lens. Taken together, these panels show that familiar truth tables do not all fail in the same way, and that different diagnostics reveal different modes of nonclosure. We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-01}.
Fix a trajectory $u(t)\in H$ on its lifespan and assume $u_j(0)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ for all depths $j$.
By the system slot HL-SPT-INV (exact feasibility invariance, \eqref{eq:HL-INV}), it follows that
\[
u_j(t)\in \mathcal{F}_j \qquad \text{for all times $t$ in the lifespan and all depths $j$.}
\]
For each fixed $t$ and each depth $j$ with $u_j(t)\neq 0$, we may therefore apply the static feasibility bound (Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-00}) to the feasible vector $v=u_j(t)\in\mathcal{F}_j$ to obtain
\[
\kappa_j(u_j(t)) \;\le\; K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j.
\]
Taking the maximum over depths yields
\[
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}}\kappa_j(u_j(t))
\;\le\;
\max_{0\le j\le J_{\max}} K^{\mathrm{feas}}_j
\;=\;
K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}},
\]
where the last equality is the definition \eqref{eq:Kpred-global}.
This is exactly \eqref{eq:t-spt-01-bound} and implies SPT-legality with threshold $K_\kappa=K^{\mathrm{pred}}_{\mathrm{glob}}$ as stated in \eqref{eq:t-spt-01-K}.

We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-02}.
Fix a time $t$ in the lifespan and a depth $j\le J_{\max}$.
Write $u:=u_j(t)\in H_j$ and decompose it into feasible and off-feasible parts using the packaging projector $E_j$ (Definition~\ref{def:packaging}):
\[
u \;=\; E_j u \;+\; (I-E_j)u \;=:\; v \;+\; w,
\qquad v\in\mathcal{F}_j,\quad w\perp \mathcal{F}_j.
\]

We prove Theorem~\ref{thm:t-spt-02}.
Fix a time $t$ in the lifespan and a depth $j\le J_{\max}$.
Write $u:=u_j(t)\in H_j$ and decompose it into feasible and off-feasible parts using the packaging projector $E_j$ (Definition~\ref{def:packaging}):
\[
u \;=\; E_j u \;+\; (I-E_j)u \;=:\; v \;+\; w,
\qquad v\in\mathcal{F}_j,\quad w\perp \mathcal{F}_j.
\]
If $u=0$ then $\kappa_j(u)=0$ by convention, so assume $u\neq 0$.

\label{prop:fm-mode}
Consider a family of depths with $|\mathcal{C}_j|\to\infty$ (hence $f_j\to 0$).
Suppose there exist depths $j$ for which the feasible set is all of the band, $\mathcal{F}_j=H_j$ (e.g.\ $\Gamma_j$ is surjective, which is possible when $m_j\ge \dim(H_j)$).
Then for each such $j$ there exists a feasible vector $v\in\mathcal{F}_j$ with
\[
\kappa_j(v)=\frac{1}{f_j}.
\]
Consequently, any fixed legality threshold $K_\kappa$ independent of $j$ fails for sufficiently deep $j$.

More generally, even in the best-case artifact regime where $\kappa^{\mathrm{emp}}_0(j)$ and $\mathrm{cond}(\Gamma_j)$ remain bounded, the feasibility envelope in T-SPT-00 scales linearly in $m_j$:
\[
\sup_{v\in\mathcal{F}_j\setminus\{0\}}\kappa_j(v)
\;\lesssim\;
\kappa^{\mathrm{emp}}_0(j)\,\mathrm{cond}(\Gamma_j)\,m_j,
\]
so if $m_j$ grows without bound with depth then the best available legality bound also grows without bound.

\label{prop:ng-ledger}
Fix a depth $j$.
Assume the feasible set $\mathcal{F}_j$ contains two orthonormal vectors $\psi_{\mathrm{uni}},\psi_{\mathrm{loc}}\in \mathcal{F}_j$ such that

\label{prop:ng-dist}
Fix a depth $j$.
For any target leakage ratio $r\in(0,1)$ and any target threshold fraction $\rho\in(0,1)$ (e.g.\ $\rho=0.9$), there exists a multiscale state $u\in H$ and a decomposition
\[
u = v + w,
\]
with the following properties:
\begin{enumerate}
\item (\emph{$v$ is SPT-legal}) for every depth $\ell$, $\kappa_\ell(v_\ell)\le 2$ (in particular $v$ is legal for $K_\kappa=2$).
\item (\emph{$w$ is globally tiny}) $\|w\|/\|v\| \le r$.
\item (\emph{$w$ is deep and localized}) $w_\ell=0$ for $\ell\neq j$, and $w_j$ is supported in a single cell of $\mathcal{C}_j$.
\item (\emph{Deep-band illegality}) the deep component satisfies
\[
\kappa_j(u_j)\ge \rho/f_j.
\]
\end{enumerate}
Thus, even when the global leakage ratio $\|w\|/\|v\|$ is arbitrarily small, the deep-band legality audit can be violated by a factor on the order of $1/f_j$.

conclusion: Many foundational no-go results can be read as constraints on what one is allowed to treat as simultaneously well-defined at a single layer. In the SBT language, the key question becomes: Are we implicitly assuming a single, globally compatible packaging map (or record algebra) that applies to all contexts at once? When that assumption is imported, one is often forced into surplus structure (hidden distinctions or influences) to preserve a unified ontological picture. SBT suggests a different diagnosis: the difficulty lies in insisting on globally compatible packaging, rather than in the causal substrate. Representative pressures include Bell-type constraints, contextuality, and epistemic-state no-go results.

\label{thm:tv-dpi}
Let $Z$ and $X$ be finite sets, let $f:Z\to X$ be a deterministic coarse-graining, and let $\mu,\nu$ be two functions on $Z$ (in particular, distributions on $Z$).
Let $f_\ast\mu$ denote the pushforward onto $X$.
Then total variation distance contracts under pushforward:
\[
\mathrm{TV}(f_\ast\mu, f_\ast\nu)\ \le\ \mathrm{TV}(\mu,\nu).
\]

conclusion: Consider a single nonnegative parameter m 0 (standing in for m_nu ) and suppose two independent packaged constraints yield approximately Gaussian log-likelihood contributions, L_i(m) = - (m-mu_i)^2 2sigma_i^2 + const, i∈\ 1,2\ , with sigma_i>0 . The combined (unconstrained) likelihood is proportional to a Gaussian with mean and variance mu_ = mu_1/sigma_1^2 + mu_2/sigma_2^2 1/sigma_1^2 + 1/sigma_2^2 , sigma_ ^2 = 1 1/sigma_1^2 + 1/sigma_2^2 . If the two packaged constraints are in tension, it is possible for mu_ < 0 even though the physical parameter space is m 0 . Enforcing the gate m 0 corresponds to truncating the Gaussian at 0, producing a (normalized) truncated density on [0,∈fty) . In that case the mode occurs at m_ mode = (0,mu_ ), so whenever the unconstrained optimum lies at mu_ 0 , the constrained mode is exactly at the boundary m=0 . This is the sense in which ``boundary modes'' (sometimes informally described as ``quasi-negative'' behavior) can arise: the negative optimum is not physical, but it is the optimizer's reconciliation point for incompatible packaged constraints, and truncation forces the packaged macro object to pile up at the boundary. Figure illustrates one such case: the unconstrained combined density peaks at a negative mu_ , while the truncated density on m 0 peaks at m=0 .

Toy~2 is a patch-expansion proxy in which each patch follows a local decelerating law, but the domain-average history under the volume-average lens can depart from homogeneous dust closure.
Table~\ref{tab:toy2} reports the diagnostic $Q(t)$ defined in Eq.~\eqref{eq:toy2_Q_def}.
Under homogeneous initial conditions, $Q$ is consistent with numerical zero (maximum absolute value at machine precision), whereas heterogeneous initial conditions yield a strictly positive peak ($Q_{\rm peak}\approx 1.74$) and a late-time regime in which $\ddot{a}_{\mathcal{D}}>0$ for most sampled times (late-time positive fraction $\approx 0.988$; Table~\ref{tab:toy2}).
This illustrates the minimal ``apparent acceleration'' mechanism: heterogeneity plus coarse-grained packaging can produce an effective acceleration proxy even when no fundamental $\Lambda$ is present in the generator.
We emphasize that $Q(t)$ here is a closure diagnostic defined by Eq.~\eqref{eq:toy2_Q_def} for this proxy model; it is not the GR-averaging kinematical backreaction term, and we do not claim Toy~2 constitutes a relativistic backreaction calculation.

conclusion: SBT predicts that closure diagnostics can depend on the staging scale (P4): changing the lens scale or the resolution at which packaging is enforced can change mismatch and the required rewrite. We demonstrate this effect in a toy ``scale sweep'' in which the lens aggregates patches into domains of varying size L before packaging. In the recorded sweep, the late-time mean mismatch varies with L (e.g., RM(L = 1) 0 whereas RM(L_ ) 1.3× 10^ -4 ), and the smallest idempotence defect occurs at a specific staging choice ( L minimizing delta in that sweep). These staging signatures motivate treating scale-cut and smoothing dependence in real analyses as potential closure fingerprints rather than as mere nuisances: if a correction term is packaging-induced, it should exhibit systematic staging dependence beyond what is expected from known measurement systematics.

SBT predicts that closure diagnostics can depend on the staging scale (P4): changing the lens scale or the resolution at which packaging is enforced can change mismatch and the required rewrite.
We demonstrate this effect in a toy ``scale sweep'' in which the lens aggregates patches into domains of varying size $L$ before packaging.
In the recorded sweep, the late-time mean mismatch varies with $L$ (e.g., $\mathrm{RM}(L{=}1)\approx 0$ whereas $\mathrm{RM}(L_{\max})\approx 1.3\times 10^{-4}$), and the smallest idempotence defect occurs at a specific staging choice ($L$ minimizing $\delta$ in that sweep).
These staging signatures motivate treating scale-cut and smoothing dependence in real analyses as potential closure fingerprints rather than as mere nuisances: if a correction term is packaging-induced, it should exhibit systematic staging dependence beyond what is expected from known measurement systematics.

expanded_source_wording_tex:
The DES SN5YR public release provides a Hubble-diagram distance vector and covariance components.
A crucial sanity step is constructing the \emph{total} covariance correctly: the ``STATONLY'' covariance component is zero by design in this release, and statistical uncertainties are provided separately as per-object distance-modulus errors. The total covariance is therefore the sum of the released systematics covariance and the diagonal statistical term.
With this construction, the covariance is symmetric and positive-definite, and SN-only fits yield a reasonable goodness-of-fit (chi-square per datum $\simeq 0.90$ in our baseline configuration).
Because SN distances do not fix $H_0$ without an absolute calibration, we fix $H_0$ in the distance calculation and absorb the normalization into the profiled intercept $\mathcal{M}$, so SN constrains shape parameters rather than absolute scale.

Fitting a flat $\Lambda$CDM background to SN-only yields a best-fit matter density $\Omega_m\simeq 0.35$.
Allowing a constant equation-of-state parameter (flat $w$CDM) yields a best-fit $w\simeq -0.82$ with a small improvement in chi-square, consistent with the well-known SN-only degeneracy between $\Omega_m$ and $w$ in the absence of external anchors.

conclusion: In our implementation, we fit a homogeneous background by mapping (H_0,Omega_m) to a predicted alpha at the effective redshift and evaluating Delta ^2 by interpolation. The combined curve peaks at alpha_ hat 0.9568 with an approximate width sigma_alpha 0.0126 in our Gaussian approximation to the local curvature at the peak. In our BAO-only fit, the Delta AIC between flat Lambda CDM and an Omega_Lambda = 0 homogeneous fit is 5.0× 10^ -2 (negligible). conclusion: We finally test a staged, phenomenological rewrite family directly on public background probes, without committing to a detailed inhomogeneous micro-model. Specifically, we fit a background rewrite model of the form H^2(z)=H_ m ^2(z)+A g(z) with g(z)=(1+z)^ -m (Section ). Table summarizes fits for SN-only, BAO-only, and the combined SN+BAO objective. For combined fits we use ^2_ tot ( ) = ^2_ SN ( ,M( )) + ^2_ BAO ( ). In both SN-only and SN+BAO fits, the rewrite model matches the best-fit chi-square of Lambda CDM but pays the expected information-criterion penalty for the extra parameter (typically DeltaAIC 2 ). Moreover, the best-fit shape parameter saturates at m 0 in these background-only fits, so the rewrite term collapses to a constant contribution over the probed redshift range. This outcome is notable: with current background probes alone, the data prefer a nearly constant closure correction, consistent with why Lambda CDM is phenomenologically successful for geometry. In the closure-first view, time variation (or additional state variables) would be demanded only if audits across multiple probes and staging choices were to require it.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
We finally test a staged, phenomenological rewrite family directly on public background probes, without committing to a detailed inhomogeneous micro-model.
Specifically, we fit a background rewrite model of the form $H^2(z)=H_{\mathrm{m}}^2(z)+A\,g(z)$ with $g(z)=(1+z)^{-m}$ (Section~\ref{sec:methods:rewrite}).
Table~\ref{tab:background_fits} summarizes fits for SN-only, BAO-only, and the combined SN+BAO objective.
For combined fits we use
\begin{equation}
\chi^2_{\rm tot}(\theta) \;=\; \chi^2_{\rm SN}(\theta,\widehat{\mathcal{M}}(\theta)) \;+\; \chi^2_{\rm BAO}(\theta).
\label{eq:chi2_tot_background}
\end{equation}

In both SN-only and SN+BAO fits, the rewrite model matches the best-fit chi-square of $\Lambda$CDM but pays the expected information-criterion penalty for the extra parameter (typically $\Delta\mathrm{AIC}\approx 2$).
Moreover, the best-fit shape parameter saturates at $m\simeq 0$ in these background-only fits, so the rewrite term collapses to a constant contribution over the probed redshift range.
This outcome is notable: with current background probes alone, the data prefer a nearly constant closure correction, consistent with why $\Lambda$CDM is phenomenologically successful for geometry.
In the closure-first view, time variation (or additional state variables) would be demanded only if audits across multiple probes and staging choices were to require it.

We next demonstrate the Six Birds audit protocol (P6) and data-layer staging machinery on public large-scale-structure (LSS) two-point vectors.
This section is intentionally framed as an \emph{audit protocol demonstration}: we ingest public data vectors, construct a block map for probe splitting, and run cross-probe predictivity checks.
A full physical 3$\times$2pt theory backend (e.g., CCL/Firecrown/pyccl) is not required to demonstrate the audit mechanics, but it \emph{is} required to interpret these LSS results as cosmological parameter constraints.
We therefore separate the protocol and I/O layer (which is definitive here) from the physics backend (explicitly limited here).

\begin{limitationbox}{Surrogate LSS backend}\label{box:surrogate_lss}
The DES Y3 and KiDS-450 LSS results in this manuscript use a \emph{surrogate} theory backend rather than a physical 3$\times$2pt forward model.
Concretely, we define deterministic probe-dependent ``template residuals,'' fit low-dimensional correction coefficients, and then evaluate held-out discrepancies (chi-square/RMSE) under the public covariance.
This approach establishes the audit protocol, probe splitting, masking, and reproducible bookkeeping under realistic vector/covariance dimensions, but it does \emph{not} constitute a physical reproduction of the DES Y3 3$\times$2pt likelihood \cite{DES2022Y3_3x2pt}.
The repository includes a plug-in backend interface and an environment probe; in the baseline environment, the physical backend import fails (e.g., \texttt{pyccl} unavailable), motivating this staged presentation.
\end{limitationbox}

conclusion: We ingest the public DES Y3 2pt (maglim) data vector and covariance and construct a per-point block index assigning each element to a probe/statistic/bin combination. For the maglim vector used here ( n=1000 ), the resulting decomposition contains n_ shear =400 cosmic-shear points, n_ clust =120 galaxy-clustering points, and n_ ggl =480 galaxy–galaxy-lensing points (with no unclassified remainder). This block map is the prerequisite for meaningful probe splits and for staging operations such as scale cuts and block bootstraps. Numerically, we apply probe masks by selecting sub-vectors and sub-covariances and compute ^2 via Cholesky-based linear solves (without explicit matrix inversion). In the baseline Y3 maglim run, the covariance is symmetric positive-definite with chol_success=true and chol_jitter_used=0.0 , while the estimated minimum eigenvalue and condition number are lambda_ 4.5× 10^ -15 and 8.7× 10^ 9 , indicating ill-conditioning but stable solves under masked Cholesky.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
We ingest the public DES Y3 2pt (maglim) data vector and covariance and construct a per-point block index assigning each element to a probe/statistic/bin combination.
For the maglim vector used here ($n=1000$), the resulting decomposition contains $n_{\rm shear}=400$ cosmic-shear points, $n_{\rm clust}=120$ galaxy-clustering points, and $n_{\rm ggl}=480$ galaxy--galaxy-lensing points (with no unclassified remainder).
This block map is the prerequisite for meaningful probe splits and for staging operations such as scale cuts and block bootstraps.
Numerically, we apply probe masks by selecting sub-vectors and sub-covariances and compute $\chi^2$ via Cholesky-based linear solves (without explicit matrix inversion). In the baseline Y3 maglim run, the covariance is symmetric positive-definite with $\texttt{chol\_success}=\texttt{true}$ and $\texttt{chol\_jitter\_used}=0.0$, while the estimated minimum eigenvalue and condition number are $\lambda_{\min}\approx 4.5\times 10^{-15}$ and $\kappa\approx 8.7\times 10^{9}$, indicating ill-conditioning but stable solves under masked Cholesky.

Using the block map, we define Probe~A as cosmic shear and Probe~B as clustering+galaxy--galaxy lensing.
We then run the PPD-style audit (Section~\ref{sec:methods:ppd}): fit a low-dimensional macro correction on one probe block and evaluate predictive discrepancy on the held-out block.
Table~\ref{tab:lss_ppd_y3} reports held-out chi-square values for two macro families in the surrogate setting: a baseline ``$\Lambda$CDM-like'' one-parameter correction and a ``rewrite-like'' two-parameter correction.
Because the backend is surrogate (Limitation~\ref{box:surrogate_lss}), the absolute scale of chi-square is not interpreted as a cosmological goodness-of-fit; instead we treat held-out discrepancy as an audit diagnostic that can be transported unchanged to a physical backend when available.
The absolute $\chi^2$ values are small because the surrogate template normalization is arbitrary; we therefore interpret only relative held-out comparisons and the reproducible train$\to$test protocol artifact.

source_wording_tex:
To test sensitivity to external geometry information, we repeat the DES Y3 probe-split audit while adding public background-probe anchors (DES SN5YR distances and DES Y6 BAO $\alpha$-likelihood) to the training objective.
Table~\ref{tab:lss_ppd_y3_anchors} compares held-out chi-square values with and without these anchors.
In this staged setting, the anchors increase the held-out chi-square for both macro families and reduce the directional differences.
This behavior is expected: adding shared geometry constraints partially fixes the degrees of freedom that the surrogate correction would otherwise have used to absorb cross-probe discrepancies.
In these anchored runs we use
\[
\chi^2_{\rm train} \;=\; \chi^2_{\rm LSS,train} \;+\; \chi^2_{\rm SN} \;+\; \chi^2_{\rm BAO},
\]
and assume independence (no modeled cross-covariances) between the LSS and background-probe likelihoods.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering
\caption{DES Y3 probe-split PPD audit under surrogate LSS backend, comparing held-out chi-square without geometry anchors vs.\ with SN+BAO anchors added to the training objective.}
\label{tab:lss_ppd_y3_anchors}
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
Direction & Model & $\chi^2_{\rm test}$ (no anchors) & $\chi^2_{\rm test}$ (SN+BAO anchors) \\
\midrule
A$\to$B & $\Lambda$CDM-like & 0.6750 & 1.0798 \\
A$\to$B & rewrite-like & 0.9967 & 1.0820 \\
B$\to$A & $\Lambda$CDM-like & 0.7186 & 1.2329 \\
B$\to$A & rewrite-like & 0.4985 & 1.2458 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

To demonstrate portability beyond DES, we replicate the same probe-split audit protocol on a public KiDS-450 3$\times$2pt bandpower data product (cosmic shear bandpowers, galaxy--galaxy lensing bandpowers, and clustering bandpowers) \cite{vanUitert2018KiDSGAMA,KiDSDataProducts}.
The ingested vector has $n=100$ with an even split between shear (Probe~A; $n_A=50$) and ggl+clustering (Probe~B; $n_B=50$).
Table~\ref{tab:lss_ppd_kids} reports held-out chi-square values under the same surrogate-backend macro families.
Although the absolute values remain backend-dependent, the protocol yields a consistent summary artifact (train--test directions, held-out discrepancy, and reproducible provenance) that can be compared across surveys.

\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{table}

conclusion: Finally, we stress-test the audit protocol on DES Y3 by varying the split definition (shear versus rest, even/odd tomographic-bin proxy, low/high tomographic-bin proxy), subsampling probe-block keys (bootstrap-like block subsampling without replacement), and perturbing the covariance with small diagonal jitter. Across 30 requested scenarios, 26 completed successfully with 4 skipped due to insufficient points after subsampling (0 failed). For the canonical shear → (clust+ggl) direction, the distribution of held-out improvement Delta ^2= ^2_ Lambda CDM-like - ^2_ rewrite-like has median 5.7× 10^ -3 and interquartile range 1.94× 10^ -2 in this surrogate setting. The small magnitude reflects the surrogate scale of residuals; the stability of the sign and distribution across splits and jitter levels demonstrates that the evidence artifacts (tables, CSVs, provenance bundles) are robust to modest protocol perturbations, as required for P6-style accounting.
expanded_source_wording_tex:
Finally, we stress-test the audit protocol on DES Y3 by varying the split definition (shear versus rest, even/odd tomographic-bin proxy, low/high tomographic-bin proxy), subsampling probe-block keys (bootstrap-like block subsampling without replacement), and perturbing the covariance with small diagonal jitter.
Across 30 requested scenarios, 26 completed successfully with 4 skipped due to insufficient points after subsampling (0 failed).
For the canonical shear$\to$(clust+ggl) direction, the distribution of held-out improvement $\Delta\chi^2=\chi^2_{\Lambda{\rm CDM\text{-}like}}-\chi^2_{\rm rewrite\text{-}like}$ has median $\simeq 5.7\times 10^{-3}$ and interquartile range $\simeq 1.94\times 10^{-2}$ in this surrogate setting.
The small magnitude reflects the surrogate scale of residuals; the stability of the sign and distribution across splits and jitter levels demonstrates that the evidence artifacts (tables, CSVs, provenance bundles) are robust to modest protocol perturbations, as required for P6-style accounting.

conclusion: We now report the core empirical claim of this paper: when packaging and staging yield a coherent closure, the induced cost structure supports a stable notion of ``near'' and ``far'' that behaves like geometry. We present four exhibits—plane-like (grid), sphere-like (curved regime), Sierpi\'nski (fractal regime), and anisotropic deformation under constraints—and interpret them through the diagnostics introduced in Section . (Curvature as holonomy is deferred to Section .) Throughout, the figures and quoted summary numbers refer to committed run packs (Section ), so the narrative is anchored to auditable artifacts rather than ad hoc screenshots. The overlay figures in this section provide a ``regime map'' across substrates: idempotence defect (closure stability), inter-scale distortion (refinement coherence), and the mean induced distance scale.

conclusion: The contested program. A prominent line in quantum gravity (``it-from-qubit'', ER=EPR, entanglement-builds-geometry) holds that bulk spacetime is fully determined by boundary entanglement: given the complete entanglement data of the boundary state, the bulk geometry is reconstructible. The fork of §5.2 forces the opposite: the gravitational readout d_3 is a sibling of the entanglement modes, not a function of them, so some geometric data must be invisible to all entanglement measures.

conclusion: The contested program. The most anticipated near-term probe of quantum gravity is the BMV proposal (Bose et al.; Marletto–Vedral) : place two masses in spatial superpositions, let only gravity couple them, and test whether they become entangled. The widely-stated inference is that gravitationally-induced entanglement would witness a quantum (coherent) gravitational mediator — a graviton-like degree of freedom. The fork of §5.2 forces the opposite: the gravitational arm is a sibling readout that does not have access to the quantum phase mode and cannot carry it coherently between parties.
